stages.name: Ossa (v1)
stages.summary: A minimum viable product for the project.

decisions.title: Native auth now, SSO seam only
decisions.statement: `AuthBackend` (`backend/app/auth_backends/base.py`) is a small protocol with one implementation, `NativeAuthBackend` (email + bcrypt password).
decisions.rationale: C-U-06/C-U-07 ask for pluggable backends and optional OAuth/SSO; actually wiring Keycloak/Authentica is Pelion-adjacent (E-U-01) and wasn't built, but the seam exists so adding a second backend doesn't require touching the rest of the app.
decisions.section: Authentication and identity

decisions.title: Login IP logging without geolocation (C-A-07)
decisions.statement: Every login attempt writes a `login_events` row with the raw IP.
decisions.rationale: Resolving IP → location was deliberately left as a nullable `location` column rather than calling an external geo-IP service at login time, to avoid a runtime network dependency and an API-key requirement in a self-hostable product. Follow-up: wire an offline MaxMind-style database when this becomes a priority.
decisions.section: Authentication and identity

decisions.title: Authentication and identity: Server admin bootstrap (I-M-05/06/08)
decisions.statement: `backend/app/services/bootstrap.py` runs on every app startup (idempotent): creates the configured server-admin user if absent, and — if `SERVER_ADMIN_CREATE_ORG` is enabled — a default organisation with that user as org admin, matching the "on first install" wording without needing a separate CLI step.
decisions.section: Authentication and identity

decisions.title: Project manager implies administrator + stakeholder
decisions.statement: Per the C-U-03 clarification, `get_effective_project_roles` (`backend/app/services/rbac.py`) folds `PROJECT_MANAGER` into also granting `PROJECT_ADMINISTRATOR` and `STAKEHOLDER` capabilities, and any assigned role implies baseline `MEMBER` (view) access.
decisions.section: Roles and permissions

decisions.title: Org admin ≠ automatic project content access
decisions.statement: The C-U-01 clarification ("no project access is guaranteed... apart from org admin being able to manage project settings") is implemented as two separate dependencies: `require_project_manage` (org admins pass) for settings/stage/component/group endpoints, and `require_project_view` (org admins do **not** automatically pass) for requirement/change-request content.
decisions.rationale: An org admin who also wants to read requirements needs an explicit project role, same as anyone else.
decisions.section: Roles and permissions

decisions.title: Org-group nesting resolves one level deep
decisions.statement: A `ProjectGroupMember` row may point at a user or an org group (C-U-12); permission resolution flattens org-group membership into the containing project group's role.
decisions.rationale: Cycle prevention is limited to not letting a group contain itself — deeper nested-group graphs aren't a requirement here and would add complexity with no described use case.
decisions.section: Roles and permissions

decisions.title: C-U-08/C-U-09 (must always have a manager)
decisions.statement: Enforced two ways: `revoke_project_role` blocks removing the last direct project-manager assignment, and `deactivate_org_user` (in `backend/app/routers/orgs.py`) checks every project in the org after deactivating a user — if that removal leaves a project with zero managers, the *acting admin* is assigned as manager, matching the requirement's specific wording.
decisions.section: Roles and permissions

decisions.title: Identity vs. version split, not valid_from/valid_to on one row
decisions.statement: `solution-architecture.md` suggests temporal columns directly on core entities; in practice, `Requirement` holds only stable identity (project/component/category, generated code, creator, archival state) while `RequirementVersion` holds every mutable field plus `valid_from`/`valid_to`/`version_number`.
decisions.rationale: The "current" version is the row with `valid_to IS NULL`. This gives the same point-in-time query capability with a simpler mental model: identity never changes, content always changes through a new version row. Change requests mirror the same pattern (`ChangeRequestVersion`).
decisions.section: Requirement lifecycle and change management

decisions.title: Locking is per-requirement, not per-project-stage
decisions.statement: C-G-12 says changes are change-request-only "once a requirement is approved for a project stage." This is implemented as `is_locked` = the requirement's current version status is `approved` or `completed` — checked directly rather than by asking whether the project's current stage is approved.
decisions.rationale: Approving a stage (`backend/app/services/baseline.py`) bulk-transitions every non-archived requirement still in `draft`/`reviewed` to `approved` and snapshots a `Baseline`/`BaselineItem` row per requirement (C-G-10) in the same transaction, so in practice stage approval and the lock happen together — but the lock itself is a property of the requirement, which is what C-G-12 actually says.
decisions.section: Requirement lifecycle and change management

decisions.title: Requirement lifecycle and change management: Unique requirement IDs (C-G-06/C-G-07)
decisions.statement: `{component.prefix}-{category.prefix}-{project.next_requirement_seq:03d}`, e.g.
decisions.rationale: `SW-PERF-014`. The sequence is a per-project counter that only increments, so archived requirements' numbers are never reused, satisfying the C-G-06 clarification.
decisions.section: Requirement lifecycle and change management

decisions.title: Ordering is move-up/move-down, not drag-and-drop (C-E-01/02/03)
decisions.statement: Each orderable entity (`ProjectComponent`, `ProjectCategory`, and a requirement's `sort_order` within its component/category) has a persisted integer position and a `/move` endpoint that swaps it with its neighbour.
decisions.rationale: This satisfies the requirement without a drag-and-drop dependency in the frontend; requirement reordering is additionally blocked outside the scoping stage, per the C-E-03 clarification.
decisions.section: Requirement lifecycle and change management

decisions.title: Discussion threads are not the change log (C-A-09 clarification)
decisions.statement: `ReviewComment` (discussion, C-R-01) and `RequirementVersion`/`ChangeRequestVersion` (change log) are separate tables from the start, so the UI's change-log view never needs to filter comments out after the fact.
decisions.section: Requirement lifecycle and change management

decisions.title: ReportLab over WeasyPrint for PDF (R-F-01)
decisions.statement: ReportLab is pure-Python with no system-level dependencies (WeasyPrint needs Cairo/Pango), which keeps the backend Docker image simple.
decisions.rationale: Markdown pre/post sections (R-G-01/R-G-02) are parsed with `markdown-it-py` and walked token-by-token into ReportLab flowables (headings, paragraphs, bullet lists) — enough fidelity for introduction/appendix-style content without a full HTML rendering stack.
decisions.section: Reporting

decisions.title: WebSocket pub/sub is in-process (I-A-04)
decisions.statement: `backend/app/services/pubsub.py` is a single-process broadcaster; the endpoint is explicitly optional per the requirement text ("may expose"), and a single-backend-instance deployment is exactly what Ossa (v1)'s deployment model is.
decisions.rationale: Scaling to multiple backend replicas would need a shared broker (Redis pub/sub or similar) — a natural extension point, not a v1 requirement.
decisions.section: Realtime

decisions.title: Enum columns use sqlalchemy.Enum(..., native_enum=False), not plain String
decisions.statement: An early version used `Mapped[SomeEnum] = mapped_column(String(N))`, which stores correctly but returns a plain `str` (not the enum) on read — anything calling `.value` on a freshly-loaded attribute would crash.
decisions.rationale: `models/base.py::str_enum()` fixes this while keeping the column a plain VARCHAR (no Postgres `CREATE TYPE`/migration friction when adding a new enum member).
decisions.section: Infrastructure

decisions.title: Infrastructure: One hand-written initial migration
decisions.statement: `alembic/versions/0001_initial.py` creates the schema via `Base.metadata.create_all()` rather than 22 transcribed `op.create_table()` calls, keeping the migration in lockstep with the models (the single source of truth).
decisions.rationale: Future schema changes should be added as normal incremental Alembic migrations generated with `--autogenerate`.
decisions.section: Infrastructure

decisions.title: Observability: metrics/health always on, Loki/Tempo/Grafana/Alloy opt-in
decisions.statement: The Ossa-tagged requirements (I-M health checks, Prometheus `/metrics`) are wired into the default `docker compose up`.
decisions.rationale: The broader Loki/Tempo/Grafana/Alloy stack described in `solution-architecture.md` is architecture-level, not individually Ossa-tagged, so it's an opt-in Compose profile (`docker compose --profile observability up`) — the default stack stays fast to start. The backend does not yet emit OpenTelemetry traces; the Alloy config's OTLP receiver is ready to forward them to Tempo the moment that instrumentation is added.
decisions.section: Infrastructure

decisions.title: I18n (U-U-02): a single string table, not a full i18n library
decisions.statement: `frontend/src/i18n/strings.ts` centralises every UI string behind a `t()` lookup.
decisions.rationale: No second language ships in v1, but no component hardcodes text inline, so adding a translated locale is additive rather than a rewrite.
decisions.section: Infrastructure

decisions.title: Backend tests run against real PostgreSQL, not SQLite
decisions.statement: The schema uses Postgres-specific types (`UUID`, `JSONB`), so `backend/tests/conftest.py` creates a dedicated `reqtrack_test` database on the same Postgres server used by docker-compose, with tables truncated between tests rather than mocking the database.
decisions.section: Testing

decisions.title: A Playwright E2E suite (tests/playwright/) runs against the actual docker-compose stack
decisions.statement: (not a dev server), exercising the full golden path in a real browser: login → create project → components/categories → requirement → stage approval (lock) → change request → PDF report → theme toggle.
decisions.rationale: This is the only reliable way to confirm the shipped Docker images actually work together, not just that each service passes its own tests in isolation.
decisions.section: Testing

decisions.title: Squashed into the same 0001_initial.py baseline, not a second migration
decisions.statement: Every Pelion v2 model change (new columns on `User`/`Organization`/`Project`/`RequirementVersion`/`ChangeRequestVersion`, and new tables for files/notifications/custom fields/favourites) was added directly to the existing models and folded into `alembic/versions/0001_initial.py`'s `Base.metadata.create_all()`, rather than written as an incremental `op.add_column`/`op.create_table` migration.
decisions.rationale: This only works because `create_all()` reflects the *current* model state at the time it runs — attempting to layer a second migration on top produced "column already exists" errors, since 0001 would create the new columns too. This is a deliberate pre-release-only shortcut: there is no real production deployment yet to preserve data for, so squashing is safe. **The moment this system has a real deployed database that must be upgraded in place, all future schema changes must go back to normal incremental Alembic migrations** (`alembic revision --autogenerate`) rather than editing 0001 again — the docstring at the top of that file repeats this warning.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Pluggable storage backend, exercised for real via MinIO, not just implemented in the abstract
decisions.statement: `backend/app/storage_backends/{base,local,s3}.py` defines a `FileStorageBackend` protocol with `LocalFileStorageBackend` (filesystem) and `S3CompatibleFileStorageBackend` (boto3; works against MinIO or real S3), selected via `STORAGE_BACKEND=local|s3`.
decisions.rationale: MinIO is added to the default `docker-compose.yml` stack and is the default backend, so I-M-10 ("must support different storage backends") is verified against an actual running S3-compatible service during manual and automated verification, not only against local disk.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: A single file_assets table backs every upload use case
decisions.statement: (requirement attachments, org shared resources, avatars, org logos) rather than one table per use case, since they all need the same metadata (storage backend, key, filename, content type, size, uploader).
decisions.rationale: Requirement attachments additionally go through a `requirement_files` link table (many-to-many, so the same shared org resource can be linked to multiple requirements per C-M-04 without duplicating the file).
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Local backend path-traversal defense in depth
decisions.statement: Storage keys are always generated by `app/services/files.py` (UUID-based), never taken from user input directly, so path traversal via a key isn't attacker-reachable in practice — but `LocalFileStorageBackend._path_for()` still resolves the path and checks `is_relative_to()` the base directory before any read/write, as defense in depth rather than relying solely on that invariant holding forever.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Disk-usage monitor (I-M-11) is a single testable function plus a thin timer loop
decisions.statement: `check_disk_usage_once()` in `backend/app/services/disk_monitor.py` contains all the actual threshold/dedup logic and takes the storage backend and prior warned-state as plain arguments; `run_disk_monitor_loop()` is just a 15-minute `asyncio.sleep` wrapper around it.
decisions.rationale: This split exists specifically so the branching logic (warn once, don't repeat while still over threshold, re-warn after recovery) can be unit-tested (`backend/tests/test_disk_monitor.py`) without waiting on the real timer or touching a real filesystem's `shutil.disk_usage`.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: In-process asyncio background tasks, not a separate worker service
decisions.statement: Both the instant-notification email path and the daily-digest batch job run as `asyncio` tasks started from the FastAPI lifespan handler, consistent with the existing single-instance WebSocket pub/sub pattern (`services/pubsub.py`).
decisions.rationale: A dedicated worker service is a real future step (already called out in `solution-architecture.md`'s "Production deployment path") once a single backend replica stops being sufficient — not required for this deployment model.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: MailHog as the default SMTP endpoint
decisions.statement: Rather than requiring a real mail provider to exercise C-N-01–05, the default Compose stack runs MailHog and points `SMTP_HOST`/`SMTP_PORT` at it, so sent notification emails are genuinely inspectable (http://localhost:8025) during development, testing, and manual verification — not just logged or mocked.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Notification triggers were added at existing call sites
decisions.statement: Notification triggers were added at existing call sites.
decisions.rationale: not as a generic event-bus: project-group join, stage transitions, change-request submit/decide, password change, and org-role permission grant. Permission *revocation* does not currently fire a notification — only grant does; this is a narrower interpretation of C-N-04 than might be expected and is a candidate follow-up if revocation notifications turn out to matter in practice.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Custom field values reuse the existing version-history mechanism instead of a second
decisions.statement: `CustomFieldDefinition` (project-scoped, `entity_kind` requirement|change_request) defines the schema; the actual *values* live in a plain `custom_fields JSONB` column added directly to `RequirementVersion`/`ChangeRequestVersion`.
decisions.rationale: Every requirement/CR edit already creates a new version row (C-A-02/C-A-09), so custom field values automatically get the same point-in-time history for free.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: A change request's custom_fields payload is validated against CustomFieldEntityKind.REQUIREMENT definitions, not CHANGE_REQUEST definitions
decisions.statement: These values represent proposed attribute values for the requirement being created/modified (mirroring `proposed_name`/`proposed_reasoning`) and are copied onto the requirement's version on approval — so they must be validated against the schema that governs requirements, not change requests.
decisions.rationale: A separate `CustomFieldEntityKind.CHANGE_REQUEST` kind still exists in the data model for attributes describing the change request itself (e.g. an "urgency" field), but no workflow currently collects or consumes those values; this is a deliberate, documented scope gap rather than an oversight.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Clone_project() deep-copies configuration and requirements, resetting workflow state
decisions.statement: Cloning a template project (C-E-05) copies components, categories, custom field definitions, groups and group memberships, and requirements (reset to `draft` status, with any project-specific custom field ids remapped to the new project's definitions) — but never copies change requests, comments, or audit history, since those describe the *history* of the template project, not a starting…
decisions.rationale: configuration for a new one.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: PM auto-assignment has an explicit fallback when cloning
decisions.statement: C-U-10 says the creator is normally added to the Project Managers group automatically; C-E-05 says this doesn't apply when creating from a template (groups/members are copied from the template instead).
decisions.rationale: If that copy leaves the new project with zero managers (e.g. the template's manager group had no members), the creator is still added as a fallback so C-U-08 ("every project must have a manager") can never be violated by a template that happens to be manager-less.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Creator reassignment (C-A-11/C-A-12) is restricted to project managers
decisions.statement: `POST .../requirements` and `POST .../change-requests` accept an optional `creator_id`; if present, the caller must hold the `project_manager` role (or be a server admin) or the request is rejected with 403 — anyone who can create a requirement/CR at all can still create one attributed to themselves, but only a manager can attribute it to someone else.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: The project changes-over-time view (C-A-10) excludes discussion comments by default
decisions.statement: `get_project_changes()` merges audit events, requirement version history, and change-request version history into one timeline; `ReviewComment` rows are only included when the caller explicitly passes `include_comments=true`, consistent with the Ossa v1 decision that discussion threads are not the change log.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Favourite projects sort ahead of everything else, then alphabetically
decisions.statement: `GET /api/v1/projects` computes the caller's favourited project ids and sorts the response with `(not is_favorite, name.lower())` as the key, so favourites always appear as a contiguous block at the top regardless of the `role`/`stage_status`/`search` filters also applied.
decisions.rationale: Favouriting is a simple per-user join table (`FavoriteProject`) with `PUT`/`DELETE .../favorite` endpoints, not a field on `Project` itself, since it's user-specific rather than project-wide state.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Structural fix: tests run against their own isolated stack
decisions.statement: The root `docker-compose.yml` is now the production-oriented stack (no test database anywhere near it); `tests/container/docker-compose.yml` is a separate, fully isolated stack whose `backend` service's `DATABASE_URL` already points at `reqtrack_test` — so `docker compose exec backend pytest` there just works, with the safety guard confirming it rather than needing to catch a mistake.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Storybook (frontend/.storybook/) plus @storybook/addon-vitest for automated story tests
decisions.statement: Storybook (frontend/.storybook/) plus @storybook/addon-vitest for automated story tests.
decisions.rationale: not just a manual component browser. `npm run storybook` gives a visual explorer; `npm run test-storybook` runs every story as a real headless-Chromium test via Vitest's Playwright browser provider, so a story that fails to render or fails an assertion in its `play` function fails CI the same as any other test — a component explorer nobody automates checking against tends to silently rot.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: The preview's withTheme decorator applies the exact same mechanism the real app uses
decisions.statement: (a `data-theme` attribute on `<html>`, read by `src/styles/theme.css`'s CSS variables) rather than a Storybook-specific theming shim, so stories render with the actual product palette.
decisions.rationale: A toolbar toggle switches themes while browsing; `LightTheme`/`DarkTheme` story exports pin `globals: { theme: ... }` explicitly so both are exercised by `test-storybook` on every run regardless of whatever theme was last selected in the UI (U-U-01: light and dark are both first-class, not just supported).
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Pytest-cov added, and used to find real gaps rather than pad numbers
decisions.statement: `pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing` (from `backend/`, or `docker compose exec backend pytest --cov=app --cov-report=term-missing` in `tests/container/`) reports per-file coverage.
decisions.rationale: It went from 90% to 92% during this pass; every added test corresponds to a specific, real gap the report identified — a fully untested `GET /projects/{id}/metrics` dashboard endpoint, `LocalFileStorageBackend` (never exercised since the dev/test stack defaults to the `s3` backend), requirement reordering, traceability links, an organisation-level role grant, and the C-U-09 manager-fallback-on-deactivation safeguard — rather than writing tests to move the percentage without a specific defect or behavior in mind.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Pelion (v2): API resource lifecycle tests
decisions.statement: "Remove" means different things by design (see the requirement-lifecycle and security-hardening sections above): most domain entities soft-delete/archive rather than hard-delete, to preserve audit history; a few resources (organisations, project components/categories/groups) have no removal endpoint at all, which each test notes explicitly.
decisions.rationale: Writing this file surfaced one real bug: `list_org_users` never filtered out archived users, contradicting C-U-05's explicit requirement that an archived user "no longer show[s] as users" — fixed by adding the missing filter.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: A systematic permission-level test matrix
decisions.statement: A systematic permission-level test matrix.
decisions.rationale: that a role below the required level is rejected (403) *and* that the role that should be allowed actually succeeds — rather than only ever testing the rejection side, which is what most of the pre-existing RBAC tests did.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: The Docker Compose backend and frontend services do not bind-mount source
decisions.statement: The Docker Compose backend and frontend services do not bind-mount source.
decisions.rationale: they `COPY` the source at build time. Editing backend or frontend code and then testing against the *already-running* containers (`docker compose exec backend pytest`, or exercising the UI at localhost:3000) silently tests stale code until `docker compose build <service> && docker compose up -d <service>` is run. This tripped up Pelion v2 verification more than once (a backend test file and a frontend UI change were both validated against stale containers before the rebuild step was remembered) — worth calling out explicitly since the mistake produces no error, just misleading "it works" or "it's broken" signals from the wrong code.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: Password-changing Playwright steps must revert via a direct API call in a finally block
decisions.statement: The new Pelion v2 E2E spec (`tests/playwright/tests/pelion-v2.spec.ts`) changes the shared bootstrap admin's password to exercise the password-changed notification, then must restore it, since `golden-path.spec.ts` and every future run depend on the fixed bootstrap password staying valid.
decisions.rationale: Reverting through a second UI form submission proved flaky (a `page.reload()` issued immediately after clicking "Change password" can abort the still in-flight request before the browser sends it); reverting via `page.request.post(...)` with the token read out of `localStorage` is synchronous from the test's perspective and doesn't depend on any UI timing. The forward change also now explicitly awaits the `change-password` network response (`page.waitForResponse`) before doing anything else, for the same reason.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: New backend models are additive, not repurposed existing tables
decisions.statement: `CommentReaction` and `Subscription` (`backend/app/models/engagement.py`) are new join tables rather than columns bolted onto `ReviewComment`/`Requirement`/`ChangeRequest`, since reactions and subscriptions are per-user state on entities that already have their own versioned lifecycle — mixing user-specific toggle state into a versioned row would be a design smell.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: SMTP/SSO organisation settings are a storage-only seam
decisions.statement: `Organization.smtp_host/port/username/password/use_tls` and `sso_group_mappings` (JSONB) are stored and round-tripped via `GET/PUT /orgs/{id}/advanced-settings` (org_admin only, password write-only and never echoed back), but nothing in `services/email.py` or the auth backends actually reads them yet.
decisions.rationale: This mirrors the same "build the seam, wire it up later" decision already made for pluggable auth backends — inventing a second SMTP-sending code path or a working SSO group-sync flow was out of scope for a UI-alignment pass and would need its own design work. **Update, see "Organisation rename and per-org/deployment-wide test-email actions" below**: the SMTP half of this seam is now partially wired — `POST /orgs/{id}/test-email` reads `Organization.smtp_*` to send a one-off test message — but ordinary notification email still always goes through the deployment-wide `Settings.smtp_*`; the seam remains otherwise unwired.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: The dark left-navigation rail is intentionally not theme-dependent
decisions.statement: New `--color-nav-*` CSS variables in `theme.css` are defined once under `:root` (not duplicated per `data-theme="light"`/`"dark"`), because the mockup's dark sidebar-on-light-canvas pattern (the same convention as GitHub, Notion, etc.) is a fixed piece of chrome, not part of the app's light/dark theme toggle — U-U-01's "light and dark are both first-class" requirement is about the *content* area…
decisions.rationale: not this rail.

decisions.title: C-A-07 IP geolocation is implemented as a background task, not an inline call
decisions.statement: C-A-07 IP geolocation is implemented as a background task, not an inline call.
decisions.rationale: so it can never add latency to or block the login response. `services/geoip.py` resolves an IP's approximate location via a free, keyless third-party API (`ip-api.com`) only when `GEOIP_LOOKUP_ENABLED=true` (default `false`, since this is a real external dependency and privacy trade-off the user must opt into) and only for addresses outside `GEOIP_LOOKUP_EXCLUDE_CIDRS` (defaults to the standard private/loopback ranges). `routers/auth.py`'s `login` schedules `resolve_and_store_login_location` via FastAPI `BackgroundTasks` *after* the response is built, updating the `LoginEvent` row in a fresh DB session. Every failure mode (disabled, excluded address, network error, timeout) resolves to doing nothing — never an exception that could affect login.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: U-P-06 pagination is opt-in, not a forced page size
decisions.statement: U-P-06 pagination is opt-in, not a forced page size.
decisions.rationale: preserving C-G-05 ("no artificial limit"): the requirements/projects/change-requests list endpoints accept optional `limit`/`offset` and report the pre-slice total via an `X-Total-Count` response header (added to `CORSMiddleware`'s `expose_headers`, since custom response headers aren't visible to browser JS otherwise); omitting both still returns every match, unchanged from before. The frontend's three list pages use a new `api.getPage()` client method and a shared `<LoadMoreButton>` component for simple incremental "load more" pagination at 30 items/page.
decisions.section: Pelion (v2)

decisions.title: U-P-05's file count is scoped to requirement attachments within the project

decisions.title: C-C-03 terminology overrides are applied through a new TerminologyProvider React context

decisions.rationale: Applied to the nav labels and the Requirements/Change-Requests page titles and "New X" buttons — deliberately not to every single occurrence of "requirement"/"stage"/etc. across the whole UI (dozens of call sites), which would be disproportionate scope for this pass. Pluralisation is a naive `+"s"` (`useTermPlural`), which reads correctly for the regular-noun default terms but not for an override with an irregular plural (a project would need to type the plural form directly as its override in that case).

decisions.title: E2E stability: Multi-worker backend
decisions.statement: `BACKEND_WORKERS` uvicorn workers, default 4, via `backend/docker-entrypoint.sh`. - Postgres advisory locks (`services/process_coordination.py`): a startup lock serialises migrations/bootstrap/syncs, and leader election means only one process runs the scheduler, digest and disk monitor. - `LISTEN/NOTIFY` fan-out for WebSocket pub/sub. - Prometheus multi-process metrics. - Lock and listener…
decisions.rationale: connections are *detached* from the SQLAlchemy pool. A pooled connection's `close()` returns it to the pool and keeps the session, and its lock, alive; the new tests caught this. - Mechanism choices (advisory locks, NOTIFY, default of 4)

decisions.title: Org group deletion
decisions.statement: New endpoint `DELETE /orgs/{id}/groups/{group_id}`, org- admin only and tenant-scoped (404 for another org's group).
decisions.rationale: Memberships, nesting links and every role the group carried cascade with it. - No floor check is needed The C-U-08 project- manager floor counts only direct grants and a project group's direct user members (`rbac._direct_project_managers`). The last-org-admin floor counts direct admins only. Neither counts anything an org group carries, so deleting one can't take either floor below one. A guard copied from `delete_project_group` was written first and then removed, because it could never fire. A test pins the property instead: deleting a group that grants Project Manager, through a nested group, leaves the project's real manager in place. - Module veto: new generic `ModuleDefinition.validate_org_group_deletion` hook (`run_org_group_deletion_hooks`). Compliance implements it to block deleting its fallback compliance-managers group while a standard relies on it, since the setting's foreign key is `ON DELETE SET NULL` and would otherwise silently drop that floor. Core imports no module code. - UI: the group's side panel gets "Delete group", confirmed with the same Tier 1 `ConfirmDialog` and toast as project groups, and refusals show the server's reason as an error toast. Tier 1 rather than Tier 2 for consistency with project-group deletion, the same operation one level down. - Audit: `org_group`/`deleted`, recording the name, member count and granted org role. - Security review (identify → verify → remediate): - Authorization: org admin only, tenant-scoped (tested). - Floors: the project-manager floor is unaffected by design (tested) and the Compliance fallback group is protected (tested). - Audit logging: present (tested). - No Restricted-classified data is returned. - Outcome: no regression found.
decisions.section: Org groups are deletable; e2e specs delete their throwaway orgs (2026-10-05)

decisions.title: Org-wide compliance dashboard listings batched
decisions.statement: With the merged polluted data, the five dashboard endpoints made 200 to 1,000 queries each, about 5 per assignment plus one per requirement row for outstanding actions.
decisions.rationale: Fired together under suite load, they kept `org-compliance-view` from ever reaching network-idle. `ComplianceVersionCache.preload_organization` now loads the whole org's data in about six queries: active assignments, versions, standards, requirements, assessment rows and scheduled reviews. Every project is then walked from memory. Single-project callers are unchanged, since without a preload each accessor queries on first use. Outstanding actions loads each assignment's assessments in one query. - On the merged data: 768 → 14 queries and 0.56s → 0.15s for non-compliant requirements (pending approvals and reviews-due are the same), and 1,030 → 164 queries and 0.77s → 0.29s for outstanding actions. - A test pins the cost of an extra project at one query or fewer. It fails without the preload.

decisions.title: Concurrent requirement/action creates got the same code (500)
decisions.statement: Found when two specs created requirements in the same project at once: both got the same code, HW-FN-311, and the second hit the unique `(project_id, unique_code)` constraint.
decisions.rationale: The two legacy counters, `next_requirement_seq` and `next_action_seq`, read and incremented without a lock, unlike `services.sequences`, which locks the project row. Both now lock the row and re-read the counter first: the in-memory `Project` may have been loaded before the lock, so its value can be stale. The two-transaction race test fails without the lock.

decisions.statement: The core "approved Requirement needs a change request to be linked" gate.

decisions.title: Shared code instead of copies

decisions.title: A second generic extension point instead of cross-module imports
decisions.statement: Modules never import each other, and Pain Points/Decisions are other modules' tables.
decisions.rationale: `ModuleDefinition.artefact_summary_providers` (`ArtefactSummaryProvider(get, list_for_project)` → `ArtefactSummary`) plus `registry.get_artefact_summary`/`list_artefact_summaries`/`has_artefact_summary_provider` lets Stakeholders validate (same project, owner module enabled), label and list targets generically. Context & Strategy and Decision Management each register their own provider; the frontend mirror is `TierAModuleDefinition.artefactPaths` + `modules/artefactPaths.ts`. Documented in `docs/modules.md` §4f. A test asserts the stakeholders package imports no other module.

decisions.title: One declarative table, not one router per kind

decisions.rationale: Link types are created per org on first use via the existing `get_or_create_link_type`.

decisions.title: Kinds and who may hold them
decisions.statement: Experiences Pain Point, Provides Requirement, Is affected by Requirement (Stakeholder or Persona); Consulted on Decision, Approves, Reviews (Stakeholder only — a Persona is an archetype, not a person who is consulted or signs off); Approves/Reviews target a Requirement or a Decision. "Approves / Reviews" is two kinds because one link type couldn't say which.

decisions.title: Stakeholders & Personas, Relationships: Reserved target
decisions.statement: "Uses Design / System Element" is declared but `available_target_types` is empty and creation is a 409, until a module registers a provider for `design`/`system_element`.
decisions.rationale: The UI shows a muted note, not an option.
decisions.section: Module 2 (Stakeholders & Personas) Phase 3 — Relationships (2026-10-05)

decisions.title: Stakeholders & Personas, Relationships: Tenancy and authorisation
decisions.statement: A target must belong to the request's project (404 otherwise, including another tenant's and a sibling project's); listing is per project, so a shared org Stakeholder/Persona shows only this project's links.
decisions.rationale: Writes need the holder kind's manage gate in the project (`stakeholder_owner`/`persona_owner` or the FGAC grant), so each role confers nothing on the other kind. A project owner may therefore link an org-scoped holder to *this project's* records, which is project-level data, not an edit of the org record. A target is only shown to a caller holding `(target_type, view)`, so a relationship never reveals a title the owner module's own screens would hide.

decisions.title: Cross-artefact gap checks count only artefacts inside the readable scope

decisions.rationale: The cost is that a gap list can over-report; it can't leak. Decisions are resolved through `registry.get_artefact_summary`, never by importing Module 4, so R6's Decision counts stay 0 until Module 4 Phase 7 links them.

decisions.title: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements: No depth limit
decisions.statement: The plan capped the tree at depth 3 and the map at 2; the user asked for a modal that lets either go as deep as they like and scroll.
decisions.rationale: The server still caps one `link-graph` read at 3 hops and 150 nodes, so depth is unbounded by *re-rooting*: opening a tree branch reads one hop around that record; the map reads two hops then one hop per "Show more" and merges the reads. Nothing is prefetched.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: A trace keeps its direction
decisions.statement: A branch continues only through edges with its own `flow`, so it never doubles back through the record it came from; a record already on the tree's path is not repeated, which ends a cycle.
decisions.rationale: The map likewise draws only direction-consistent edges.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Map capped at 60 drawn records
decisions.statement: Breadth-first, nearest the record first, with a note giving the shown and total counts; the tree is uncapped and is the way to reach the rest.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Empty-state hint is text, not a link
decisions.statement: The plan said to link org admins to the link-type direction setting.
decisions.rationale: The panel does not know the viewer's organisation role, and a link a non-admin cannot use is worse than none, so the hint names the setting's location. Revisit if the panel gains the org role.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements: Native keyboard access
decisions.statement: Tree branches are real buttons (`aria-expanded`) and records real links (Tab, Enter); the map is SVG links in reading order with its own scroll region focusable, and the Tree tab is its text alternative.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements: Map polish pass
decisions.statement: The map gained tinted lanes (Upstream | This record | Downstream, a wide Related band), arrowheads pointing downstream (at the focus end for upstream links, none for related), relationship pills on the edges, a direction stripe and a ringed focus node, a spacing pass (the "Show more" pill's padding is now symmetric and named, `CHIP_PAD_X`; node text padding is `MAP_NODE_PAD_X`; nodes are taller…
decisions.rationale: so labels clear the pill; the kind line fits "Stakeholder need · Active"), a key (`LinkTraceLegend`, opened from a "Key" button in a `Popover` so it takes no space until asked for, on the user's follow-up request; it omits "Show more", which labels itself, and the hint says a click opens the record), and hover/focus highlighting of a record's own edges with the rest dimmed. **"Show more" is now a labelled pill hanging off the node's bottom edge** (`LinkTraceChip`), the one place no edge attaches (main-band edges leave from a node's sides; a related edge only leaves from the bottom of a node that is already open), with a tooltip, hover and focus states, a spinner while it reads, and a "No more links" note on the record once it found nothing. Click-to-select was deliberately not added: a click on a record is navigation (its title is a real link), so a second meaning for the same click would break both. Tint and stripe colours come from the theme's existing info/accent/muted variables and are secondary to position, headings and arrowheads. The map scroller's height now fits the dialog so only the diagram scrolls. Loading uses the shared `Spinner`.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements: Tabs focus ring
decisions.statement: The Trace tabs rendered exactly like every other `Tabs` bar; what looked off was the heavy rectangular outline `.tabs-tab:focus` left around a tab after a mouse click, against the underline language the style guide sets for tabs.
decisions.rationale: It is now `:focus-visible` in the shared stylesheet, so every call site (Link types, Compliance) gets the same fix and keyboard focus is unchanged.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Skip and join, not just filter
decisions.statement: A hidden record is not drawn, but its own links, in the same direction, are joined to the record in front of it ("via DEC-001" in the tree, a dashed edge on the map); a chain of hidden records is followed to the end.
decisions.rationale: The focus record is never hidden. Hidden records the tree or map needs are read on demand (one read each), so switching the filter off costs nothing.
decisions.section: Trace tree and map: Platform enhancements Phase 7 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Decision Management reports: Project-level only
decisions.statement: No organisation-wide variant: the module defines no org-scoped role to put in `org_role_key`, and the framework requires one for an aggregate.
decisions.rationale: Include-child-projects covers a parent and its sub-projects.
decisions.section: Decision Management reports: Platform enhancements Phase 8 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Waiting time comes from the audit log
decisions.statement: D2 measures days from the latest `proposed` / `submitted_for_review` audit event matching the Decision's current status, falling back to `created_at`; `updated_at` moves on every edit and would reset the clock.
decisions.section: Decision Management reports: Platform enhancements Phase 8 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Decision Management reports: D4 definition of "linked"
decisions.statement: A live Decision (Draft to Approved) has rationale when it links to at least one non-Decision artefact the caller can read; Decision-to-Decision links (supersession, depends on, conflicts) are not rationale.
decisions.rationale: Requirements are checked directly (core), every other type through its owner's artefact-summary provider. A requirement is uncovered when no non-archived Decision links to it in either direction. A link to a record the caller cannot read counts as absent, so a gap list may over-report but never reveals a hidden record.
decisions.section: Decision Management reports: Platform enhancements Phase 8 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Neutral report document model and DOCX export: Library: python-docx
decisions.statement: Pandoc/LibreOffice rejected (extra binary, larger attack surface).
decisions.rationale: Added to `backend/requirements.txt`.
decisions.section: Neutral report document model and DOCX export: Platform enhancements Phase 9 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: PDF unchanged, proven rather than assumed
decisions.statement: Before the refactor, golden PDFs were generated from both renderers with ReportLab's invariant mode (plain and branded, chaptered and continuous, empty, hostile markup, an image).
decisions.rationale: After it, both framework PDFs are byte-identical and every requirement PDF has identical page-content streams; the only difference is a new PDF `/Title` metadata entry (the project name), added because the model always carries a title. A `Gap` block (vertical whitespace, ignored by DOCX) exists only to keep the PDF's spacing exactly as it was.
decisions.section: Neutral report document model and DOCX export: Platform enhancements Phase 9 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Inline Markdown stays literal in both formats
decisions.statement: The PDF has always shown a paragraph's source text verbatim (`**bold**` appears with its asterisks).
decisions.rationale: Interpreting inline formatting in only DOCX would make the formats differ, so neither does, and no hyperlink or field-code path exists to attack. Richer inline text would be a change to both renderers together; the plan's "hyperlinks limited to http(s)/mailto" rule therefore has nothing to constrain today.
decisions.section: Neutral report document model and DOCX export: Platform enhancements Phase 9 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Not in scope: Compliance's two bespoke reports
decisions.statement: `generate_project_compliance_pdf` / `generate_org_compliance_pdf` (their own multi-line narrative cells, routes outside the framework) still render PDF/CSV only; the plan scoped DOCX to the requirement report and framework reports.
decisions.rationale: They sit on `report_document` helpers unchanged. Moving them onto the model is the natural follow-up if Word is wanted there.
decisions.section: Neutral report document model and DOCX export: Platform enhancements Phase 9 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: A blank entry is "inherit" and stores no row
decisions.statement: The old model kept an empty string and a nullable org column and needed `*_is_organisation_default` flags to explain which was which.
decisions.rationale: Now "no row" is the only way to inherit, `PUT` replaces a scope's whole set (a type absent from the body loses its content), and the editor's "Use inherited" simply blanks the field.
decisions.section: Per-report-type content across template, project and organisation tiers: Platform enhancements Phase 10 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Placeholders are substituted into parsed text blocks, not into Markdown source
decisions.statement: `report_model.fill_placeholders` runs inside `markdown_to_blocks` on heading, paragraph and list text: allow-list `project_name`, `report_title`, `generated_on`, `organisation`; unknown `{{...}}` stays literal; single pass (a value is not rescanned).
decisions.rationale: Substituting into the source before parsing, as the plan literally said, would let a project named `# x` or `![](attachment:...)` become a heading or an image; block-level substitution makes the value ordinary text by construction. It applies to ad-hoc `pre_markdown`/`post_markdown` sent by the generation page too, since that page sends the unfilled resolved text.
decisions.section: Per-report-type content across template, project and organisation tiers: Platform enhancements Phase 10 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Report types are a drop-down, not tabs
decisions.statement: Every enabled module report is a type, so a real organisation lists a dozen or more; the first build used `Tabs` and wrapped over four rows.
decisions.rationale: `ReportContentEditor` now has a labelled "Report type" select (types holding content are suffixed "(has content)"), shared by Report Defaults, the template modal and Report Setup.
decisions.section: Per-report-type content across template, project and organisation tiers: Platform enhancements Phase 10 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Per-report-type content across template: Org bundle
decisions.statement: Export carries every tier's entries (`org.json` `report_content`, each template's `content`, each project's `report_content`) and the images they reference (`report_images` map plus `files/` entries); import re-uploads each as a shared resource of the target organisation and rewrites the `attachment:` ids (`services/report_content_bundle.py`), reusing a byte-identical resource already there so…
decisions.rationale: importing twice does not duplicate. Bundles written before this change (flat `default_report_*`, template `intro/chapters/appendices`, project `report_*`) still import, as a `requirements` entry; an entry for a report type this build lacks is skipped with a warning rather than failing. Org logo and login-background bytes already round-tripped; a regression test now pins it. Platform-level default logos remain unexported (not org-owned). Merge import writes template and project content but never the target's organisation tier (the org profile rule).
decisions.section: Per-report-type content across template, project and organisation tiers: Platform enhancements Phase 10 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Nested-project checklist (CLAUDE.md), decided at design time
decisions.statement: This is a project-scoped definition-like table and children *do* fall back to the nearest ancestor, always on, independent of `role_inheritance_mode`.
decisions.rationale: Edit and delete stay scoped to rows a project owns; only the resolve path walks ancestors. Unlike Action Types, resolution is per field, so a child can inherit its intro from one ancestor and its appendices from another.
decisions.section: Per-report-type content across template, project and organisation tiers: Platform enhancements Phase 10 (2026-10-11)

decisions.title: Risk Management Phase 0 sign-off: Per-cell rating override (core)

decisions.rationale: Becomes **Phase 1a**, a core scoring extension that Pain Points and Stakeholders also receive. Shape (names a band, two-axis models only, org + project, all-or-nothing, ancestor fallback)

decisions.title: Risk Management Phase 0 sign-off: Treatment effectiveness

decisions.title: Risk Management Phase 0 sign-off: Nested projects

decisions.title: Principal fields are a column pair, not three FKs
decisions.statement: `<name>_type` and `<name>_id`, the id without a foreign key (the `ArtefactLink` trade-off), shaped by `models/principal.py` helpers (`principal_type_column`, `principal_id_column`, `principal_check_constraint`) so every field has the same check constraint (type in user / org_group / project_group; an optional field has both columns or neither).
decisions.rationale: `PrincipalType` is a closed core enum; a module never adds a value. , confirming the plan's proposal: three typed FKs per field cannot be shared by a validator, a filter or a usage hook.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 1: the shared principal mechanism (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Membership is the existing resolver
decisions.statement: `rbac.effective_project_group_member_ids` is new (direct users, nested org groups with their descendants, referenced source projects, each re-checked as same-organisation) and `rbac.project_group_ids_for_user` is its inverse; org groups reuse `effective_org_group_member_ids`.
decisions.rationale: A project group's membership counts even while it holds no role, unlike the role resolution, because a role-less group is still a named team.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 1: the shared principal mechanism (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Usage hook
decisions.statement: `ModuleDefinition.principal_references` (`PrincipalReference`: model, field, label, audit entity type, mandatory, optional `live_filter`) plus core's `CORE_PRINCIPAL_REFERENCES` (empty until Phase 6).
decisions.rationale: Core never imports a module. `live_filter` excludes older version rows: they are not counted or changed on deletion and render as a deleted group, so history keeps the id it recorded.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 1: the shared principal mechanism (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Deleting an in-use group
decisions.statement: `GET .../groups/{id}/usage` (org admin / project manager) and `DELETE ...?replacement_type&replacement_id&clear_optional` on both group routers.
decisions.rationale: Records still naming the group give 409 unless a replacement (user, org group, and for a project group also a project group of the same project; never a project group for an org group) takes every row, or `clear_optional` empties optional fields; a mandatory field always needs a replacement. Each changed row writes its own audit event (`principal_reassigned` / `principal_cleared`) and the group's `deleted` event records the counts. The UI is `GroupInUseDialog`, a configuration of the shared `DeleteInUseDialog` (extended with `renderMovePicker`, `moveHeading`/`moveHint` and `remove.heading`/`buttonLabel`, all optional) rather than a new dialog.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 1: the shared principal mechanism (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Both fields adopt the shared mechanism
decisions.statement: `Decision.owner` (mandatory) and `decision_maker` (optional) are `<name>_type` / `<name>_id` pairs built with the `models/principal.py` helpers; migration `0076` (module chain; the next free number is 0077) adds the type columns, backfills `user`, drops the two foreign keys to `users` and adds the check constraints.
decisions.rationale: Decision maker is included although only the owner was named, because the parity rule applies to it equally. , as the Phase 10 spec said; the user can trim it.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 2: Decision owner and decision maker (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: The owner gate uses effective membership
decisions.statement: `_require_owner_of_decision_or_role` passes for the owner user or any effective member of the owner group (`principals.is_principal_member`: transitive org groups, project groups with their nested groups).
decisions.rationale: Nothing else moved: the project-membership check runs first, so a group member without project access still gets a 404/403; the approve permission, the `decision_owner` role and the content lock are untouched, so a group owner confers no approval or edit right. , per the plan.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 2: Decision owner and decision maker (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Probe, not a capacity read
decisions.statement: (the three asks) and **Agent** (the mechanism).
decisions.rationale: `services/disk_monitor.py` could not have caught this: it only reads local disk percentage and never ran for the S3 backend. `services/storage_health.py` writes, reads back and deletes a tiny object through whichever backend is configured every 5 minutes, so it catches a full disk, a bad credential or an unreachable bucket alike, with no knowledge of the storage service's internals.
decisions.section: File storage health monitoring (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Four fields adopt the shared mechanism
decisions.statement: `PersonaVersion.owner` and `champion`, `StakeholderVersion.owner` and `StakeholderNeedVersion.owner` are `<name>_type` / `<name>_id` pairs; migration `0077` (module chain; the next free number is 0078) adds the type columns, backfills `user` on **every** version row (so history keeps who owned each version), drops the foreign keys to `users` and adds check constraints.
decisions.rationale: All four are optional, so none is `mandatory`. `StakeholderVersion.user_id` ("this stakeholder is this login") is an identity link and stays a user, as the plan said. , per the plan.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 3: Stakeholders and Personas owner and champion (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Scope rule (Phase 3)
decisions.statement: A project group is valid only on a project-scoped record in that project; an organisation-scoped Persona or Stakeholder is shared by every project, so it can name users and organisation groups only (`validate_principal` receives the record's `project_id`, `None` for organisation scope, and the UI passes no `projectId` so the picker never offers a project group there).
decisions.rationale: Already the Phase 1 rule; this is the first adopter with both scopes.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 3: Stakeholders and Personas owner and champion (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Versioned records and group deletion
decisions.statement: Each field declares `live_filter` (`valid_to IS NULL`): only the current version is counted and reassigned or cleared, and older versions keep the group id and show as a deleted group in history.
decisions.rationale: **New generic field `PrincipalReference.record_id_field`** (default `id`): for a version row the audit event must be about the Persona / Stakeholder / Need, not the version row's own id, which would be an audit entry about nothing a user can open. Found by looking at what `log_event` was passed for a version table, not by a failing test.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 3: Stakeholders and Personas owner and champion (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Three fields adopt the shared mechanism (Phase 4)

decisions.rationale: All three are optional, so none is `mandatory`. , per the plan.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 4: Context & Strategy owners (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Scope rule (Phase 4)
decisions.statement: Pain Point and Open Question are project-scoped, so they accept users, organisation groups and that project's groups.
decisions.rationale: A Guiding Principle is org- or project-scoped: an organisation-level one is shared by every project, so it takes users and organisation groups only (`validate_principal` gets `project_id=None`; the detail page passes no `projectId` for the org route, so the picker offers no project group).
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 4: Context & Strategy owners (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Three fields adopt the shared mechanism (Phase 5)
decisions.statement: `ComplianceStandard.owner` (**mandatory**), `ComplianceReview.owner` and `ComplianceRequiredActionAssessment.assignee` are `<name>_type` / `<name>_id` pairs; migration `0079` (module chain; the next free number is 0081) adds the type columns, backfills `user` on every row, drops the foreign keys to `users`, makes the standard's type `NOT NULL` and adds the check constraints. , per the plan.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 5: Compliance owners and assignees (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Scope rule (Phase 5)
decisions.statement: A standard and a standard-level review are organisation-scoped, so they name users and organisation groups only (`validate_principal` with no project); a project-level review and an assessment may also name that project's groups.
decisions.rationale: The old guards (`_require_org_member_or_none`, `_require_project_member_or_none`) are replaced by `validate_principal` on every write path.

decisions.title: Validation is deliberately looser in two places
decisions.statement: A standard created without an owner defaults to the creator and that default is not checked, because the manage gate admits a server admin or a module-role holder who is not an organisation member (a bootstrap-admin test creates standards in organisations it does not belong to); a supplied owner is always checked.
decisions.rationale: An update that leaves the owner unchanged is not re-checked either, so editing the name of a standard created that way is not blocked.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 5: Compliance owners and assignees (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity: Notifications fan out
decisions.statement: The review sweep notifies the compliance officers or managers plus every member of the owner (`principal_recipients`: a person in several groups is told once; inactive, archived and banned users are dropped); the required-action sweep notifies the assignee's members, and falls back to the project's compliance officers when the field is empty or no member can be notified (previously an inactive…
decisions.rationale: assignee was still addressed). A recurring review's next cycle copies the owner pair.
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Phase 5: Compliance owners and assignees (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: One field adopts the shared mechanism

decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Risk "5b": Risk owners (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity, Risk "5b": The owner gate uses effective membership
decisions.statement: "The owner may assess a treatment / record a review" is now `is_risk_owner` (`is_principal_member`): a member of an owner group passes, a removed member stops passing, and the group confers nothing else (a member still cannot edit the Risk; that stays the Risk Manager role).
decisions.section: Users and groups on parity, Risk "5b": Risk owners (2026-10-12)

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity, Risk "5b": Notifications fan out
decisions.statement: `risk_recipients` returns every active member of the owner (`principal_recipients`), and falls back to the project's Risk Managers and Project Managers when the Risk is unowned **or the owner group has no one to notify** (an empty group would otherwise silence the Risk).
decisions.rationale: The review sweep and the change-detection hook both go through it. Behaviour change: a user owner who is inactive, archived or banned is no longer notified (previously the id was addressed regardless), consistent with the other adopters.

decisions.title: Users and groups on parity, core fields: Approval_authority_id stays a user

decisions.title: CI: frontend coverage badge stuck at 0%: Drift guard

decisions.title: Stakeholders & Personas, Stakeholder groups: Write gate (item 31)
decisions.statement: Every group write needs the Stakeholder manage gate for its tier (owner role, or a `(stakeholder, manage)` grant) **or** a `(stakeholder_group, manage)` grant.
decisions.rationale: The second was added after review: registering the artefact type creates the atom, and an atom an administrator can grant that does nothing would mislead. The new atom does not confer Stakeholder management (tested).

decisions.title: List filter and group-by run client-side; the API offers both too

decisions.section: Module 2 (Stakeholders & Personas) Phase 3c: Stakeholder groups (2026-10-13)

decisions.title: Stakeholders & Personas, Stakeholder groups: Exclusive groups and visibility
decisions.statement: The `exclusive_children` check considers only groups the actor can see (organisation plus this project), so the error never names another project's group; the one case it cannot see (a stakeholder in a sibling branch only through another project's group) is accepted.
decisions.rationale: Setting the flag, or moving a group, re-checks the whole subtree and is refused if any stakeholder would sit in two branches.

decisions.title: Help is a link, not a page

decisions.rationale: The header icon is an external link (`target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, accessible name "Help (opens in a new tab)"); `/help` redirects for old bookmarks. The six help files were diffed against the website first: sign-up and external users, roles, lifecycle, change requests and reports are all covered there, so nothing was moved.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 1: neutral report label, configurable Help link, docs image (2026-10-14)

decisions.title: Platform review: Docs site image
decisions.statement: `docs/website/Dockerfile.prod` builds the static site and serves it with unprivileged nginx (port 8080, health check, stock welcome page removed).
decisions.rationale: The site bakes its base path into asset URLs, so `DOCS_BASE_URL` and `DOCS_URL` are build arguments read by `docusaurus.config.ts` (defaults unchanged for GitHub Pages). The published image is built for the root of its own host; a sub-path such as `/docs/` needs a self-build with `--build-arg DOCS_BASE_URL=/docs/` (a reverse proxy cannot strip a prefix from a site with absolute asset URLs). CI builds a `/docs/` variant first and smoke tests the home page, a nested page and a 404, then builds and pushes `-docs` with the same tags as the other images. Compose gets an optional `docs` service under the `docs` profile (port 8200). Found while testing: the health check must use `127.0.0.1`, because `localhost` resolves to IPv6 in the alpine image while nginx listens on IPv4, which left the container permanently "starting".
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 1: neutral report label, configurable Help link, docs image (2026-10-14)

decisions.title: Platform review: Markdown renderer hardening
decisions.statement: `utils/markdown.ts` rendered a ```` ```mermaid ```` fence as raw, unescaped HTML for the help page.
decisions.rationale: After the help page was gone its only caller is `RichTextEditor`, which renders user-authored report content, so that branch was an HTML-injection path (a fence containing an ``). The branch is removed: every fence now renders escaped, and a story pins it. The `mermaid` dependency (about 875 lock-file lines) and the `.help-content` styles went with it.

decisions.title: Platform review: Link checker
decisions.statement: `scripts/check_doc_links.py` fails on a Markdown link or a `docs/...md` path that does not resolve.
decisions.rationale: It runs in the CI `docs` job, in `.githooks/pre-commit` and as `backend/tests/test_doc_links.py` (skips when the repository root is not mounted, as in the backend container). It skips `docs/website/` (Docusaurus already fails the build on broken links), ignores links quoted in code spans, and checks only the real links in `decisions.md`, whose path mentions may name since-deleted files.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 2: closed plans archived, doc link checker (2026-10-14)

decisions.title: Source files never name plans
decisions.statement: Plans are archived and rewritten, so a comment citing one rots.
decisions.rationale: Every explicit plan reference (document names and paths, "Phase N" attached to one) was stripped from about 200 source files, and `scripts/check_doc_links.py` now fails on a source file naming a plan document. The strip ran from `HEAD` with an AST comparison (Python) and a comment-stripped comparison (TypeScript) proving only comments and strings changed; a first attempt that also tidied punctuation damaged `()` in code and was discarded and redone. **Completed afterwards ** The remaining wording was rewritten by hand and by narrow, reviewed rules across about 450 source files: every "Phase N"/"Phase 7.1"/"Phase A" tag (including paths wrapped across two lines), "Module N" numbering, plan question and resolution numbers ("Q8", "resolution 3"), "PR4"-style sub-steps of the members/groups rework, "roadmap item N", "UX audit" asides, "Design Principle N", "the plan's" phrasing and "this phase". Chronological "Phase N adds ..." module docstrings became present-state descriptions. `ux-audit-2026-08.md`, `future-modules-2026-09-overview.md` and `Compliance_Module_Requirements.md` (: all complete) moved to `docs/plans/completed/`. Kept deliberately: requirement section numbers (`§20`) that cite those archived documents, and pointers to `docs/decisions.md` and `docs/ux-style-guide.md`. One test file was renamed from `test_platform_review_phase8_link_and_action_locking.py` to `test_link_and_action_locking.py`. Verified: Python syntax trees identical to `HEAD` outside strings, TypeScript identical outside comments and test titles, `tsc` and `ruff check` clean, link checker clean.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 2: closed plans archived, doc link checker (2026-10-14)

decisions.title: Platform review: IPv6 listeners
decisions.statement: The first pass skipped the nginx `[::]` listener (Agent judgement: no benefit once probes use `127.0.0.1`, and a risk on kernels without IPv6).
decisions.rationale: The user overruled it: IPv6 is never excluded intentionally. Every listener now serves both families: nginx (frontend, docs image) has `listen PORT;` plus `listen [::]:PORT;`; the backend binds `--host ::`; the docs dev server binds `::`; the MCP server binds a pre-created dual-stack socket, because `host="::"` alone is IPv6-only under asyncio (verified: IPv4 was refused until the socket was passed in). Verified in the test stack: backend, MCP, frontend and docs each answer on `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`. Probes stay on `127.0.0.1` (works on every host). Rule added to `CLAUDE.md` ("IPv6 Support") and pinned by `backend/tests/test_ipv6_listeners.py`. The production docs image (`Dockerfile.prod`) gets the same nginx template; its image build was not run here.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 12: container health probes address 127.0.0.1, `/health` returns 503 (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Platform review: Measured first (Phase 3)

decisions.title: Platform review: Measured first (Phase 4)
decisions.statement: `orphaned-controls.spec.ts` (`ICON_REPORT=1`) against the unchanged stack: 21 icons in medium buttons were 14px on the six pages that had any (requirements list and detail, action detail, project admin, organisation admin, preferences); every other page was already correct.

decisions.title: Platform review: CSS decides
decisions.statement: `.btn svg` 16px, `.btn-sm svg` 14px, `.badge svg` 12px (every pill icon was already 12px), all `flex: none`.
decisions.rationale: The rule beats lucide's `size` attribute, so the fix is structural. A codemod (TypeScript API) then removed the now-redundant `size` prop from 181 icons nested in a JSX element whose `className` has `btn`; icons passed to a component prop (for example `icon={<Plus size={16} />}`) are left alone because the component, not the CSS, decides there.

decisions.title: Platform review: Scale outside buttons
decisions.statement: 12px in pills and removable chips; 14px beside caption or small text, disclosure chevrons and `ActionMenu` items; 16px beside body text, in headings and in the nav rail.
decisions.rationale: The existing code already followed it apart from four icons, changed: `Spinner` 18 to 16, `Info` in `ProjectMembersTable` 13 to 14, the nav-rail "Customise navigation" icon 12 to 14; the removable-chip and removable-list "x" icons stay 12. decisions.title: Platform review: Collapsed rail uses 14px
decisions.statement: The user preferred the smaller icons the collapsed rail showed before (a side effect of the squeeze below).
decisions.rationale: Made deliberate: `.nav-rail-icons .nav-link svg` is 14px; the expanded rail stays 16px; the check enforces both.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 4: icon sizes set by the button's CSS (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Platform review: Behaviour kept
decisions.statement: Requirement and Action restore stay immediate (no dialog); the Requirement and Action pages keep editing in place (no Edit pencil; they edit inline).
decisions.rationale: Where a page rendered controls regardless of role and let the backend refuse, it still does (Activate/Retire, Action Archive); where it gated by role (`canArchive` on a Requirement, owner-only on a read-only org record shown inside a project) the menu item is omitted, not disabled.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 5: one `RecordHeader` and one object-action menu (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Specs that located a heading by its code
decisions.statement: The Decision page's `h1` was the code (`DEC-001`) and the Requirement page's was `code — name`; with the code now a sibling of the title, those specs (decision lifecycle, decision group owners, mockup engagement) and the `openRequirementBy*` helpers look inside `.record-header` instead.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 5: one `RecordHeader` and one object-action menu (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Bundles refer to a record by title, not by its label
decisions.statement: Stakeholder relationship and engagement-outcome bundles referenced linked records by summary label and matched them by label on import.
decisions.rationale: Labels now lead with a code that an import numbers afresh, so a Need's reference (`NEED-001 title`) would have matched the wrong record or none. `services.codes.label_title` strips the code on export and on the import match, so the reference is the title as before.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 7: codes for every project-scoped type (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Platform review: Display rule
decisions.statement: A record the organisation owns is **always shown qualified by the organisation code** (`ACME-PER-001`), on organisation pages as well as in projects.
decisions.rationale: The plan said the Phase 6 rule applies "with the organisation standing in for the project", which would let it show bare on organisation pages when the person prefers; but a bare `PER-001` is ambiguous the moment it is pasted next to a project's own `PER-001`, and an organisation page has no project noise to avoid. A project-scoped record follows the Phase 6 rule unchanged.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 8: codes for organisation-scoped types (2026-10-18)

decisions.title: Components first, then call sites
decisions.statement: About 250 forms' fields were hand-written `<label className="stack">` blocks across ~130 files, so the sweep built the missing shared parts and moved every call site onto them rather than touching forms one at a time.
decisions.rationale: `RecordFormFields` moved out of the Stakeholders module to `components/FormFields` because core pages now use it (core must not import a module's directory). New or extended: `FormFields` (`ColorField`, `FileField`, `UploadField`, `ToggleField`, `labelExtra` for an `OverridePill`, `autoGrow`, `inputProps`, `disabled`), `FormActions` (error, Cancel, primary, `leading`), `LabeledSelect` (`hint`, `ariaLabel`, `inputProps`), `ActionFields` (one action form for the Actions page, the requirement's create-and-link dialog and the action page). The mechanical part used throwaway scripts (a field/footer/checkbox rewrite and a TypeScript-AST pass that wraps a dialog's fields in a `FormGrid`); every changed file was then read and the layout (pairs, full-width titles and text areas) set by hand where the script's guess was wrong. The scripts are not kept.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 10: forms aligned to the style guide (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Detail pages use the compact picker
decisions.statement: `RecordPrincipalField` always renders `PrincipalPicker compact`, so owner, champion and assignee on the Persona, Stakeholder, Need, Pain Point, Guiding Principle and Open Question pages show the value with a pencil and an x, not an open search box.
decisions.rationale: Stories and the two group-owner specs now click "Assign: …" first.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 10: forms aligned to the style guide (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review: A guard
decisions.statement: `scripts/check_form_markup.py`, pinned by `backend/tests/test_form_markup.py`, fails a file that brings back a hand-written labelled field or a Cancel/Save row; its baseline (`scripts/form_markup_baseline.json`) is empty, so no file is exempt.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 10: forms aligned to the style guide (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Changing a default never moves an existing project
decisions.statement: Changing `project_default_enabled` first freezes the current value into the row-less projects of every organisation without its own row.
decisions.rationale: Where an organisation has the module hard-off, `freeze_projects_module_default` is deliberately a no-op (existing behaviour), so such a project picks the default up when the organisation turns the module on.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 13: module availability (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Hiding reverses a recorded behaviour
decisions.statement: `GET /orgs/{id}/modules` omits non-entitled modules unless the caller is a server admin (it used to list them greyed out for upsell); `GET /projects/{id}/modules` omits modules the organisation has disabled or has no entitlement for, and the project sub-component list omits organisation-disabled sub-components.
decisions.rationale: A project's own rows are kept, so a module returns with its state on re-enable. The single-module `.../enablement` reads still answer. The Project Admin page lost its now-unreachable "turned off for your organisation" branch and string.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 13: module availability (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, navigation: Deviation from the plan
decisions.statement: The plan had `Layout.tsx` read `GET /projects/{id}/modules`, which is one request per module for sub-component state.
decisions.rationale: `GET /projects/{id}/enabled-modules` now returns `disabled_sub_components` per module, computed by `is_module_subcomponent_enabled` (the function the routers' 404 gate uses), so nav and routes cannot drift. The client filter is generic over `sub_component`.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 14: navigation (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Challenge to the plan: one shape for every kind would have lost features
decisions.statement: A single table with the shared columns cannot carry Stakeholders' Influence, Interest, Cadence, Last engaged and Groups columns or the group filters and Group by (the answer to "custom column" for categorical data).
decisions.rationale: So several kinds share one table (`PeopleListView`, `RecordListView` over a `PeopleRow` model with a Kind column) and **one kind alone shows that kind's own list** (`PersonaListView`, `StakeholderListView`, the extracted `NeedListView`, the group manager). The kind choice is in the URL. The last chip cannot be turned off.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 16: one People page and "Save and activate" (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, quick-link on create: Component and contract
decisions.statement: `QuickLinkField` (`components/`) is a combobox that only **collects** links (`CollectedLink`, the shape the change-request form already uses); `useCommitQuickLinks` creates them after the record exists and toasts the outcome.
