decisions.rationale: The field searches with the Links panel's own finder, asked about a record that does not exist yet (`DRAFT_ARTEFACT_ID`, which the finder reads already accept for the proposing form), so the server's rules apply unchanged: visibility, enabled modules, link-type restrictions and the caller's link authority. A caller who cannot link the type gets a refusal from the options read and the field renders nothing. `defaultOptionKey` (the "Related to" default) moved to `components/linkOptions.ts` and the Add-link dialog now uses it too, so both controls default a pair identically.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 17: quick-link on create (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, quick-link on create: Endpoint: POST /projects/{pid}/artefacts/{type}/{id}/links/bulk
decisions.statement: The plan named `/projects/{pid}/links/bulk`.
decisions.rationale: The link router is page-artefact-scoped (the page record is the authorisation anchor: project membership, then `link`/`manage` or the default role), so the bulk call sits beside the single-link one and reuses `create_link_for_artefact` per link rather than a second authoriser. It is all-or-nothing: any refusal rolls the transaction back and re-raises with the single-link status and `Link i of n:` prefixed to the message; a pair repeated inside the request is a duplicate; the request is capped at 25 links (`MAX_BULK_LINKS`) so a client cannot turn it into a bulk writer.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 17: quick-link on create (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, quick-link on create: Failure semantics
decisions.statement: The create call is unchanged (making every create endpoint transactional with links would change all of them).
decisions.rationale: If the link step fails the record is kept and an error toast says it was saved, why the links were refused, and to add them from its Links panel. The plan's "retry on the new record" is that Links panel: the shared `Toast` has no action button and a new one is not justified by one use.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 17: quick-link on create (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, quick-link on create: Same project only
decisions.statement: Linking to an ancestor or descendant project needs the project selector, which stays in the Links panel's dialog; a compact field should not grow it.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 17: quick-link on create (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, quick-link on create: Requirement create
decisions.statement: Its "Create & attach files/links" second step carried a requirement-only "Add link" popover built on the legacy endpoint, a fourth one-off linking widget.
decisions.rationale: The link half is removed, links are chosen in step one with `QuickLinkField` (any linkable type, not only requirements), and the step is now **Create & attach files**. This is a visible rename; the Storybook stories and `requirement-create-attach.spec.ts` were updated, and the unused `requirements.*` link strings removed.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 17: quick-link on create (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, tags on every item type: Requirement keywords are tags
decisions.statement: Requirements already had "keywords (aka tags)" (requirement C-M-01) in their own table; a second tagging mechanism beside them would give a requirement two overlapping label sets.
decisions.rationale: Migration 0102 copies every `requirement_keywords` row into a tag in the requirement's project (whitespace collapsed, 40 characters, grouped per project) and drops the table; `RequirementOut.keywords`, the create/update `keywords` field, the `keyword` list filter, the CSV `keywords` column, templates, reports and the bundle keep working over tags (`services.tags.get_keywords`/`set_keywords`). Consequences: keywords now **keep the casing they were typed with** (old ones are lower case); the `keyword` filter compares ignoring case; the downgrade recreates the table with lower-cased names. **Behaviour change:** an update that **omits** `keywords` now leaves the tags alone (it used to clear them, because the default was an empty list), because the requirement edit form never edited keywords and sent back a stale copy, which would now remove tags added from the header since the page loaded. The MCP `update_requirement` and the frontend no longer send a stale copy.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 18: tags on every item type (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Platform review, tags on every item type: Name rules
decisions.statement: Trim, collapse inner whitespace, 1 to 40 characters, unique ignoring case with the first casing kept.
decisions.rationale: The plan said "no commas"; **semicolons and control characters are refused too**, because the CSV keyword column splits on `;` and a tag containing one could not round-trip. A record carries at most 50 tags.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 18: tags on every item type (2026-10-19)

decisions.title: Rows from another project are read-only in the list
decisions.statement: (Agent): no bulk checkbox or reorder buttons; they open in their own project (`rowProjectId`).
decisions.rationale: The stakeholder group filter and create pickers offer this project's groups only. **The risk matrix plots every listed risk **, so a product's risk can be read across the sub-projects that make it up; likelihood and consequence levels are organisation-wide, so a related project's risk lands in the right cell, and the cell colours use the viewed project's bands.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 20: nested-project scope filter on every list (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review, global search: Organisation-owned Strategies
decisions.statement: They are created and read at organisation level (the organisation overview and `/orgs/{id}/modules/context_strategy/...` pages) and no project shows them, so they are not `organization_owned` (per-project hiding).
decisions.rationale: They declare `organization_subcomponent` instead: in the all-projects scope they are searched for every member of an organisation where the matching organisation-level sub-component is on, the rule the organisation's own list applies (`require_org_subcomponent_enabled`), and open at their organisation page (`TierAModuleDefinition.orgArtefactPaths`). A search of one project also covers its organisation's records, on by default (, 2026-10-20): `include_organization_records` on the request, else the person's `search_include_org_records` preference (Preferences → Search, validated as a boolean), shown as an **Include organisation records** filter on the page in a project scope; a project where the module's sub-component is off never shows them. A module's unit (a standard) does not return them. The first version of this phase said they had no page and excluded them; that was wrong and was corrected on the user's challenge (2026-10-20).
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 23: global search (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Compact search dropdown
decisions.statement: `SearchHitSummary` gains `density="compact"`: one line per hit, muted code, title truncated with a tooltip, place right-aligned.
decisions.rationale: The row does not repeat the type badge (the dropdown's group heading already names the type) or show status and snippet (they stay on the results page). Slimmer headings and padding; ARIA combobox behaviour unchanged.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Quick-link reach: root cause
decisions.statement: The link-type matrix is complete (a backend test pins that every registered type reaches every linkable type), so it was not a data gap.
decisions.rationale: The defect was in the finder: it matched the stored label (`REQ-001 Title`), so a code typed the way it is shown elsewhere (`ACME-REQ-001`, qualified by the project or organisation code) found nothing. The finder now also tries the text without the searched project's or organisation's code, and (, 2026-10-20: "it should be an actual search") searches by **words**: every word must appear in the record's code or title, in any order, anywhere in the title. The type's own query narrows by the longest word and the other words filter in Python (up to 200 candidates). The placeholder now says "Search any record by code or title…". `QuickLinkField` and the Links panel's dialog share the endpoint, so both gain it.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Help in the test stack
decisions.statement: `tests/container/docker-compose.yml` is already a separate test stack that runs its own `docs` service on port 3001, so it sets `HELP_URL` to that directly instead of an extra `docker-compose.local-docs.yml` overlay.
decisions.rationale: The production `docker-compose.yml` keeps the public default. If an overlay is still wanted, say so.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Filter placement
decisions.statement: `ListPageLayout` puts the title, its actions, an optional tab strip and the list in the left column and the filter panel in the right column from the title's row down, so the panel's top edge is level with the title.
decisions.rationale: The filter comes after the list in the DOM (the list is first for keyboard and screen-reader users); grid areas place it, and on narrow viewports the order is title, filter, list. 17 pages moved onto it (the module record lists, Requirements, Change requests, Actions, Reviews due, Notifications, Search, Projects, Organisations, Compliance standards, and the People and Needs pages through `RecordListView`'s `page` prop). Page settings such as the scoring-model switcher are children of the list column. `scripts/check_list_page_layout.py` (a pytest) fails a file with an `<h1>` and a hand-written `side-grid`; the baseline is empty and the two admin shells (`OrgAdminPage`, `ProjectAdminPage`, whose `side-grid`s are sections inside tabs) are exempt with the reason. Embedded panels with no page title of their own keep the plain `side-grid`. Playwright pins the alignment on three lists.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Menus that fit
decisions.statement: `Popover` takes `fit`, and `ActionMenu`/`MenuButton` use it: the menu is as wide as its longest label up to the viewport width less a margin, and an item that still does not fit wraps (`.menu-item`) instead of clipping.
decisions.rationale: `clippedMenuItems` (in `testing/orphanedControls.ts`) is the shared check; the label "Stakeholder from organisation user" is unchanged.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Required fields
decisions.statement: `required` on the shared field components (`TextField`, `TextAreaField`, `DateField`, `LabeledSelect`, `PrincipalFormField`, `RecordFieldGroup`, `CheckboxField`, `ColorField`, `FileField`, `UploadField`) draws a `*` after the caption and sets `required`/`aria-required` on the control.
decisions.rationale: The star is drawn by CSS (`::after`), so it is not part of the caption's text: a lookup by label text still finds the field and assistive technology does not read it. `FormGrid` shows a "* required" line only while it contains a mark (`:has`). "(optional)" and "(required)" are removed from every label; `scripts/check_required_markers.py` (a pytest) fails a label that says "(optional)". Marked in this change: the create and edit forms of every record type (requirement, change request, action, persona, stakeholder, need, group, engagement, decision and template, risk and its lifecycle, review and treatment dialogs, strategy, guiding principle, future state, open question, pain point, compliance standard, requirement, evidence, review, version and applicability), the project, organisation, user, group, role and tag forms, and the signup page. **The sign-in pages are exempt :** email and password are expected there, so they carry the browser's `required` but no `*` or legend. Each was compared with what its Save button blocks on and the API's required fields. Marked fields on forms that are not in a `FormGrid` (the tag add row) show the star with no legend. **Not swept:** settings panels that save on change (SMTP, branding, security) have no Save gate and no required field, so there is nothing to mark; a field added later declares itself. Story tests (`requiredCaptions` in `testing/requiredMarkers.ts`) pin the marked fields for the persona, strategy, decision, new-user and shared-field forms.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Custom tag colours
decisions.statement: `ColorField` gains a hex box (accepts `#rgb` and `#rrggbb`, with or without `#`, stores lower-case `#rrggbb`), preset swatches and an optional "no colour" button; `TagAdminPanel` uses it for adding a tag and for a per-tag "Change colour" dialog in place of the select with its unusable "custom" option.
decisions.rationale: **Security (SOC 2 change-management review):** the colour reaches a style attribute, so it is validated on write (`^#[0-9a-fA-F]{6}$`, already enforced by `services.tags.validate_colour`) and now also read-validated by `TagChip` (a bad stored value shows no colour). Found and fixed while testing: the pattern used `match` with `$`, which accepts a trailing newline; it now uses `fullmatch`. Nine injection strings are tested on create and update.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Add user menu
decisions.statement: One `AddUserMenu` ("Add user ▾": Invite user, New user) on Server Management and Org Admin.
decisions.rationale: `AddUserModal` takes a fixed `mode` (no mode select in the form). API, behaviour and audit unchanged; the access-control policy was re-read and needs no change.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 26: third review, nine usability fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Version label
decisions.statement: `RecordHeader` takes `version` and shows "Version n" (muted, `title` "Version n of this record") on the badge line, never as its own line.
decisions.rationale: Persona, Stakeholder, Need, Strategy, Future State, Guiding Principle and Risk pass it; the hand-formatted `v{n}` is gone from every detail page (list columns still show `v{n}` in their own "Version" column, where the header names it). It is shown always for a versioned record, so it never appears and disappears. "Archived" on Persona, Stakeholder and Need was appended subtitle text; it is now a `Badge`, as it already was on Risk.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Tag input
decisions.statement: `TagInput` is the chips plus a chip-shaped `[+]` ("Add tag", `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, tooltip) that opens the shared `Popover` holding the unchanged input and suggestion list.
decisions.rationale: Enter adds the tag and keeps the popover open, cleared and refocused; Done, Escape (the suggestion list first, then the popover) or an outside click closes it and focus returns to the `[+]`. The popover is portalled outside the surrounding form, so Enter never submits it, and a modal's own Escape handler ignores it (the focus-containment guard in `useDialogA11y`). `RecordTags` and `TagField` get it through `TagInput`, so there is one implementation.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Detail cards
decisions.statement: `DetailCard` (heading, optional `action`) is the one card element of a detail page; the header stays on the background.
decisions.rationale: **Finding: the plan assumed the existing panels were already cards; they were not.** `RepresentationPanel`, `HeldNeedsPanel`, `EngagementTimelinePanel`, `EngagementAudiencePanel`, `ResearchPromptsPanel` and the outcomes panel are `RecordFieldGroup`s (field-shaped), and the versions table, attachments, comments, scoring, rating, treatments and reviews were sections separated by a top border. every `RecordField`, `RecordPrincipalField` and field-group panel of a record goes in the page's one "Details" card; each section-shaped block is its own `DetailCard` ("Versions", "Attachments"/"Evidence", "Comments", "Scoring", "Rating", "Treatments", "Reviews"). `VersionHistoryTable`, `RecordDiscussion` and `ArtefactCommentsSection` draw their own `DetailCard`, so a page places them directly. Comments inside are flat rows (`.comment-row`), also in `CommentThread` used by the Requirement, Change Request and Action pages, because cards never nest (they were cards inside a card before). A research finding stays a card of its own beside Details. Requirement, Change Request and Action pages moved from hand-written `card stack` to `DetailCard`; the Compliance standard overview and assignment status cards too. `scripts/check_detail_cards.py` (a pytest, empty baseline) fails a card written inside a `DetailCard`; `entity-accent-card` rows are not cards.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Nav rail
decisions.statement: The scroll container starts at the top of the rail (the first link is level with the collapse toggle, measured).
decisions.rationale: The spec inset the WebKit track and relied on right padding for Firefox; Firefox's thin scrollbar cannot be inset, so that left the bar under the toggle there. Instead the container leaves the toggle's inner half (`--nav-toggle-overhang`, 14px) free with `margin-right`, so neither a link nor the scrollbar can run under it in any browser. Cost: icon-only links centre in 42px rather than 56px (a 7px shift). A measured Playwright check covers both widths (`nav-rail-geometry.spec.ts`).
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Overview scope select
decisions.statement: `ProjectScopeSelect` is the bare select; `ProjectScopeFilter` keeps its `FilterField` and hint using it, and the overview uses it `compact` in the title row beside the primary button, with the explanation in a `Tooltip` (hover and keyboard focus) mirrored in a screen-reader-only description (`aria-describedby`) so touch and assistive technology do not lose it.
decisions.rationale: A widened scope has an accent outline. The select renders nothing for a project with no openable relatives.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: One aside card
decisions.statement: `DetailLayout` owns the card and the title (the tab strip, or one "Links" heading without Activity).
decisions.rationale: `ArtefactLinksPanel` reads `useInDetailAside()` and draws no card or heading there, keeping its Add, Trace and View options buttons right-aligned. A standalone or `compact` use is unchanged.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Transition comments: audit of where each comment is stored and shown
decisions.statement: Pain Point (triage, accept, address, close, reject, mark duplicate), Open Question, Strategy, Future State, Guiding Principle, Persona, Stakeholder, Need, Decision (approve, reject) and Risk (status change) all write the comment as the audit event's `detail.comment`; the versioned ones (Strategy, Future State, Guiding Principle, Persona, Stakeholder, Need, Risk) also store it as the version's…
decisions.rationale: `change_note`, which their Versions table shows. The gap: `describeActivityEntry` rendered only `change_note` (appended after a dash), so a Pain Point, Open Question or Decision comment, and a change request's decision note, never reached the Activity tab, the project overview card or the history page. Fixed once in the shared renderer: `activityEntryNotes` returns `comment` then `change_note` (each once), shown by `ActivityNote` as a quoted block under the sentence, collapsed to three lines with "Show more", as text (never HTML). **A third key was found: a change request's decision audit wrote `detail.note`.** It now writes `comment` (and omits an empty one); entries written before the change keep `note`, which the renderer reads for change request approved/rejected entries only. Decision propose and submit-for-review take no comment (the endpoints have none). **Open question for the user (not added unprompted):** requirement approve takes no comment (its change note is the fixed "Approved directly."); should it take an optional one like the other approvals?
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Score settings
decisions.statement: `DirectoryTable` columns take `headerAction`, rendered as a sibling of the sort button (never inside it), so pressing it does not sort.
decisions.rationale: The Pain Point Score column carries a `SettingsPopoverButton` (new, shared: gear, tooltip and accessible name stating the active model and roll-up, accent border when either differs from the default) holding the existing `ScoringModelSwitcher`. The choice stays per view and is not saved (the popover says so). The Blocker badge moves after the title beside Intentional (`badge-after`); the Score cell holds only the score. The detail page's scoring panel and the prioritisation report keep the badge beside the score (not a title column).
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Platform review: Checkbox text
decisions.statement: `.checkbox-label` (flex, no wrap, text hangs beside the box) is used by `CheckboxField`, the switch field and the ten hand-written checkbox labels found by the sweep (change request fields, Links view options, permission picker, tree select, delete-in-use, CSV mapping, group forms, compliance assessment).
decisions.rationale: Labels that wrap a number or date input stay `.row`.
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Pain Points open by default
decisions.statement: "Open only" starts ticked unless the link says `open=0` or names a slice the default would hide (a valid `status`, `scored`, `blocker=1` or `intentional=only`); `open=1` keeps it on.
decisions.rationale: The empty state says when the default caused it. The report's "Pain Points" figure links with `open=0` because it counts every status. The open question about Risks, Decisions and Open Questions was answered by the user and implemented: see "Leftovers (October 2026) Phase 4".
decisions.section: Platform review (October 2026) Phase 27: fourth review, ten display and layout fixes (2026-10-20)

decisions.title: Leftovers, close-out: Branch protection applied
decisions.statement: The "Main Branch" ruleset is Active with the five current check names; read back from GitHub, it requires 0 approvals with no bypass actors, and the user chose to keep it at 0 (): there is one maintainer and nobody else can approve, and GitHub does not count an author's own approval, so 1 would block every merge.
decisions.rationale: The change-management policy and control matrix record this as an accepted exception (no author/merger segregation until a second reviewer exists), not a gap awaiting action.
decisions.section: Leftovers (October 2026) Phase 11: close-out (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: PR checks: Dependency scan
decisions.statement: `dompurify` 3.4.16 carried a critical advisory; raised to `^3.4.17` (no ignore list, per the scan's policy).
decisions.section: PR checks: dompurify bump, stale e2e specs, stakeholder router cache (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: PR checks: Slow Reports page
decisions.statement: `/report-catalogue` took 3-4.6 s because the Stakeholders module's `get_router()` / `get_project_router()` rebuilt a 775-route composite router on every call.
decisions.rationale: They are now built once (`functools.cache`, about 0.15 s per catalogue call), which was the cause of the Reports-page specs that failed their first attempt and passed on retry (also seen on `main`). Pinned by `test_router_build_cached.py`.
decisions.section: PR checks: dompurify bump, stale e2e specs, stakeholder router cache (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: No short-form exception for the form header
decisions.statement: 47 files use `FormActions`; 44 sit in a `Modal` or `SidePanel` and 3 are inline panels (`AddToGroupControl`, `AnonymousParticipantsPanel`, `RepresentationPanel`) that keep their own row of actions.
decisions.rationale: A size threshold would add a judgement per form for no benefit, so every dialog form gets the header, as the user asked for `Modal` (Q4); `SidePanel` forms follow by the one-component rule.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 1: rules written first (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Cover title
decisions.statement: The cover-page title is the accent colour as text on white paper, a different rule from text on a fill.
decisions.rationale: `branding.readable_on_white` darkens the accent (same hue and saturation, lightness lowered in 0.03 steps) until it reaches 4.5:1 against white, the same approach as the screen's `ensureContrast`; a dark accent is left exactly as chosen. Used by the PDF (`title_flowables`) and Word (`_cover`) covers. Header and cell text still use `text_on` (black or white on a fill).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 2: coloured report cells keep their colour in PDF and Word (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, form header: No form attribute needed
decisions.statement: The style guide says forms submit through the `form` attribute; in practice none of these dialogs use a `<form>` element (buttons call `onSave` directly), so there is no Enter-to-submit behaviour to preserve and nothing to rewire.
decisions.rationale: A future dialog that does use `<form>` can pass `form` through `FormActions`' buttons when needed.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 5: form header (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, form header: Popover resets the slots
decisions.statement: It has no header, and its `FormActions` (`AddToGroupControl`, the requirement-detail popovers) would otherwise jump to the dialog behind.
decisions.rationale: The three inline panels (`AddToGroupControl`, `AnonymousParticipantsPanel`, `RepresentationPanel`) are outside any dialog and stay inline.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 5: form header (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, form header: Hand-written footers converted
decisions.statement: Three dialogs had their own Cancel/primary rows: `CsvImportWizard`, `StandardImportModal` and the compliance reject-with-note dialog.
decisions.rationale: They now use `FormActions`, which gained `cancelDisabled`, `saveTone="danger"` and an optional `onSave` (Cancel-only while the import conflict choice is shown). Confirmation dialogs (`ConfirmDialog`, `DeleteInUseDialog`, `RestoreOrgDefaultsButton`) are not forms and keep their short footer; the style guide's confirmation tiers govern them.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 5: form header (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Why filters moved into the URL
decisions.statement: Restoring a scroll offset is only correct if the list shows the same rows, and 17 of the 18 `ListPageLayout` pages held their filters, search and sort in `useState`, so Back remounted them with defaults.
decisions.rationale: The plan already said such a list is moved to URL state first. `hooks/useUrlFilter.ts` gives `useState`-shaped hooks (`useUrlText`, `useUrlFlag`, `useUrlChoice`, `useUrlList`, `useUrlSort`); `useTagFilter` and `useOpenOnly` are built on them, so 13 lists got the tag filter in the URL at once. Alternative rejected: persisting each page's state object in `sessionStorage`: it would have worked without touching the pages' hooks, but the filtered list would not be bookmarkable or shareable and every page would need its own serialiser.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 6: list position kept (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Deep links keep their names
decisions.statement: `status`, `priority`, `stage`, `completed`, `open`, `intentional`, `blocker`, `scored`, `model`, `rollup`, `roadmap`, `overdue` and the others are the same parameters the dashboards and reports already linked with.
decisions.rationale: They used to seed state once and (on Requirements and Change Requests) be stripped from the URL; now the URL is the state, so the strip effects are gone and the e2e specs that expected a bare `/requirements` after a dashboard link accept a query string. Search is `q`, the archive switches `archived`, defaults are absent (`open` is the exception: always written, because its default depends on how the page was opened and must not be re-derived after the person picks a status).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 6: list position kept (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, list position kept: Same-tick setters
decisions.statement: React Router's functional `setSearchParams` applies each call to the same stale parameters, so a "clear filters" handler would keep only the last write; `write()` in `useUrlFilter` accumulates within the tick (story `SettersInOneHandlerAllTakeEffect`).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 6: list position kept (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Rename must not override
decisions.statement: The shared panels send `definition` only when it changed, otherwise renaming an organisation type in a project would copy the organisation's text into the project as an override and freeze it against later organisation edits.
decisions.rationale: Pinned by a story.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 7: Pain Point types get an optional definition (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Shared panels, opt in
decisions.statement: `OrgTypeVocabularyPanel`/`ProjectTypeVocabularyPanel` take `withDefinition`; Persona, Stakeholder and Risk types are unchanged.
decisions.rationale: `DefinitionListField` gained `multiline` (a growing text area in the row and in the add form), the generic form of the long-text rule. In the add form the text area's accessible name is its visible label, so it differs from the row's.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 7: Pain Point types get an optional definition (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Project bundle: a gap
decisions.statement: Context & Strategy (and Decisions) register no `project_bundle_hooks`, so their records and type vocabularies do not travel in a project bundle at all.
decisions.rationale: The user ruled that every module's project components must (, 2026-10-23); it is its own phase (7b) in the plan, and the Phase 7 `definition` fields are included in it. The user also ruled that the organisation bundle must carry every module's organisation-level components and that both are standing agent instructions (); `CLAUDE.md` now has the section **Every Module Travels in the Project and Organisation Bundles**. Not fixed in Phase 7.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 7: Pain Point types get an optional definition (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Preview is the apply, rolled back
decisions.statement: Each row runs through the type's own create or update inside a savepoint; a preview rolls the whole transaction back, an apply commits the valid rows and records one `records_imported` event.
decisions.rationale: The alternative, a second "dry" implementation of each type's validation, would drift from the real one and is exactly what an update-capable import must not do. Consequence: a provider must never commit, and a preview takes the project row lock for the length of the run (counters are rolled back, so a preview burns no record code).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 8: record tables, the export and import extension point (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Approval gate and version lock
decisions.statement: Requirement `status` is export-only (`approval_gated=True`; a test fails if a gated provider imports a column named `status`).
decisions.rationale: The edit goes through `services.requirements.edit_requirement`, which the edit endpoint now calls too (extracted, not copied), so an approved requirement refuses the row with the endpoint's own message ("changes must be made via a change request") and a draft keeps its status. `services.actions.create_action` / `edit_action` and the shared list queries (`filter_requirements`, `list_actions_filtered`) were extracted the same way, so a filter or rule added to the endpoint reaches the file. Create applies the creator rules the form does (earliest target stage by default, importer as owner).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 8: record tables, the export and import extension point (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Per tag, not per type
decisions.statement: The plan allowed "per tag (and, if needed, per type)".
decisions.rationale: Nothing needs per-type yet: the tag already says what kind of data a column is, and a per-type matrix would be 20 rows times 3 tags of mostly identical answers. A later need adds a column to the override table without changing the resolver's callers.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 8b: personal-data policy for record export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Server default is a default, not a ceiling
decisions.statement: An organisation administrator may allow a tag the server excludes.
decisions.rationale: That is what the user asked for ("organisations must be able to set this differently"), but it means a server administrator cannot stop a tenant from choosing to export its own personal data. The control the server keeps is the fresh-install default; there is no "forbid" tier. Raise it if a deployment ever needs a hard ceiling.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 8b: personal-data policy for record export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, shared list actions: Legacy Requirements endpoints removed
decisions.statement: `GET /requirements/export`, `POST /requirements/import`, `services/requirement_csv.py`, `RequirementImportResult` and the old wizard are gone; nothing else called them (MCP, scripts and bundles do not).
decisions.rationale: Their tests moved to the shared routes (`test_requirement_table_roundtrip.py` for the full round trip, custom fields, owner and reviewer, row errors; the component-category, lifecycle, core-principals and link-nesting tests now call `.../records/requirement/...`). The format changed in ways a person with an old file will meet: `component_prefix`/`category_prefix` are `component`/`category`, `owner_email`/`owner_group` are one `owner` cell, enums are labels (`Recommended`), and the first column is `code`. The wizard's mapping step absorbs the header differences (an old file maps by hand once); the cell differences (a group in `owner_group`, a raw enum value) are the one thing it cannot map, which is accepted because the plan makes one file format both ways the rule. The audit event `requirements_imported` is replaced by the engine's `records_imported`.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 9: shared list actions (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, shared list actions: Choices on a column
decisions.statement: `RecordColumn.choices` (and `RecordColumnOut.choices`) lists the accepted cell texts when they are a closed list.
decisions.rationale: It exists so "same value for every row" keeps the pick list the old wizard had for component, category, level and target version, instead of a free-text box that invites a typo. Only a column with `choices` gets the toggle (the old wizard's own rule: name and description are per-row by nature). Category choices are the distinct prefixes of the project (a category prefix is unique per component, not per project), so the preview, not the picker, reports a component and category that do not pair.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 9: shared list actions (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Import is no longer behind the New button
decisions.statement: `RequirementsPage` used a `SplitButtonTrigger` whose only alternative was "Import from CSV".
decisions.rationale: With Export and Import now on every list beside its create button, the chevron duplicated an entry and put import behind a menu stop on one page only. The page has a plain "New requirement" button; `SplitButtonTrigger` stays for a create button with real alternatives. The style guide's list-actions pattern and the split-button section say so. Open to override.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 9: shared list actions (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Import template moved into the Export menu
decisions.statement: "Download import template" is an `extras` entry of the Export popover (the old wizard had it there too); it is the importable columns, `code` first, header only.
decisions.rationale: The popover also carries a muted `note` line for columns the personal-data policy left out ("Some columns holding personal data are left out by your organisation's policy" or "... you need the permission to export personal data"), which closes the Phase 8b hand-off.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 9: shared list actions (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: It is a platform report, not a module report
decisions.statement: The report framework is module-shaped (`ModuleDefinition.reports`, routes under a module's mount, catalogue by `module_key`), and this report belongs to no module: putting it on one module would be the per-module hand-edit the boundary rule forbids, and inventing a pseudo-module would make `is_module_enabled` lie.
decisions.rationale: So the route is a plain core router, `report_catalogue` prepends `record_list_report.catalogue_entry` (`module_key` `platform`), and the document is built with the framework's shared pieces (`ReportResult`, `render_pdf`, `render_docx`, branding). No registry, enum or stylesheet gained a module value; `test_the_report_names_no_module` pins it.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 10: the Record list report (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: CSV is the export's file, byte for byte
decisions.statement: `format=csv` returns `table_csv` of the same table, so the Reports page's CSV re-imports instead of being a second, lossy CSV with display labels.
decisions.rationale: PDF, Word and JSON use the columns' display labels.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 10: the Record list report (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: A file is an export, the on-screen run is not
decisions.statement: `pdf`, `docx` and `csv` write one `records_exported` event (counts, filter keys, sensitivity tags, never cells); `json` does not, because the Reports page re-runs it on every parameter change and it shows what the list already shows.
decisions.rationale: Authored report content (introduction, chapters, appendices) is not offered for this report, only the organisation's branding template, because there is no per-type report key to attach content to.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 10: the Record list report (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, the Record list report: Row limit for documents
decisions.statement: A PDF or Word file over 5,000 rows is refused with a 413 that says to narrow the filters or download the CSV; the CSV and the on-screen run have no such limit.
decisions.rationale: A document of many thousands of rows holds a worker for a long time and cannot be read.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 10: the Record list report (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, roll-out A, core types: Change requests are export-only
decisions.statement: The request was import with update "where feasible".
decisions.rationale: It is not, for a change request: its content depends on its `kind` (which requirement fields change, proposed links, attachments, an action to add or remove, a link to remove), `changed_fields` decides what approval applies, and the request moves through submit, vote and approval. A flat file cannot author that safely, and the create/update logic lives inline in the router (about 270 lines) rather than in a service a provider could call. A file that created drafts of one kind only would be a second, narrower form. The reason is `CORE_NOT_IMPORTABLE["change_request"]` (new, the core twin of `ModuleDefinition.not_importable`, merged by `get_not_importable_types`), which the wizard, the `.../columns` response (`importable: false`, `not_importable_reason`) and the import route (422) all use.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 11: roll-out A, core types (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: One write path for page and file
decisions.statement: Same rule as Phase 8: the import calls the type's own create and edit logic, extracted rather than copied.
decisions.rationale: Context & Strategy: new `edits.py` (`create_project_*_record`, `edit_project_*_record`, `project_*` list queries) which `project_router.py` now calls for all five types (the content lock past review, the terminal outcome of a Pain Point and an Open Question, principal tenancy, the Pain Point type check and the `created` / `updated` audit events live there once). Stakeholders: each `*_from_payload` that committed is split into `stage_*` (validate, write, audit, no commit) plus the wrapper the endpoint still calls (`stage_persona`, `stage_persona_update`, and the same for stakeholder, need, engagement, finding, group). The provider builds the endpoint's own request payload (`PersonaCreate`, `StakeholderUpdate`, ...) from the cells, so length limits, required fields and tenancy checks apply unchanged and a refusal is that row's error. Shared list queries: `project_personas`, `project_stakeholders`, `filter_engagements`, `visible_groups`, `project_strategies` and the other four, used by the list endpoints and the export (a test per type compares the export with the filters).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Status is export-only for all eleven
decisions.statement: Strategy, Future State and Guiding Principle move through propose / review / approve; Pain Point and Open Question through transitions that need a comment; Persona, Stakeholder and Need through activate / retire.
decisions.rationale: A created record starts as its form starts it (draft, submitted, open). The five Context & Strategy providers are `approval_gated`, so the registry test fails if one ever imports `status`.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Page filters reach the file
decisions.statement: Those pages filter in the browser, so each provider takes the same filters server-side by the page's names: `status`, `priority`, `search` (code or main text, case-insensitive, as the page matches), `include_archived`, plus Pain Point `open_only`, `hide_intentional`, `only_intentional`, `blockers_only`, `scored` (with `model_key` and `rollup`, evaluated by the scoring service the page's score…
decisions.rationale: column uses), Future State `roadmap_only`, `target_passed_only`, `no_measures_only`, Open Question `open_only`, `overdue_only`, `unowned_only`, Persona and Stakeholder `type` (a type name), `include_org`, `include_hidden` and a Stakeholder `group_id` / `direct_only`, Engagement `type` (a channel label) plus its participant, persona, date range and retention filters. Unknown values are a 422. **Bug found and fixed on the way:** the Strategy, Future State and Guiding Principle search boxes searched the literal text `{s.unique_code} {s.title}` (a missing `$`), so searching by code never matched; they now search the code and title. The Future State and Open Question "date passed / overdue" filters compared the UTC day; the pages and the export now use the person's day (`localToday()` and `effective_today()`).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Personal data (Phase 12)
decisions.statement: A Stakeholder's name, role and organisation or group are `personal`; its contact details and availability `contact`; its description, interests, responsibilities, goals, priorities, constraints and workflows, and an Engagement's summary and notes, `free_text_people`.
decisions.rationale: A Persona is a fictional archetype and holds none; owner, champion, reviewer-style columns follow the Requirement owner precedent (untagged: a project member already sees them). A fresh install therefore exports a Stakeholder as code, type, cadence, scope and status only. A create whose required column the policy removed fails with the payload's own message ("name: Field required"). The tagging test the plan deferred (`test_every_column_that_holds_a_persons_data_is_tagged_and_a_persona_holds_none`) fails if one of these columns loses its tag; the data classification policy names them.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Organisation-owned rows in a project list
decisions.statement: The Persona, Stakeholder and Stakeholder Group lists show the organisation's records too.
decisions.rationale: They are exported with the organisation-qualified code (`ACME-PER-001`, always qualified, as `display_code(organization_owned=True)` defines) through a new generic `RecordTableProvider.organization_owned`, and are never matched by an import into a project (`find` searches the project's own records), so they come back as an unknown-code row. `include_org=false` leaves them out. Changing an organisation's records from a file is the organisation-level export and import (Phase 12b).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: People list with several kinds
decisions.statement: `RecordListView` gains `exportRecords` (one kind or several); `ListPageLayout` takes one or an array; a list of several kinds renders a named pair per kind (**Export personas**, **Export stakeholders**, **Export groups**) because each button acts on one record type.
decisions.rationale: A kind with no concept of an active filter (a group has no status or type) is not offered while that filter is set, as its file would be empty. The group manager (a tree, not a filtered list) shows the group pair beside its New menu. The Engagements page was moved onto `ListPageLayout` (it had a hand-written `<h1>` above the list), so its filters now live in the URL and it keeps its place like the other lists. The tag and scope parameters repeated in eight pages moved into `utils/listFilterParams.ts` (`addSharedListFilters`).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12: roll-out B, Context & Strategy and Stakeholders (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Organisation tier is a second table on the provider, not a second provider
decisions.statement: The columns are declared once (`_strategy_columns`, `_persona_columns_for(type_choices)`, ...) and serve both tiers; only what differs is declared in `OrganizationRecordTable`: the sub-component that gates it, how the organisation's own rows are listed and found, and which create and edit function and role check apply.
decisions.rationale: Rejected: a separate registry of organisation providers (every column would be written twice) and an optional `owner` argument on every existing callable (it would have changed the signature of some forty provider functions for six types).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12b: the organisation's own lists export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: One write path for the organisation page and the file
decisions.statement: The organisation Strategy, Future State and Guiding Principle endpoints had their create/edit logic inline.
decisions.rationale: It moved to `edits.py` as `create_*_record` / `edit_*_record` taking a `RecordOwner` (a project or the organisation); the `*_project_*` functions are thin wrappers, and the organisation endpoints and the file both call the same functions (lock past review, principal check, audit event). New shared list queries `organization_strategies`, `organization_future_states`, `organization_guiding_principles`, `organization_personas`, `organization_stakeholders`. Personas, Stakeholders and Groups were already scope-generic (`stage_*` take a scope and ids).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12b: the organisation's own lists export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Org Pain Point type vocabulary
decisions.statement: Stays out: it is a vocabulary panel, not an artefact type with a code or a list, and it already travels in the organisation bundle.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 12b: the organisation's own lists export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: One write path
decisions.statement: Decision create/edit/list queries moved to `modules/decisions/edits.py`, Evidence to `modules/compliance/evidence_edits.py`, Risk's `create_/update_risk_from_payload` split into `stage_risk` / `stage_risk_update` plus committing wrappers, as in Phase 12.
decisions.rationale: The endpoints and the file call the same functions (type and principal validation, the content lock, the accepted-risk lock, the version history, the audit events).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 13: Risk, Decisions and Compliance export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Status is never imported
decisions.statement: Risk, Decision and the assessment type are `approval_gated`; their status is export-only.
decisions.rationale: A new risk starts Identified and a new decision Draft, as the forms start them.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 13: Risk, Decisions and Compliance export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Compliance types without a code
decisions.statement: The compliance requirement and its two project-level children have no `PREFIX-nnn` code (the recorded gap), so the Code column of their exports holds the requirement's clause reference (blank when it has none) and the standard, version and requirement columns identify the row.
decisions.rationale: Because they cannot be matched by a code they are not importable, and each also has a workflow reason (assessments go through justification and approval; a standard's requirements are authored in a draft version tree). Giving them real codes would make them importable only if a reason to import them existed; it was not done here.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 13: Risk, Decisions and Compliance export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX: Engine generalisation
decisions.statement: `OrganizationRecordTable.subcomponent` may be `None` for a module with no sub-components (Compliance), and an organisation tier may be export-only (no `create`/`update`, a reason in `not_importable`).
decisions.rationale: The Standard Requirement is organisation-owned: its organisation tier lists every standard's requirements (filters `standard`, `version`, `search`, `include_archived`); its project tier lists the requirements of the versions assigned to the project. The project tier accepts `include_archived` only so both tiers share filter names; it has no effect there.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 13: Risk, Decisions and Compliance export and import (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, the bulk edit grid: Closed-value kinds only
decisions.statement: A grid cell is an `editable`, importable column of kind `enum`, `number`, `date` or `bool` (`GRID_KINDS`).
decisions.rationale: Free text is not a grid cell: the Long Text Fields Grow rule says a fixed box hides what was typed, and most providers marked every text column `editable` in Phases 11–13, which would have made the grid a wall of text boxes. The plan's "select for enums, number, text" is narrowed accordingly; people (owner, assignee) are not grid cells either (no inline picker exists; the form and the file edit them).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Pain Point scores are now file columns
decisions.statement: Severity, Frequency and Confidence are `RecordColumn`s holding the "all personas" level's name, declared once and used by the file and the grid.
decisions.rationale: The Phase 12 reason (the grid owns them) disappears once the grid reads the same column set; keeping two definitions of one field is the failure the shared-provider design avoids. A Pain Point scored per persona exports them blank and refuses a value (`cell_lock`; one level cannot stand for several personas, and the scores endpoint refuses mixing). Writing them is the manager tier, as the scores endpoint (`can_update` for Pain Points is already that tier; a create with scores from a non-manager is a row error). They are written through the same function the endpoint calls (`edits.edit_project_pain_point_scores` over `set_pain_point_scores`), so the `scored` audit event and level validation are unchanged. Per-persona editing stays on the Pain Point page.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Concurrency without a version column
decisions.statement: A save sends the changed cells and the values they had when the grid loaded (`expected`); a cell whose current value differs is refused with 409 and the current value, and nothing is written.
decisions.rationale: Types with a version lock keep it through their own update path; this covers the types without one (a Pain Point's scores, an Action's due date) and a stale grid left open for hours. Only changed cells are sent, so two people editing different columns of one record do not conflict.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, the bulk edit grid: One request per row
decisions.statement: Up to five rows are in flight at once; no bulk endpoint, since the per-row path keeps the type's own lock, validation and audit event and one failure never blocks the rest.
decisions.rationale: A failed row keeps its changes and its message; the toast reads "N saved, M failed". No second audit event: the type's update path already records one.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Read-only reasons are a courtesy, not the gate
decisions.statement: `RecordTableProvider.read_only_reason` (a row: an approved Requirement, a Pain Point at a terminal outcome) and `RecordColumn.cell_lock` (a cell) let the grid show text with the reason instead of a control that would be refused; the save still refuses with the type's own message (409) if a client ignores them.
decisions.rationale: Other types without the hook show a control and report the refusal in the row; adding the hook there is a one-line change per provider. Rows of a related project (widened scope) and organisation-owned rows are always read-only in the grid; their edit is in their own project or the organisation.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: View mode is a stored preference
decisions.statement: The Pain Point list uses `useViewMode` (synced to the person's preferences like the other tile/list toggles) rather than a URL parameter, so the grid comes back as the person left it.
decisions.rationale: The grid's filters are the list's URL filters, so list position and links are unchanged.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 14: the bulk edit grid (2026-10-23)

decisions.title: Compliance derived types are not counted
decisions.statement: `in_overview=False` on the standard requirement, a project's assessment of it and the required-action assessment: they are one row per clause of an assigned standard, so counting them would let a 400-clause standard drown every real record and describe the standard, not the work.
decisions.rationale: Compliance Evidence is authored and counts.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 15: the overview's total records by type (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: One kebab menu instead of Export and Import buttons
decisions.statement: A list's export and import actions are one "List actions" `ActionMenu` (kebab icon) beside the New button: Export as CSV, PDF and Word file, Download import template, Import from CSV, and the personal-data note as the footer.
decisions.rationale: `ReportExportButton` is unchanged for report pages; the list actions no longer reuse it.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: one export and import menu, help above dialogs (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Named "List actions" with the kebab icon
decisions.statement: A burger icon was first used and read as the List view toggle directly under it, so the trigger is the kebab every other action menu uses and is named "List actions", like the "{record} actions" menus.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: one export and import menu, help above dialogs (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Several kinds share one menu
decisions.statement: The People list (and the Compliance assignment detail) render one `ListActions` per kind; each registers its items with the surrounding `ListActionsMenu` under a heading (`ActionMenuItem.group`), so the page shows one kebab, not one per kind.
decisions.rationale: A `ListActions` rendered alone wraps itself in its own menu, so the ten direct call sites needed no change. Registered on mount so kinds keep their order however late their columns arrive.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: one export and import menu, help above dialogs (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Import opens the file picker from a menu item
decisions.statement: The hidden file input stays mounted outside the popover (the popover unmounts on select), and the item clicks it synchronously inside the click that chose it, which keeps the browser's user-activation requirement.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: one export and import menu, help above dialogs (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: List data and form UX review changes: Help tooltips above dialogs
decisions.statement: `Tooltip` sat at z-index 1000 under `Modal` and `SidePanel` (1100) and `Popover` (1150), so field help opened inside a create form was drawn behind it (the Scoring model help on a new Pain Point).
decisions.rationale: The bubble is now 1175, above every overlay a control can sit in and below the toast stack (1200). Pinned by `FieldHelp.stories.tsx` (`HelpShowsAboveAModalAndASidePanel`).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: one export and import menu, help above dialogs (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Filter panel collapses to a bar above the list
decisions.statement: The first version, a text "Hide filters" button on the title row, was rejected as ugly.
decisions.rationale: The panel is now a card with a "Filters" title row (as other cards have, so the search no longer floats untitled) holding a round icon toggle in the nav rail's style; collapsing hides the card, the list takes the full width, and a "Filters" button with the panel icon appears next to the List actions kebab on the title row to bring it back (the user's correction of a first version that left a slim bar above the list). `ListPageLayout` provides the state through `FilterCollapseContext`; the state survives a change of view. The grid view first started collapsed (`filterCollapsedByDefault`); the user reversed that, so switching to the grid leaves the panel as it was and the prop was removed. Not persisted: it is the page's state, because a remembered "collapsed" on a list the person later opens to filter would read as a missing panel. A collapsed panel does not show whether a filter is active (the result count does reflect it).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: hideable filter panel, grid editing state and column choice (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Editing column in the grid
decisions.statement: Each row states Editable, Partly editable or Read-only with the reason in a tooltip (and for assistive technology), beside the Status column, which is now shown by default.
decisions.rationale: Generic: the reason is the provider's existing `read_only_reason` / `cell_lock`, so no module code changed.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: hideable filter panel, grid editing state and column choice (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Column choice in the grid
decisions.statement: A Columns menu (`MultiSelectDropdown`) lists every column of the type; non-editable ones show as read-only text.
decisions.rationale: Stored per person and type as the keys toggled away from the default (`grid_columns:{type}` in `ui_preferences`), so new columns follow the default. A column with unsaved changes cannot be hidden, so a change is never saved out of sight.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: hideable filter panel, grid editing state and column choice (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: List data and form UX review changes: Toolbar simplified
decisions.statement: Columns is a table-icon menu button beside Save (`MultiSelectDropdown` gained an `icon` trigger); the Reload button and its confirm are removed (records change slowly, the version lock catches a stale cell on save, and a page refresh reads the list again).
decisions.rationale: Discard stays as an undo icon: with the browser's unsaved-changes prompt a refresh is a clumsy way to drop many edited cells.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: hideable filter panel, grid editing state and column choice (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Toolbar on the view toggle's row
decisions.statement: `<columns> <discard> <save> | <list> <grid>`.
decisions.rationale: `RecordGrid` takes a `toolbarHost` element and portals its controls (and the divider) into it, because the state they act on lives in the grid while the row belongs to the page; without a host the toolbar stays inside the grid beside the count. A locked value is drawn at the same left offset as the select text in its column.
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) review changes: hideable filter panel, grid editing state and column choice (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: List data and form UX, close-out: Website review
decisions.statement: Phases 7–15 each updated the site as they landed (CSV import and export, personal data, Pain Point scoring grid and type definitions, bundles, overview chart, coloured report cells, field help, list position).
decisions.rationale: Three gaps remained and were closed: the pinned form header and auto-growing long text (`workflows/creating-records.md`) and the collapsible filter panel as a general list behaviour (`core-features/search-filtering-and-view-mode.md`, previously only mentioned on the Pain Point scoring page).
decisions.section: List data and form UX (October 2026) Phase 16: close-out (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Image scan split out of docker-build
decisions.statement: A fixable HIGH CVE in the docs image's `brotli-libs` only surfaced after `frontend`, `backend-tests` and `e2e-tests` (~40 minutes) had passed, because the Trivy scan lived in `docker-build`, which needs them.
decisions.rationale: The image builds, docs smoke test and Trivy scan are now the `image-scan` job with no `needs`; `docker-build` needs it, so nothing vulnerable is pushed. Cost: `docker-build` rebuilds the images to push them (no shared builder cache between jobs).
decisions.section: CI: image scan runs alongside the tests (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Docs and frontend images run apk upgrade
decisions.statement: The finding (the same `brotli-libs` CVE in both nginx-based images) had a released fix in the Alpine repository but not in the pinned nginx base layer; upgrading at build time clears it.
decisions.rationale: Trade-off: builds are less reproducible between base-image rebuilds.
decisions.section: CI: image scan runs alongside the tests (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Engine: restic, several destinations, optional plain bundle
decisions.statement: The user asked for multiple destinations and liked both a restic repository and plain-file copies over scp.
decisions.rationale: Resolved with them to one engine, not two: restic is the only backup path and fans each snapshot out to every configured destination (`restic copy`); a separate optional `bundle` command writes one age-encrypted tar of the latest set for hand-copying with scp or any tool. Two full engines would have doubled the prune/encrypt/verify code and its restore-test cases.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0: decisions and spikes (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Runner: Compose backup profile service plus thin host wrappers
decisions.statement: Network-only, no Docker socket; `scripts/backup.sh` and `restore.sh` keep their names.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0: decisions and spikes (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Destinations: S3-compatible, SFTP, local/NFS path, Azure Blob
decisions.statement: "scp" is served by the SFTP backend (same SSH, nothing extra on the target) and by the bundle command.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0: decisions and spikes (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Security posture: both controls approved
decisions.statement: `BACKUP_SECRETS_MODE=config|none` and the CLI `--force-reset` with single-use reset links, a credential epoch and a generic emailed forgot-password flow (Phase 3b).
decisions.rationale: This adds a flow to core authentication: the access control and encryption policies are consulted, and the identify, verify, remediate review is recorded when it is built.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0: decisions and spikes (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Stats as one pydantic document, in services/dr_stats.py with a thin CLI
decisions.statement: The plan named `backend/scripts/dr_stats.py`; the logic lives in a service so tests import it, and the script only wires arguments (`--snapshot`, `--compare`, `--no-storage-probe`, `--manifest-schema`).
decisions.rationale: The document has no timestamp or host, so two documents of the same data are equal; volatile identity is the manifest's.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 1: manifest format and `dr_stats` (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Counted from the catalogue and the registry, never from a list
decisions.statement: Table counts come from `information_schema`; records per type come from each type's registered search provider (table, id column, standing conditions); encrypted columns are found by walking `Base.metadata` for `EncryptedString`.
decisions.rationale: A module adds nothing here. A registered type without a search provider is named in `uncounted_types` instead of dropped (none today; a test asserts the list is empty so a new gap is noticed).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 1: manifest format and `dr_stats` (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery: Snapshot-exact counts
decisions.statement: `collect_stats` runs in one `REPEATABLE READ` transaction and can join the snapshot a `pg_dump --snapshot` exported (`SET TRANSACTION SNAPSHOT`); the id is validated against the Postgres snapshot-id shape before it reaches SQL because the statement takes no bind parameter.
decisions.rationale: Tested: a row committed after the snapshot is absent from the pinned view and present live.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 1: manifest format and `dr_stats` (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Probes tell "wrong key" from "no secret"
decisions.statement: `EncryptedString` hides a failed decrypt as `None`; the probe reads the raw ciphertext and uses the new `decrypts_with_current_key`, so a restore with the wrong `APP_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` fails verification instead of looking like unconfigured SMTP/OIDC/2FA.
decisions.rationale: The file probe needed `exists(key)` on the storage backends (a `HEAD` for S3, `is_file` for local; S3 treats only 404 as absent so a denied or unreachable store fails the run rather than reporting files missing).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 1: manifest format and `dr_stats` (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery: Comparison rules
decisions.statement: Alembic revision, every table count and every business statistic must match exactly; probes are not compared but judged on their own (`probe_failures`), because they describe the target's health.
decisions.rationale: A table on one side only is a mismatch.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 1: manifest format and `dr_stats` (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: The tool is Python in the backend codebase, run in a backup image stage
decisions.statement: `app/services/dr_backup.py` (orchestration), `dr_restic.py`, `dr_object_mirror.py` and the thin `scripts/dr_backup.py`; `backend/Dockerfile` gains a `backup` target (application image plus `pg_dump` 16 from the PostgreSQL repository, restic, age, ssh) and keeps `backend` as the last, default stage, so every existing build is unchanged.
decisions.rationale: It reuses `collect_stats` directly, so backup and verify share one definition of "the same". `pg_dump` 16 is pinned because Debian ships 17, whose dumps contain `SET transaction_timeout`, which a 16 server rejects.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Mirror deletion rule simplified from the plan
decisions.statement: The plan pruned mirror objects only when no retained manifest listed them.
decisions.rationale: Because each restic snapshot captures the mirror as it was, an object only has to survive in the mirror through the one run whose dump may still reference it (deleted after the dump, before the sync). The sync flags an object that left the store as missing, keeps it for that run's snapshot, and drops it at the start of the next run. No per-set key lists are needed. A deleted record's attachment therefore stays in backups until retention rotates those sets out, which the retention policy already states.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, backup tool: Failure semantics
decisions.statement: Any failure before the snapshot exists aborts the run.
decisions.rationale: A destination that fails afterwards is recorded per destination and still makes the run exit 1, because a silently missing off-site copy is the failure mode this exists to prevent. A failed run never overwrites the last-success time (carried forward in `status.json` and the metric). A refused concurrent run exits 75 and does not touch `status.json`. A hung restic command (a dead remote is retried for many minutes) times out per command, and the existence probe has its own short limit.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Status.json and the metrics hold no secret, row value or storage key
decisions.statement: Errors pass a redactor (URL credentials and every known secret value); an unexpected exception is recorded by class name only; an unsafe object key is named by a 12-hex digest.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Backup secrets handling is set by BACKUP_SECRETS_MODE
decisions.statement: `none` never opens the `.env`; `config` refuses to run without a mounted `.env` and an age recipient, so a set never silently lacks the key material it advertises.
decisions.rationale: The `.env` is encrypted to an age *public* key, so the backup host cannot decrypt it. The encrypted-column probe needs `APP_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY`; `collect_stats(probe_encryption=False)` leaves it empty when the key is withheld (`BACKUP_PROBE_ENCRYPTION_KEY=`), because a placeholder key would report every secret undecryptable.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Scripts/dr-backup.sh, not a rewrite of scripts/backup.sh
decisions.statement: The plan replaced `backup.sh` in this phase.
decisions.rationale: Doing so would leave backups that no shipped tool can restore until the restore tool exists, so the new wrapper has its own name and `backup.sh`/`restore.sh` keep working until the restore tool replaces both together.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 2: backup tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Restore into a scratch database, verify, then rename into place
decisions.statement: The plan dropped and recreated the database after a pre-restore safety dump.
decisions.rationale: The tool instead restores the set into `<name>_restore_<set>` in one `pg_restore --single-transaction --exit-on-error` transaction, recomputes `dr_stats` on it, compares with the manifest, and only then renames it over the live name. A failed restore, a failed verification or a crash therefore leaves the live database exactly as it was, with no window in which it is empty. In place, the replaced database is kept as `<name>_pre_restore_<UTC time>` (rollback is a rename; it still holds all the old data, so the runbook says to drop it once not needed); on a fresh host the verified-empty database is dropped. This removes the unencrypted safety dump file the plan would have left on the staging volume.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Restore needs the image the set was taken with
decisions.statement: The statistics are computed by the application's own models, which cannot read a database at another schema revision, so verification only works when the image's Alembic head equals the set's.
decisions.rationale: A newer or older revision is refused with the image tag to use (the `backup` service now passes `IMAGE_TAG` so the manifest records it); the operator restores with that image and upgrades afterwards, the newer image migrating on start. Restoring an old set directly into a newer image would have meant skipping verification, which is the property the plan exists for. Also refused: a dump from a newer PostgreSQL major than the target, a `STORAGE_BACKEND` that differs from the set's, too little free space on the staging volume, a non-empty target for `fresh`, and `in-place` without `--yes`.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Objects go back before the swap, additively
decisions.statement: Every mirrored object is put under its key and its stored size checked; nothing is deleted, so a failed run cannot lose an attachment and a retry is safe.
decisions.rationale: Objects the set does not know stay in the store as orphans. The set is fetched with `restic restore --verify` and each component is checked against the manifest's SHA-256 before anything is changed; the object mirror is checked by count (it can hold more than the manifest's live count: objects kept one run after deletion).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Unreadable secrets: fail by default, clear on request
decisions.statement: The encrypted-column probe runs on the scratch database; a value the configured key cannot decrypt fails the restore and names the columns.
decisions.rationale: `--clear-unreadable-secrets` removes exactly those values on the scratch database before the swap (a user whose TOTP secret goes is also marked not enrolled, via a small column-dependency table) and writes one `restore`/`secrets_cleared` audit event with counts per column and the `cli:<os user>` actor. It is refused without a key to judge by, because with no key every secret would look unreadable and be wiped.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Config command and the wrapper
decisions.statement: A fresh host has no `.env`, and Compose will not even parse the file without one, so `scripts/restore.sh config` runs the image with plain `docker run` as the caller's uid and writes the decrypted `.env` to stdout redirected into a 0600 file; it refuses an existing file.
decisions.rationale: `restore.sh` otherwise runs the new `restore` Compose service (the backup image with the restore entrypoint, local files writable). For `in-place --yes` the wrapper runs a dry run first and stops the application only if that passes, so a refused restore does not take the application down. `restore.sh FILE` still restores legacy `backup.sh` files, now in one transaction with `ON_ERROR_STOP`, fixing the previous script's half-restore behaviour.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Scratch mode and --force-reset are not in this phase
decisions.statement: The tool is target-agnostic: pointed at an isolated Compose project's `DATABASE_URL` and storage, `fresh` is the scratch restore; the orchestration (own project, ports, email sink, `EMAIL_DELIVERY=disabled`, teardown) is the restore-test harness of the next phase.
decisions.rationale: The `--force-reset` hook the plan listed here has nothing to call until the credential-reset CLI exists, so it is left to that phase rather than shipping a flag that does nothing; the runbook says so.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3: restore tool (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: A host-side Python orchestrator driving an isolated Compose project
decisions.statement: `scripts/restore_test.py` (stdlib only, Python 3.9+, wrapped by `scripts/restore-test.sh`) must drive `docker compose`, and the backup and restore tools deliberately have no Docker socket, so the orchestration lives on the host while everything that needs the application's code runs inside the scratch containers (`backend/scripts/dr_verify.py`, `app/services/dr_verify.py`).
decisions.rationale: The logic is Python, not Bash, because fault injection, report building and redaction are logic.
