decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 4: restore-test harness and CI (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: The scratch project cannot touch or reach the real deployment
decisions.statement: `docker-compose.restore-test.yml` (override) removes published ports and the fixed storage container name, sets `EMAIL_DELIVERY=disabled`, turns the bootstrap server administrator off (it would add a user the backup does not hold, so statistics could never match) and gives the backend a patient health check.
decisions.rationale: Credentials are generated per run into a 0700 directory removed at the end; of the operator's environment only `PASSTHROUGH_KEYS` (the encryption key, image settings, off-site credentials) is used, and a test pins that a production database password, JWT secret, admin password and SMTP password are never copied. The repository is mounted read-only through a generated override (an external volume for a named repository, a bind for a path) and restic read commands run `--no-lock` there (`BACKUP_REPOSITORY_READ_ONLY`), so a defect in a test cannot alter the backups it reads.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 4: restore-test harness and CI (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: The restore may add exactly one audit row
decisions.statement: Found by the first real run of the recovery-without-key case: `--clear-unreadable-secrets` writes one audit event, so `audit_events` is one above the manifest.
decisions.rationale: `dr_verify --extra-rows audit_events=1` allows exactly that and only when the restore reported cleared secrets; one more or one fewer still fails (tested).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 4: restore-test harness and CI (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Fault injection proves the checks bite
decisions.statement: `--inject delete-row|delete-object|wrong-key|corrupt-dump` damages the restored copy (a leaf-table row, an object, the key, a pack of a repository copy) and the exit status means "the fault was caught by the check that exists for it".
decisions.rationale: A fault that could not be applied, or that was caught for another reason, fails the self-test. A wrong key must be reported with exactly the encrypted columns that hold values and their counts (compared with the manifest). Found by running it: the first damaged-repository copy was root-owned, so restic failed with "permission denied" and the test passed without testing damage; the copy now belongs to the tools' user and an access failure is never accepted as detection (tested).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 4: restore-test harness and CI (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery: Self-check script and CI
decisions.statement: `scripts/restore-test-selfcheck.sh` builds a source stack, seeds the end-to-end dataset, adds an encrypted value (the seeded data holds none, so a wrong-key test would otherwise prove nothing), takes a real backup and runs the positive case, recovery without the key and the four faults, then checks no scratch volume or container remains.
decisions.rationale: CI runs it as the `restore-test` job with no `needs`, and `docker-build` needs it, so a backup that cannot be restored is never published (pinned in `test_ci_gates.py`). The unit suites (`test_dr_verify.py`, `test_restore_test_harness.py`) run in the backup-image step with `scripts/` mounted.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 4: restore-test harness and CI (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: One service, four entry points
decisions.statement: The user approved the CLI, the emailed reset link and the credential epoch in the Q7 sign-off, then asked on 2026-10-24 that the tools be documented as ordinary user management, and that organisation admins and server admins can send password resets for users.
decisions.rationale: `services/credential_reset.py` is the only place a password is reset without the old one; the signed-out "forgot password" flow, an organisation or server admin sending a link, a server admin's forced reset and `python -m app.cli.credentials` all call it. The operator page is `docs/website/docs/workflows/password-reset-and-credential-recovery.md`, written for people managing users, with the disaster-recovery runbook linking to it rather than owning it.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: The credential epoch is users.token_version
decisions.statement: Every reset increments it, so every earlier session already fails `deps._resolve_user_from_token` and the WebSocket re-check; no second mechanism.
decisions.rationale: The new column is `users.must_reset_credentials` and the new table `credential_reset_tokens` (migration 0106).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: The link is a bearer secret, treated as one
decisions.statement: A 256-bit `secrets.token_urlsafe` value; only its SHA-256 is stored (as PATs are); it travels in the URL **fragment** (`/reset-password#token=...`), which browsers never send, so it stays out of the frontend's access logs and referrers, and the page removes it from the address bar on load.
decisions.rationale: Redemption is one `UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL AND expires_at > now RETURNING`, so two simultaneous uses cannot both win; it then spends every other outstanding link. Default lifetime 60 minutes (`CREDENTIAL_RESET_TOKEN_MINUTES`, 5 to 1440); the CLI may ask for up to 1440.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: An administrator never sees the link
decisions.statement: A link sent by an organisation or server admin goes to the account's own address and nothing else; returning or displaying it would let an administrator choose a password for someone else's account, which is exactly the takeover this feature must not be.
decisions.rationale: Only the CLI prints a link, to the operator's terminal alone (standard output; counts and warnings go to standard error), because its authority is shell and database access to the deployment, not an application login.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: A reset is not a sign-in and does not touch 2FA
decisions.statement: Choosing a new password proves control of the mailbox, not possession of the second factor, so the person signs in afterwards and is asked for their code.
decisions.rationale: Clearing 2FA is a separate, explicit choice of the forced reset (`--reset-2fa`). An ordinary reset does not revoke personal access tokens (consistent with change-password, which deliberately does not); a forced reset does.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, credential reset: Who may do what
decisions.statement: Sending a link: an organisation admin for a member of their organisation (404 otherwise, like every org-scoped account action), a server admin for any account.
decisions.rationale: Forced reset: server admin only. An organisation admin was not given a forced reset for "my organisation" because a person can belong to several organisations and the action would end their sessions and require a new password everywhere; the single-person link is the safe equivalent. Revisit if organisation admins ask for it.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, credential reset: Forced-reset semantics
decisions.statement: Every account in scope has its sessions ended; every account holding a local password is marked `must_reset_credentials` and refused native sign-in even with the correct password (HTTP 403 with a distinct message, only after the password is right, so it cannot be used to enumerate accounts; a pending 2FA challenge issued before the reset is also refused); personal access tokens are revoked…
decisions.rationale: outstanding links are spent; deactivated and archived accounts are included, because reactivating one must not restore a suspect credential. SSO accounts are listed in the CLI output and counted in the API result, never silently skipped, and have their sessions ended. SCIM tokens, `JWT_SECRET` and `APP_SECRET_ENCRYPTION_KEY` are not rotated by it; the runbook and the incident plan say so.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, credential reset: The command line
decisions.statement: `python -m app.cli.credentials force-reset|issue-link` with scopes `--all`, `--org <code|id>`, `--user`, `--server-admins`; `force-reset` shows its scope and changes nothing without `--yes`.
decisions.rationale: It needs only `DATABASE_URL`, so it works with the application down, email down and every administrator locked out. The audit actor is `cli:<os user>` in the event detail (`actor_id` is a foreign key to users, so it is null), as the restore tool's secret-clearing event already does.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, credential reset: Restore integration
decisions.statement: `restore.sh ... --force-reset [all|server_admins] [--reset-2fa]` applies the reset to the scratch database after verification and before the swap, so the live database is only ever replaced by an already-reset copy.
decisions.rationale: It sends no email (a restored host may have none); the runbook has the operator print links afterwards.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, credential reset: Restore-test cases
decisions.statement: The plan listed "forced reset" and "CLI reset with the administrators locked out" as two cases.
decisions.rationale: A forced reset of everyone *is* the lockout, so one run (`--force-reset all --reset-2fa`) proves both: a new `credential-recovery` check requires every local account marked, a pre-reset session dead, the real command line to print a link for a server administrator, that link to set a password exactly once, and the new password to sign in. It replaces the `login` check for that run (restored passwords are unusable by design). A new fault, `unmarked-account` (clear one marker after the restore), must be caught by that check, so it cannot pass vacuously. The restore may add one audit event for the reset, allowed in the statistics comparison as the secrets-clearing event already is.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 3b: credential reset (2026-10-24)

decisions.title: Three ways to schedule, one set of tools
decisions.statement: A Compose `backup-scheduler` service (backup only), systemd timers and cron (backup and restore-test).
decisions.rationale: They call the same entry points (`dr_backup.py run`, `dr-scheduled.sh`), so status files and metrics are identical whichever is used; the runbook says to pick one. The restore-test is **host-only** because it drives `docker compose` and the backup image deliberately has no Docker socket; giving the scheduler container the socket to run it would undo that isolation.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: The in-container schedule is a small loop, not cron
decisions.statement: `services/dr_schedule.py`: `BACKUP_SCHEDULE` is `HH:MM` (daily) or `every Nh` (N divides 24, aligned to UTC midnight).
decisions.rationale: A daily time is a *future scheduled wall-clock time*, so it is stored as local time plus an IANA zone (`BACKUP_SCHEDULE_TIMEZONE`) and resolved to UTC only when the next wait is computed (Time and Dates rule: shape 2); a skipped local time runs an hour later that day, a repeated one runs once at its first occurrence. Tested at UTC+10 (09:00), UTC-8 (23:00), a week either side of the Sydney daylight-saving change, the nonexistent and the repeated 02:30, and the 25-hour day. A full cron grammar was not built: nobody needs more than daily or every few hours here, and a cron parser is the thing most likely to be wrong. It **catches up once at start** when no success followed the last slot (a container that was down at 02:30 does not wait a day), **retries a failed run once** after 30 minutes (never past the next slot; `BACKUP_SCHEDULE_RETRIES`, `_RETRY_MINUTES`), and a heartbeat thread (separate from the run, which can take hours) writes `reqtrack-backup-scheduler.prom` every 30 seconds and on every state change, under a lock so a slow beat cannot overwrite a newer state; the container health probe reads its age.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Staleness thresholds follow published intervals
decisions.statement: The plan said "backup older than 1.5x interval" but a Prometheus rule cannot know the interval.
decisions.rationale: Each tool publishes it (`reqtrack_backup_expected_interval_seconds`, from `BACKUP_EXPECTED_INTERVAL_HOURS`, derived from the schedule by the scheduler; `reqtrack_restore_test_expected_interval_seconds`, `--expected-interval-hours`, default 168) and the rules compute from it: backup stale at 1.5x, restore-test stale at the interval plus a day (8 days when weekly, as the plan states). Changing a schedule therefore needs no rule edit, and a cron user who backs up every 6 hours sets one variable. An empty `BACKUP_EXPECTED_INTERVAL_HOURS` (what Compose passes when unset) means the default, with a test.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Metrics reach Prometheus through Alloy's textfile collector
decisions.statement: `prometheus.exporter.unix` with only the `textfile` collector, a relabel to `job="reqtrack-backup"`, and `prometheus.remote_write` to Prometheus, which gains `--web.enable-remote-write-receiver`.
decisions.rationale: Chosen over adding `node-exporter` because Alloy is already the project's documented shipper and this adds no service. Verified on real containers: Alloy read textfiles written by the real writers and Prometheus held the series, evaluated the rules (alerts reached `pending` on real data) and loaded them from `observability/alerts/`. The bundled stack still has no Alertmanager; alerts show in Prometheus and Grafana and the runbook says how to add one.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Disaster recovery, scheduling and monitoring: One status directory
decisions.statement: `BACKUP_STATUS_VOLUME` (default the named volume; may be an absolute host path) is mounted by the backup, the scheduler and Alloy; the host restore-test writes to the same directory with `--status-dir`.
decisions.rationale: `dr-scheduled.sh` requires an absolute host path for the restore-test so its metrics land where Alloy reads, and refuses with a message otherwise. Both tools now write their files with a temp file and rename (the restore-test used `write_text`, which a scraper could read half-written).
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Dr-scheduled.sh reads, never executes, its settings file
decisions.statement: `/etc/reqtrack/dr.env` is parsed line by line (`KEY=value`, one pair of surrounding quotes stripped), not sourced, because a sourced file is code run as the job's user.
decisions.rationale: A test puts `$(...)`, backticks and `; touch` in a value and asserts nothing runs. The same file works as a systemd `EnvironmentFile`. Exit 75 (another run active) is a success for systemd.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Alert rules are tested twice
decisions.statement: `promtool test rules` unit tests for every alert (a failed backup, staleness at 1.5x for two intervals, a destination down naming itself, missing metrics, a silent scheduler, a restore-test one day inside and outside the window, a failed restore-test, an unreadable file) run in CI beside the backup-image tests; and a pytest cross-check fails if a rule reads a `reqtrack_*` metric no tool emits, if…
decisions.rationale: an alert lacks `for`, a severity or a unit test (it caught a missing one while writing it). The cross-check is what stops the tools and rules drifting apart, which a syntax check cannot.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 5: scheduling and monitoring (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: The mirror is sound against real SeaweedFS 3.97
decisions.statement: Run on a throwaway SeaweedFS with the real `ObjectMirror`: a bucket of 2,124 keys across nested prefixes (one of 6 MB) lists in full through the paginator (past the 1,000-key page); the ETag of a single put equals the object's MD5, including the 6 MB one; a same-size, different-content overwrite changes the ETag and is re-fetched (the digest changes); an unchanged second sync downloads nothing; a…
decisions.rationale: deleted key is flagged missing, kept for that run and removed on the next. No code change was needed for any of it.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0, spike B closed: object-store mirror and a read-only identity (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: SeaweedFS 3.97 cannot express a read-only identity
decisions.statement: The first spike saw a `Read`+`List` identity denied everything and left "other action forms" to try.
decisions.rationale: Tried now, each on its own identity, with and without a shared `account` (to rule out bucket ownership): `Read:bucket`+`List:bucket`; global `Read`+`List`; `Read:bucket/*`+`List:bucket/*`; both forms together. All were denied for list, get, head and put (so authentication worked; authorisation refused). The pattern: an identity is refused **every** operation on a bucket unless it holds `Write:<bucket>` (or Admin): `Read`+`Write` can get but not list, `Write`+`List` can list but not get, `Read`+`List`+`Tagging` or `+Write:<other bucket>` or `+Write:<bucket>/<prefix>/*` is denied outright. So any identity that can read the bucket can also write it. Two further attempts on a second throwaway container (2026-10-25) changed nothing: a bucket created through `weed shell` (so it has no S3 owner) and identities stored in the filer with `s3.configure` instead of a config file both gave the same denials, which rules out bucket ownership and the config-file path. A different mechanism (SeaweedFS's token-based advanced IAM, `-iam.config`) was not pursued: it is a larger change to the bundled storage than this goal justifies, and the image is pinned deliberately. Re-test on a SeaweedFS upgrade.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 0, spike B closed: object-store mirror and a read-only identity (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: The runbook is one page, the website page is a summary that links to it
decisions.statement: `docs/disaster-recovery.md` gained the missing operator material: an at-a-glance table (RPO, RTO, proof, what is not covered), a "which situation" table and flowchart, key custody, and a troubleshooting table.
decisions.rationale: The new website page `installation-deployment/backup-and-disaster-recovery.md` carries the same shape in less detail and points at the runbook for every setting, so there is one place to keep current. `deployment.md`, the website storage page and the production-deployment upgrade step now name `dr-backup.sh` first and call `backup.sh` a one-off dump that does not cover SeaweedFS objects or the `.env`; the old text recommended it for upgrades, which would have lost attachments on the default storage backend.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 6: runbook, docs website, SOC 2 and architecture docs (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: RTO is stated as unmeasured
decisions.statement: A recovery time needs a clean-machine run, which has not happened.
decisions.rationale: The runbook, README limitations and SOC 2 mapping say so, and name the restore-test's recorded duration as an upper bound until then, rather than inventing a figure.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 6: runbook, docs website, SOC 2 and architecture docs (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Erasure does not reach existing backups
decisions.statement: Retention applies to every repository, so a record hard-deleted in the application (an organisation, a Stakeholder, an Engagement) stays in older sets until they expire (up to about a year at the default 12 monthly sets), and restoring an old set brings it back.
decisions.rationale: The retention policy now says so (Implementation and Known Gap 2, replacing the gap about rotation, which the tool closed) and tells the Company to state the window to customers and to re-apply erasures after restoring an old set. Rewriting immutable encrypted snapshots to purge one record would defeat their integrity guarantee, so no per-record purge is planned.
decisions.section: Disaster recovery Phase 6: runbook, docs website, SOC 2 and architecture docs (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Every production image is published for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64
decisions.statement: The matrix is five images, not the three the plan assumed: `backend`, `backup`, `frontend`, `mcp-server` and `docs`, the same set `docker-compose.yml` pulls.
decisions.rationale: A test fails if compose pulls an image the matrix does not build.
decisions.section: Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) production images in CI (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Native runners, not QEMU
decisions.statement: `ubuntu-latest` for amd64 and `ubuntu-24.04-arm` for arm64 (free for this public repository).
decisions.rationale: Emulated arm builds of the pip and npm layers run several times slower and would threaten the job timeout. GitVersion moved to a separate `version` job so no leg installs it.
decisions.section: Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) production images in CI (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Push by digest, tag once
decisions.statement: Legs push untagged digests; `docker-publish` runs only on `main` after every leg passed, builds the manifest list with the SemVer, SHA and `latest` tags and fails if either platform is missing.
decisions.rationale: A broken arm image therefore never receives a tag. An orphan untagged digest can remain after a partly failed run; it is unreachable by any tag and accepted.
decisions.section: Multi-arch (amd64 + arm64) production images in CI (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: CAdvisor in the observability profile only
decisions.statement: Read-only mounts of `/sys`, `/var/lib/docker` and the Docker socket, `docker_only`, no published port (Prometheus reaches it on the compose network), not privileged.
decisions.rationale: The socket mount is needed because without it cAdvisor cannot read container labels and every series is an anonymous cgroup path (verified on Docker Desktop: the plan's `/var/run` mount did not expose the socket). OOM kills need `/dev/kmsg` and the single `SYSLOG` capability (without it the read is refused and `container_oom_events_total` is absent). Recorded as a Known Gap in the system-operations policy, with the compensating controls pinned by `backend/tests/test_resource_dashboard.py`.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 1: container-level metrics (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Per-worker RSS and pool gauges come from the app, not psutil
decisions.statement: `/proc/self/statm` needs no dependency; `getrusage` is the non-Linux fallback.
decisions.rationale: `liveall` gauges give each worker a `pid` label; each worker (not only the leader) refreshes its own every 5 s. `prometheus_client` never drops a dead worker's `live*` file, so `/metrics` removes files of pids that no longer exist before it aggregates (otherwise a restarted worker leaves a frozen series).
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 1: container-level metrics (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Series are keyed by compose service and project
decisions.statement: cAdvisor lists every container the daemon runs, so the scrape keeps only compose containers and labels them `service` and `compose_project`; the dashboard legend is `project/service` so a second stack on the host cannot be summed into the first.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 1: container-level metrics (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Grafana now provisions Prometheus and one dashboard
decisions.statement: `observability/grafana/`; Loki and Tempo remain manual.
decisions.rationale: Docs that said "nothing provisioned" were updated (README, deployment guide, website, policy).
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 1: container-level metrics (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: T0 is generated, not the e2e seed
decisions.statement: `seed_e2e_dataset.py` needs fixed credentials and ordering the throwaway stack does not have; T0 is 30 requirements from the same generator, so every tier is on one data model.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 2: dataset tiers, load generator and portable runner (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Skeleton by API, records by bulk insert
decisions.statement: Organisation creation seeds link types, roles and module state through hooks a hand-written insert would miss; only the high-volume records are bulk-inserted.
decisions.rationale: Drift is guarded by a parity test (every column the API create path populates is populated by the generator, for requirements, versions, comments, links, actions, tags and audit events). Zipf exponent 0.6 for link endpoints: 1.1 gave one requirement about 13% of all endpoints, 0.6 gives hubs of hundreds at 20,000.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 2: dataset tiers, load generator and portable runner (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: No published ports at all, perf-only image names, scrubbed Docker environment
decisions.statement: The plan said loopback on ephemeral ports; nothing needs a host port (the load generator is in the project, the runner execs), so none is published.
decisions.rationale: Perf images are `reqtrack-perf-*` so a build can never retag a production `latest`. Docker runs with an allowlisted environment so an exported `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `COMPOSE_FILE` cannot leak in or redirect it, and `lib/compose.py` refuses prune, `--rmi` and any removal naming a resource outside `reqtrack-perf-*`.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 2: dataset tiers, load generator and portable runner (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Backend memory is sized from the worker count
decisions.statement: With four workers the backend sat at its whole 1.69 GiB cap for every scenario at T0 and Docker flagged an OOM kill.
decisions.rationale: The cap is now the budget minus the other services' floors, and a budget under 0.5 GiB per worker plus 0.5 GiB is refused (about 4.05 GiB for four workers). On Docker Desktop the default budget is half the VM and free memory is measured VM-wide, because every container shares it. On this Mac, beside the development stack, a 3.2 GiB budget therefore gets two workers.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 2: dataset tiers, load generator and portable runner (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Workers auto is the runner default
decisions.statement: It picks the most the CPU and memory budget supports, at most 4 (the production default, so a larger host is not profiled at a count the default deployment does not use), at 0.5 GiB per worker plus 0.5 GiB for the parent, and refuses a budget that cannot run one.
decisions.rationale: The count and `workers_auto` go in `run.json`, and a full run with an automatic count carries a note that it is not comparable with another count. The same selection for the real backend entrypoint is deliberately not done yet: the per-worker cost and the worker model are what the in-process profiling work measures.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 2: dataset tiers, load generator and portable runner (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: EXPLAIN (GENERIC_PLAN), not EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)
decisions.statement: A stored statement has no parameter values, so `ANALYZE` cannot run it; `GENERIC_PLAN` plans it with `$n` placeholders, executes nothing and keeps no literal.
decisions.rationale: It shows the planner's choice and estimates, not actual time; actual time per statement is in `pgstat.csv`. An `ANALYZE` of a flagged statement is a manual step with real parameters on a kept stack (documented; output is not committed).
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4: PostgreSQL profiling (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Resource profiling, PostgreSQL profiling: Only DML is kept
decisions.statement: `pg_stat_statements` replaces constants in `select/insert/update/delete`, but a utility statement (`SET`, `CREATE ROLE ...
decisions.rationale: PASSWORD`) keeps its literals, and results are committed to a public repository. `pg_stat_activity` is read for counts only. `::type` casts are dropped from kept text (they read as IPv6 addresses to the anonymisation check). The runner runs `ANALYZE` after the dataset loads (it stands in for the autovacuum a real database would get), otherwise `plans.csv` describes an empty database.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4: PostgreSQL profiling (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Pool is configurable: DB_POOL_SIZE (5) and DB_MAX_OVERFLOW (10)
decisions.statement: The pool was SQLAlchemy's default, fixed in code, so a small host could not lower the connection budget the plan asked to document.
decisions.rationale: Defaults are unchanged. A worker holds at most `pool + overflow + 2` connections (the `LISTEN` listener and the leadership lock are outside the pool): 17 by default, 68 for four workers against 97 usable under `max_connections=100`; a test pins that the defaults fit. README, configuration reference, deployment guide and the website scaling page now state the formula.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4: PostgreSQL profiling (2026-10-25)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: How results travel
decisions.statement: A run prints the path of its anonymised `.tar.gz` (`~/.cache/reqtrack-perf/`); copy it between machines and extract it under `perf/results/<label>/`.
decisions.rationale: `analyse.py` and the repository's scrub test read whatever is there. Bundles committed before this change remain in git history; they passed the anonymisation check, and the history was not rewritten.
decisions.section: Resource profiling: results are not kept in the repository (2026-10-26)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: Audit trail indexes
decisions.statement: After the count change the capacity ceiling stayed at about 250 requests per second with the database at its cap.
decisions.rationale: The next largest cost after the list page was the activity timeline's three sequential scans of `audit_events`, a table with no index besides its key that gains a row with every write, so migration 0108 adds `(entity_type, entity_id)` and `(project_id, entity_type, created_at)`. Cost: two more index entries per audit insert. The list page's own plan (a scan of the current versions) is an experiment, not a change (O12).
decisions.section: Resource profiling: the project lock no longer blocks foreign-key checks (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Tested before proposing an index
decisions.statement: On a replica of the T3 data in a scratch database, a partial index on current versions changed neither the plan (a scan of all 50,000 current versions) nor the time (45 ms): the default order needs every row of the project for each page.
decisions.rationale: The cost is linear in project size by construction. Not added.
decisions.section: Resource profiling: the T3 capacity climb and the database memory settings (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: New runner options
decisions.statement: `--pg-shared-buffers` and `--pg-work-mem` set the perf stack's database memory settings for a tuning experiment (PostgreSQL's defaults otherwise; refused above half the database's memory cap).
decisions.rationale: They exist so the setting is chosen on evidence (O4, O10, O13), not advised from a guess.
decisions.section: Resource profiling: the T3 capacity climb and the database memory settings (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: A registry hook, not a central test table
decisions.statement: `ModuleDefinition.scaling_probes` / `no_scaling_probe` (core types in `services/scaling_probes_core.py`) follow the `perf_generators` convention, so a new module cannot skip the guard and no core file names a module's type.
decisions.rationale: A probe creates records through the real create endpoint, so it cannot drift from the application's own path and needs no generator.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the scaling-shape guard (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling, the scaling-shape guard: What it asserts
decisions.statement: Statements for the list, detail, comments and depth-1 link graph at 3 and 9 records are equal; the response may grow (an unpaged list returns every row), the statements may not.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic, so it runs in CI with the rest of the suite.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the scaling-shape guard (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Known growth is a strict list
decisions.statement: `KNOWN_GROWING` names each growing check and its finding (O16 lists, O17 comments in `docs/performance.md`); it fails if a check grows and is unlisted, and if a listed check stops growing, so it can only shrink.
decisions.rationale: The four compliance types are `TRACKED_GAPS` (no probe yet; the same shrinking convention as the generator list).
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the scaling-shape guard (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: Planted hubs
decisions.statement: A Zipf tail alone gave a largest hub of about 60 links at 5,000 requirements, so the most-linked record of every type pair is planted with `hub_max_degree` (1,000) links, capped by the records available to link from.
decisions.rationale: A T3 project has a 1,000-link hub in every pair.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the cross-type link dataset (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: Dormant links
decisions.statement: In a nested profile 2% of cross-type links join a record to a record of a sibling project, which is outside the ancestry; the application treats these as dormant (counted unavailable, never shown), so the graph's unavailable path has data.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the cross-type link dataset (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Records the viewer cannot see
decisions.statement: In a nested profile one member holds no role on the deepest projects, so a parent's link graph omits those records and counts them as hidden for that member (tested).
decisions.rationale: A viewer who lacks a type's view permission rather than a project role is not generated, because the skeleton gives every member the same roles.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the cross-type link dataset (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: Proposed links
decisions.statement: A quarter of the change requests carry one to three proposed links, with the outcome following the request's status.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the cross-type link dataset (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Resource profiling: Compliance probe
decisions.statement: `compliance_evidence` now has a scaling probe (and a strict `KNOWN_GROWING` entry: its list issues a link query per row); the other three compliance types stay tracked gaps because they come from assigning a standard.
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 4c: the scenarios for the other types and the links (2026-10-27)

decisions.title: Compose memory limits are env-tunable and sized for the default install
decisions.statement: Every always-on service in `docker-compose.yml` has a `mem_limit` read from `.env` (`BACKEND_MEM_LIMIT` 5g, `DB_MEM_LIMIT` 2g, `STORAGE_MEM_LIMIT` 1g, `FRONTEND_MEM_LIMIT` 128m, `MCP_MEM_LIMIT` 256m; `0` removes one).
decisions.rationale: Rejected: fixed limits at peak + 40% (the plan's wording), because the backend need spans 4.5 GiB to 11 GiB with project size and would make the stack refuse to start on a small host; and no limits, because a runaway service could then take the host down. **Risk accepted:** the default covers four workers on projects up to about 1,000 requirements only; a deployment with 5,000-requirement projects that does not read the sizing guide can see the backend killed during an export or import. The guide, the website's configuration reference and the README say so, and the backend entrypoint logs a warning at start when its cgroup memory limit is below 1.2 GiB per worker plus 0.1 GiB (pinned by a test that runs the entrypoint against a fake limit file).
decisions.section: Resource profiling Phase 5: memory limits, sizing and the run-to-run diff (2026-10-28)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Page numbers by format
decisions.statement: (): PDF exact; HTML and the preview links only; Word and OpenDocument get a real contents field with every entry written in and linked and **no cached page numbers**, which a person adds by updating the field (Word: right-click, Update field; LibreOffice: Tools, Update).
decisions.rationale: No "update fields?" prompt on opening and no estimated numbers (a wrong number is worse than none). The website says so plainly.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 105: table of contents, spike across the four formats (2026-11-03)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Multi-project run
decisions.statement: (): one contents for the joined report, where the block sits, listing every project's headings.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 105: table of contents, spike across the four formats (2026-11-03)

decisions.title: Custom reports, the table of contents block: Rules (validator)
decisions.statement: One per layout (the second is named, with the first's path); not inside `each`/`group` (it would print once per record: , checked through the validator's scope); not inside an At page bottom block; not in a table layout (it has the Contents sheet).
decisions.rationale: Inside `if` and `section` is allowed. An empty contents (no headings at that depth) prints nothing, not even its title or break.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 106: the table of contents block (2026-11-03)

decisions.title: Header and Footer are two groups
decisions.statement: `LAYOUT_SETTING_GROUPS` replaces `band` with `header` and `footer`; each has its own bar, "1 changed" mark and remembered state (`layoutSettings:header`, `layoutSettings:footer`).
decisions.rationale: Both start closed. The old combined group's remembered state is not carried over In the dialog the band explanation sits inside the Header group.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 108: header and footer separate, Page and Margins collapsible, "Custom" (2026-11-03)

decisions.title: Page and Margins are two collapsible groups
decisions.statement: `page` is size, orientation and mirror; `margins` is the margins and gutter.
decisions.rationale: Their bars show the effective value ("A4 portrait", "A3 landscape, mirrored"; "1.5 cm", or each side when they differ) through `pageGroupSummary` / `marginsGroupSummary`, with the accent edge only when a value is not the default.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 108: header and footer separate, Page and Margins collapsible, "Custom" (2026-11-03)

decisions.title: Nothing selected marks the whole box
decisions.statement: `wrapWholeText` wraps each non-blank line's words, keeping a list bullet, number, heading hash or quote mark and the line's outer spaces outside the mark (so `** a **` is never written, and a bulleted list stays a list); an empty box still gets a `****` pair with the caret inside.
decisions.rationale: This is the shared behaviour, so the header and footer cells changed too: a collapsed caret there used to write an empty pair. A second press on already-marked text marks it again (no toggle off); a toggle would need reading marks back and is not built.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 111: Bold and Italic buttons on heading and text (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: A value and its unit share a row
decisions.statement: `BlockField.inline` (schema, served in the block catalogue) draws a field on the same row as the field before it; `arrangement_problems` fails an inline field that is first or follows a field of another group or an inline field.
decisions.rationale: `ReportLayoutBlockForm` wraps such a pair in `.block-field-row` (a two-column grid that stacks below about 18 rem). Set on `width_unit` and `height_unit` of image, shape and record images; names, stored values and the text view are unchanged. A module block uses it by declaring the flag, with no core edit.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 112: the picture blocks follow the arrangement; a completeness test (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: One shared component
decisions.statement: `ReportFormatDownload` (list, button, blocked reason) is used by `ReportRunner`, so the record list's Download report dialog and the Reports dialog's run view agree.
decisions.rationale: The rule for the starting choice is `utils/reportFormatChoice.ts`.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 113: formats as a radio list, then Download (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Left as menus
decisions.statement: `ReportExportButton` stays where it is a toolbar item with no step to configure: the compliance panels, the requirement report's *More formats* beside *Generate PDF*, and the layout designer's preview panel.
decisions.rationale: The pack runner has one output (a zip) and was already a single button.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 113: formats as a radio list, then Download (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Text colour is automatic when not set
decisions.statement: Unset, `DocumentStyles.table_head_colours` returns black or white by `text_on` against the fill actually used, including when only the fill is set.
decisions.rationale: Only a text colour set: the accent remains the fill. The contrast boundary is pinned by a test on either side of the crossover.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 114: default table heading colours for a layout, model and renderers (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: One control, two places
decisions.statement: `TableHeadingColours` (fill and text colour as two `ColourChoiceField`s, so the layout's scheme names are offered, plus a sample heading row) is drawn by the Blocks view's layout panel in place of the two generic colour fields, and by the Page setup dialog in a new *Look* group, so the two agree.
decisions.rationale: The two fields were already in the block catalogue; `GROUP_OF_FIELD` now places them in *Look* (they had fallen into *Other*), and the group's pill counts each colour set. "No colour" is not offered (the server refuses `none` here); the first line of each list is the reset (*Default (the organisation's accent)*, *Automatic (black or white)*).
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 115: the table heading colours control, demo and docs (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: The sample follows the renderers
decisions.statement: `utils/tableHeadingColours` mirrors `DocumentStyles.table_head_colours` (fill, else the accent; text, else black or white by contrast with the fill actually used) only so the sample and the custom-table editor can show the result before a run; the server stays the judge.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 115: the table heading colours control, demo and docs (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Library as a fourth source
decisions.statement: `source: "report_image"` lists the project's own pictures (`project_id` is the project and the file is not an organisation resource), once each, with no record.
decisions.rationale: Its origin link is the project's *Report setup* page (`/projects/{id}/admin/reportSetup`): the library has no page of its own (it is a dialog in the layout designer), so that is the nearest stable address. A viewer who cannot manage the project sees that page's own refusal; the label states the source in either case. The organisation's library belongs to no project and stays out (, Q5). A confidential picture stays listed for the project's members: the mark only keeps a report from printing it, as the library itself already applies (`models.file`); the download gate is unchanged.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 116: the Files page lists report library pictures, previews them, and can be searched and filtered (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: One service, two reads
decisions.statement: The row building moved from `routers/projects/core.py` to `services/project_files.py` (`project_file_rows`, `FileFilters`), which pushes every filter into the SQL of each source query, so a narrowed list never loads the rest.
decisions.rationale: Nested-project scope is still `ProjectScope.collect` with the endpoint's own `requirement` view gate, over that one function, so a related project's pictures and files carry the same `from_project_*` labels and a stranger project's never appear.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 116: the Files page lists report library pictures, previews them, and can be searched and filtered (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: The file name search is a POST
decisions.statement: `POST /projects/{id}/files/search` carries the filters in its body so the text is in no URL the access log records; the read writes no audit event, logs nothing and uses the text only as a bound `ILIKE` pattern with `%`, `_` and `\` escaped.
decisions.rationale: `GET /files` stays for callers with no filters. The page's own address does hold the typed text (`?q=`), as every list's search does; a reload sends that address to the web server's log. That residue is the same on every list page and is not new here.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 116: the Files page lists report library pictures, previews them, and can be searched and filtered (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: The upload window is two UTC instants
decisions.statement: The plan said a calendar date sent with `X-Client-Date`; that header carries only the person's *today*, from which the server cannot recover the person's UTC offset for another day.
decisions.rationale: The page keeps plain `YYYY-MM-DD` days in the URL (the person's own days) and the browser sends `uploaded_from` (first moment of the first local day, inclusive) and `uploaded_before` (first moment of the day after the last, exclusive) as UTC instants (`localDayWindow`); the API refuses a time without a zone. Time shape: a past instant in UTC, filtered by a window of the person's calendar days. Tested at the boundary hours (23:00 UTC on 3 Nov = 09:00 on 4 Nov at UTC+10; 07:00 UTC on 5 Nov = 23:00 on 4 Nov at UTC-8) and at the exact edge instants.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 116: the Files page lists report library pictures, previews them, and can be searched and filtered (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: No export or import
decisions.statement: The Files page is not a registered artefact type, so the list export/import rule does not apply; a files export would be a new request.
decisions.rationale: The overview's "Files" tile still counts requirement attachments only (its documented scope); it does not count library pictures.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 116: the Files page lists report library pictures, previews them, and can be searched and filtered (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: One serialiser
decisions.statement: `services/report_exchange.py` wraps the project bundle's own entries (`layout_entry`, `pack_entry`, `image_entries`) in a small envelope (`manifest.json`, `reports.json`, `files/<n>_<name>`) and imports through `import_layout_entry` / `import_pack_entry`.
decisions.rationale: A field added to a layout reaches the file with no change; nothing re-implements how a layout is read or written. The file is a first-class format, but the bundles stay the full-fidelity backup.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: One request body, not a GET per layout
decisions.statement: A file holds several layouts and packs, so export is `POST .../report-file/export` with the selection in the body (a long selection never travels in a URL); import is `POST .../report-file/import?dry_run=` (multipart: `file`, `on_conflict`, `folder`), a preview by default.
decisions.rationale: Project and organisation have the same pair. The plan's per-layout `GET` and "multi-select Export" collapse into one endpoint.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Packs bring their layouts
decisions.statement: A pack export includes the layouts it names that the source scope can reach (switch *Include the layouts the packs use*, on by default; names it cannot reach are listed in the manifest as `left_out` and the import warns).
decisions.rationale: Saved sets travel as the source scope sees them (`effective_sets`). Import creates layouts first, renames a taken layout and re-points the pack's entries at the new name; a pack naming a layout neither in the file nor in the target is warned about, not refused.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: No people in the file
decisions.statement: The bundle's `created_by_email` is dropped on export: a file leaves the organisation.
decisions.rationale: The importer is the author; the version comment travels (a current-version-only file notes "Imported from file: <name>, version n").
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: The file is untrusted
decisions.statement: Whole file ≤ 60 MB; ≤ 600 entries; only the names `manifest.json`, `reports.json` and `files/<n>_<name>` (a name is never used as a path; `..`, a leading `/`, a backslash or any other name is refused); ≤ 200 MB uncompressed in total and each entry read with a cap, so a lying header cannot inflate more; a compression-ratio limit for large entries; ≤ 100 layouts, 100 packs, 200 pictures, 200…
decisions.rationale: versions each; format version newer than this installation is refused. Every layout tree is validated again against the target (`check_tree` in the preview; the create path on apply, which also checks pictures). A layout with no valid version is `left_out` with the first problem; nothing partial is stored. Each picture is re-sniffed from its bytes (the declared type is ignored) and an SVG re-sanitised exactly as a library upload is; an EPS or PDF is never converted from a file (an export holds only raster and SVG). A picture that fails is reported and its layout version is dropped like any invalid one.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Pictures are the target's own
decisions.statement: Each picture lands in the target tier's library (a project's for a project import, the organisation's for an organisation import).
decisions.rationale: An organisation picture the importing organisation already owns is reused by reference. A cross-organisation organisation picture imported into a *project* goes into the project's library, never published to the whole organisation as a side effect.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Audit and logs
decisions.statement: One `report_file_exported` and one `report_file_imported` event with counts and keys (layouts, packs, pictures, skipped, history, on_conflict), never layout text or names; the uploaded text is not logged.
decisions.rationale: Test pinned.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Custom reports: Nesting, parity, bundles
decisions.statement: No new project-scoped config table, so no inheritance decision; a child project's import makes the layout its own (shadowing an inherited one of the same name, as the existing rule says).
decisions.rationale: A layout carries no person (the importer is the author), so no group case. No new table or column, so no bundle hook or migration. Not a registered artefact type: no code, search or list export applies. Perf: not a list or heavy path (a file is at most 100 layouts and 100 packs; export reads each layout's versions once); `perf/` is untouched.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 118: export and import layouts and packs as a file (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Fix in the shared code, not at the call site
decisions.statement: `ResultActions` renders the one primary **OK** (plus optional extra controls) and registers the dialog as settled through the dialog slots; `useDialogGuard.isDirty` returns false while a settled marker is mounted, before it looks at `dirty` or the DOM.
decisions.rationale: A new dialog that ends in a result gets the behaviour by using the component. The unfinished steps keep the guard (a story and a Playwright test pin that a chosen file still asks). The Q2 default stands: OK, not Done or Close.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 119: a finished import closes cleanly and ends with OK (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Grouping by tags is one group per tag
decisions.statement: `_Run.group_labels`: a record with two tags is in both groups, an untagged record in `(none)` (last); groups are ordered by tag name.
decisions.rationale: Counts can therefore add up to more than the records, which the help and the website say. Tag names forbid commas, so the joined text splits back safely. No other field is multi-valued.
decisions.section: Custom reports Phase 121: the group's name offered in the editors, one group per tag (2026-11-04)

decisions.title: Product Feedback: Requesters are paged
decisions.statement: The Demand card returned and rendered every requester, so a widely-asked request meant a huge payload and an unbounded table; the Links panel has the same shape (see the limit below).
decisions.rationale: `GET .../demand` now takes `limit` (default 50, 1–500) and `offset`, returns the heaviest-first page with `offset`/`limit`, and keeps `requester_count` and `weighted_demand` over **every** requester (the headline and the scoring never read a page). Only the page's names are looked up. The card loads 25 and shows "Showing N of M requesters" with **Show more**; a channel change or a new requester reloads as many rows as are on screen so a long list never collapses. The MCP tool takes the same `limit`/`offset` and its description says to page on when `requester_count` exceeds what came back. (the User asked whether it coped with more than ten; it did not). - **Known limits, not fixed here:** there is no search within the requesters (a name match would need every party's visibility resolved, or it would reveal that a hidden requester exists), the "Raised in" engagement line and merged-duplicates list are not paged, and the shared Links panel (`ArtefactLinksPanel`) still lists every link, grouped and collapsible, but unpaged: paging it is a change to a shared component used by every record type and is its own piece of work.
decisions.section: Module 14 (Product Feedback): request form review, one-row owner and live scores (2026-11-05)

decisions.title: External references is a sub-component
decisions.statement: (`external_references`, on by default) of the Product Feedback module, so the existing machinery gives what was asked with no new settings code: a project administrator switches it off for the project, and the organisation sets its default for new projects (or turns it off for everyone) on the Modules page.
decisions.rationale: Off hides the feature: the reference routes and the external system lists (project and organisation) answer 404, a create carrying references is refused with 409, and the page leaves out the card, the create form's section and the **External Systems** settings entry. Stored references are kept and return when it is switched back on, and still travel in the bundles. An existing project is unchanged on upgrade (no row means the registry default, on). The inbox follows the organisation's own switch. (disable per project, organisation default); sub-component as the mechanism - **Core extension, generic:** `OrgAdminSectionDef` and `ProjectAdminSectionDef` gained an optional `subComponent`; the two admin pages leave out a section whose sub-component is off, for every module, so no module is special-cased. A shared `useProjectSubComponentEnabled`/`useOrgSubComponentEnabled` reads the generic listing (`useResearchExtras` now uses it too).
decisions.section: Module 14 (Product Feedback): request form review, one-row owner and live scores (2026-11-05)

decisions.title: Section order: project default, personal override
decisions.statement: The request page's sections (Details, External references, Scoring, Demand, Close the loop, Version history, Evidence, Comments) render in an order resolved as: the person's own, else the project's, else built in (`utils/sectionOrder`: the first non-empty layer wins and layers never merge; keys it names come first, the rest follow in built-in order, unknown keys are ignored, so a section added…
decisions.rationale: later still appears). The project default is a nullable JSON column on `project_feedback_settings` set by a project administrator with `PUT .../settings` (partial update; audited with the count only; keys validated for shape and uniqueness, not against the page's list, so the server stays free of UI names) and it **travels in the project bundle**. The personal order is a `ui_preferences` entry, edited from the page's **Arrange sections…** action. The editor is the shared `SectionOrderEditor` (rows with move up/down, as the nav editor does), built generic so another record page can adopt it. The "Ready to deliver?" banner stays on top; it is a prompt, not a section. (project default with a user override); drag-and-drop was not built (move buttons are keyboard-reachable and match the existing reorder lists)
decisions.section: Module 14 (Product Feedback): request form review, one-row owner and live scores (2026-11-05)

decisions.title: Requesters in the edit form
decisions.statement: The edit form's Requested by field only added; it listed no one.
decisions.rationale: The edit form now has a **Requesters** section, closed by default (`CollapsibleSection`, remembered per person), headed "N so far", that lists the requesters the Demand card has loaded (with "merged duplicate" / "via an Engagement" noted, hidden ones as "A requester you can’t view", and "Showing N of M" when more exist) above the field that adds more. Removing a requester is done from the Demand card (the next entry); the edit form's field says so. The create form keeps the plain Requested by field. (list them, collapsible); read-only list
decisions.section: Module 14 (Product Feedback): request form review, one-row owner and live scores (2026-11-05)

decisions.title: One control for the score columns
decisions.statement: The filter panel's "Scores shown" multi-select (a `model` URL parameter) is removed: it duplicated the chooser and chose the same thing.
decisions.rationale: The ticked score columns are the models the list shows; the first ticked is the primary (it drives the Unscored filter and the Score sort), and a hidden model is simply not asked for. Until a person has chosen, the list sends no `scoring_model` and the server's default (the scheme's enabled models) applies, so a first load never repeats; after a choice it sends exactly the ticked models, and Export and the grid follow the same parameter.
decisions.section: Module 14 (Product Feedback): request form review, one-row owner and live scores (2026-11-05)

decisions.title: A set, not a per-level fallback
decisions.statement: (; the User chose per-level thresholds).
decisions.rationale: A set must name every level and rise with the weights, because mixing one level from the project with another from an ancestor could put the thresholds out of order. A set that no longer covers the axis (the organisation added or deleted a level) is dropped by the level writers, so projects fall back to the organisation's values.
decisions.section: Product Feedback: per-project Demand thresholds, requester weight source, formal wording

decisions.title: Scoring is omitted from the Pain Point dialog opened this way
decisions.statement: (): the form offers scoring only to someone who may score and that check belongs to the list page; the Pain Point's own page scores it.
decisions.rationale: This is a deliberate difference from the Pain Points list's create form.
decisions.section: Requests and Pain Points: a column, a filter, and "Create new" in the Links panel

decisions.title: Two-level admin navigation: Modules grouped
decisions.statement: Context & Strategy ("Pain Points"), Product Feedback, Risk Management, Stakeholders ("Personas and Stakeholders").
decisions.rationale: Decisions has one section per tier and stays at one level (: a group of one adds a click and no information). Product Feedback's project settings section, which shared its module's name, is now "Submission policy".
decisions.section: Two-level admin navigation (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Two-level admin navigation: Header does not navigate
decisions.statement: The header only expands and collapses, so the keyboard and screen-reader model is the standard disclosure button; arrow keys move through the rows shown and navigate only on a link.
decisions.section: Two-level admin navigation (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Links panel: Not creatable
decisions.statement: `compliance_requirement`, `project_compliance_requirement` and `compliance_required_action_assessment` are derived from an assigned standard and cannot be authored.
decisions.rationale: They are declared once, on the Compliance module, through a new generic `ModuleDefinition.not_creatable_from_links` (`{type: reason}`, read by `get_not_creatable_from_links_types`), the same shape as `not_importable`. No core file names a module.
decisions.section: Links panel: "Create new" for every creatable type (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: The form is the type's own, with quick links and tags
decisions.statement: Each creator wraps the form modal its list page uses (create and edit share one field group), and the quick-link and tag fields stay in it: the new record may need links beyond the page record, and the panel's own link is made in addition.
decisions.rationale: Shared save step: `hooks/useLinkedRecordSave`. Creators receive `pageRecord` (the record whose panel opened the dialog): a Change Request pre-selects the requirement when that is the page record, and a Finding pre-selects the engagement.
decisions.section: Links panel: "Create new" for every creatable type (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Links panel: Core types
decisions.statement: Requirement, Action and Change Request had their create forms inline in their pages.
decisions.rationale: They are extracted to `RequirementCreateModal`, `ActionFormModal` and `ChangeRequestCreateModal`, and the three pages now use them, so there is one implementation each (, the shared-component rule). Their creators are listed in `modules/coreLinkedRecordCreators.tsx` and loaded on first use. The Actions page's inline create card became the same modal as every other create form (header with Cancel and Create).
decisions.section: Links panel: "Create new" for every creatable type (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Links panel: Permission rule
decisions.statement: A type the person may not create is never offered; the server flag from the previous phase is the only gate.
decisions.rationale: `backend/tests/test_creatable_record_types.py` replays each creatable type's create request (its scaling probe's) as a plain member, a project manager, a stakeholder and the holder of each module role, and requires `can_create` to equal whether the endpoint accepts. **It found one divergence:** the Change Request provider declared no `can_create`, so the panel fell back to the `propose_create` permission while the endpoint admits managers, administrators, stakeholders and, when the project allows it, plain members (36 disagreements). The rule is now one function, `services.change_request_list.may_submit_change_request`, used by the endpoint and the provider; `CAN_SUBMIT_ROLES` moved with it. Every other type already agreed.
decisions.section: Links panel: "Create new" for every creatable type (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Pain Point submission policy: Platform default is restrictive
decisions.statement: The user asked for the default to be on the restrictive side, so a new organisation, and a fresh install, start with Pain Point Managers only; ordinary requests go to Enhancement Requests.
decisions.rationale: **Existing organisations :** migration `0142` writes an explicit organisation default of `members` for every organisation that exists at upgrade and has none, so no one loses "New Pain Point" silently; an administrator moves them to managers-only in one change. A downgrade removes nothing (the rows look like chosen ones). This departs from the broad-creation model the Context & Strategy source overview describes (§6.5), which is now opt-in.
decisions.section: Pain Point submission policy (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Engagement outcomes: create new: A separate server flag
decisions.statement: Outcome links are dedicated (made with their own action), so `link-types` leaves them out and carries no `can_create` for them.
decisions.rationale: `GET .../engagement-outcome-target-types` returns each target type with `can_create` from `creatable_record_types`, the same check as the Links panel and the type's create endpoint. A type whose module is off, or that the caller may not view, is omitted, as the target picker already does. The response carries no label: the registry label ("Pain point") differs from the UI label map, which stays the one source of display text.
decisions.section: Engagement outcomes: create new (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Engagement participants: Create form
decisions.statement: `ParticipantsField` (multi-select with filter) on the full create form only, sent as `stakeholder_ids` and applied in the same request and transaction; the edit form and the compact "Log contact" form do not show it (an edit manages participants from the detail page; the quick add already knows its Stakeholder).
decisions.rationale: Facilitators, covered Personas and audience groups stay on the detail page. (the plan names participants only).
decisions.section: Engagement participants (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Engagement participants: Anonymous participants on create
decisions.statement: `EngagementCreate.anonymous_participants` (label and optional Persona, at most 100) is stored in the same request and transaction as the engagement, with one `anonymous_participant_added` audit event per row (ids only).
decisions.rationale: It is refused with 409 while the Research extras sub-component is off for the project (the existing routes answer 404 there; a field on an always-available endpoint cannot), the Persona must be visible to the project (404) and a blank label is 422, all before anything is written. The form has no separate field: anonymous participants are added from the Participants (+) itself (, 2026-11-07; the field is a (+) beside the caption over a row of removable chips, Stakeholders and anonymous alike, matching the detail page, ), where text typed that matches no Stakeholder is offered as "Add “…” as an anonymous participant" (a generic `addFromFilter` option on `MultiSelectDropdown`), and each anonymous chip carries a Persona select; while the sub-component is off nothing is offered. The "label, not a name" note stays visible because it prevents personal data being recorded. A (+) panel opens to the right of its button (`Popover` `placement="side"`) and a dropdown with a visible trigger opens aligned with, and as wide as, that trigger (`matchAnchor`); both are recorded as rules in the style guide's compact-forms pattern (). The CSV import is unchanged (the column set is the export's), and the MCP `create_engagement` tool takes the field through its schema; the module guidance and tool reference are updated.
decisions.section: Engagement participants (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: One Participants list on the detail page
decisions.statement: The Engagement page's Participants panel (`EngagementParticipantsPanel`) lists Stakeholders and anonymous participants as chips under one heading and one (+): the picker offers the Stakeholders not yet recorded (choosing one adds it at once), and typed text that matches none is added as an anonymous participant while the Research extras are on; an anonymous participant's Persona is chosen in the…
decisions.rationale: create and edit forms, not on the page, so every chip on the page reads alike (, 2026-11-07). The edit form shows the create form's `ParticipantsField` filled with the recorded participants (a late arrival, a Persona learned later); `engagementParticipantEdits` compares the result with what was recorded and calls the existing add, remove and `PATCH` endpoints one at a time (: no new endpoint, so audit events and the extras gate are unchanged). The content update is saved first; if a participant call then fails, the form stays open with the error and compares the next attempt with what is recorded then. A Stakeholder hidden from the project is not shown in the field and is left untouched. When the participants cannot be read the edit form omits the field rather than risk emptying the list. Removal of either kind keeps its tier-1 confirm. The separate Anonymous participants panel is removed. Personas covered reads a new read-only `GET /engagements/{id}/personas-reached`: the recorded covered Personas plus those a Stakeholder participant represents and, with the extras on, those an anonymous participant represents, hidden Personas left out. Only recorded ones carry a `link_id` and can be removed; the derived ones are marked "via a participant" and are not stored. Display only was (nothing in the request said the derived Personas should become stored links): the engagement list's Persona filter and the reports still count recorded coverage, so the page and those can differ; storing them would need rules for removal and for a participant who is later removed, so it is left for the user to ask for. The endpoint reads each participant's Stakeholder's represented Personas one Stakeholder at a time (participants per Engagement are few), is not on the scaling probe and is not an MCP tool.
decisions.section: Engagement participants (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Record codes on the detail page
decisions.statement: The codes beside Participants and Personas covered made them inconsistent with Facilitators, which show none.
decisions.rationale: They are hidden by default; the Engagement actions menu has **Show codes** / **Hide codes**, stored as the per-user UI preference `engagement.showRecordCodes`. `RepresentationPanel` takes `showCodes` (default true, so the Stakeholder, Persona and Need pages are unchanged). a preference rather than page state, so the choice survives navigation.
decisions.section: Engagement participants (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: One generic table
decisions.statement: `artefact_placements` (migration `0143`): `(artefact_type, artefact_id, component_id, category_id NULL)`, a plain registry-validated type string like `artefact_tags`, project-scoped, cascading with the project.
decisions.rationale: A record holds any number of pairs with no primary one (two partial unique indexes, with and without a category). The component is required and a category must sit under it, validated in `services.placements`.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Only the requirement keeps columns
decisions.statement: The plan said requirements *and change requests* keep a single component.
decisions.rationale: The code says otherwise: a change request has no component of its own, only `proposed_component_id`/`proposed_category_id`, which say where a *new* requirement would go. A change request is therefore placed through the table like any other record; `COLUMN_PLACED_TYPES` is `{requirement}`. `pairs_for_records` presents one resolved view for every type.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: A record owned by the organisation cannot be placed
decisions.statement: A component belongs to one project, so an organisation-owned persona or strategy has no tree to sit in; the API answers 422 and `can_edit` is false.
decisions.rationale: No ancestor fallback: a placement is a reference to a row, not a definition table, so the nested-project question is answered "none".
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Derived compliance types are not_placeable
decisions.statement: New `ModuleDefinition.not_placeable` (reason per type, read by `get_not_placeable_types`): the compliance requirement, the project's assessment of it and the required-action assessment are classified by the standard's own structure.
decisions.rationale: Every other type needs no declaration.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: One filter dependency
decisions.statement: `?component_id=…&category_id=…` (repeatable, matching any) is composed into `TagFilter`, so the 20 list endpoints that already take it, the record-table export and the record-list report filter by placement with no per-endpoint edit and cannot forget one.
decisions.rationale: Tag and placement filters both apply when both are given.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: Export and import
decisions.statement: The engine, not a provider, adds a shared `placements` column (`services.placements.placement_column`) to every type's table except the requirement's, written as component prefixes, `SW` or `SW/PERF`, `;`-separated, the form the requirement table uses.
decisions.rationale: It is omitted when the project has no components. An import applies it after the type's own create or update path through `set_record_placements` (so audit events and validation are the same as the API's); a person who may not place gets a row error for a non-blank cell, and an update whose only change is placements skips the provider's update (no empty new version).
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: Keeping the tree consistent
decisions.statement: Deleting a category moves its placements to the category that replaces it (a record already there keeps one); deleting a component that records still sit in is refused with 409, as a component with categories already is.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Frontend: one insertion point, not 60 edits
decisions.statement: `TagField` renders `ComponentField`, `RecordTags` renders `RecordPlacements`, and `TagFilterField` renders `ComponentFilterField`, so every create form, record page and list that already has tags has components, and a new taggable type gets them with no further edit.
decisions.rationale: The create form's choice reaches the create path through `hooks/pendingPlacements` (a store keyed by project and type, cleared when the field unmounts) and is applied by `useCommitTags`, because adding a fourth argument to the `onSave` of about 25 forms and 35 call sites was a larger and riskier change than the one contract tags already use. The cost is that the names `TagField`/`useCommitTags` now cover classification; the style guide's "Pattern: components on a record" says so. The list filter state lives in `useTagFilter` (`in_component`, `in_category` in the URL, `listFilters` for the API wrappers); the requirements list, which has its own component filter, passes `components={false}`.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: Components column
decisions.statement: `DirectoryTable`'s optional `placements` prop reads the page's places in one request (`GET .../placements/{type}?id=…`, at most 500 ids, records the caller cannot open left out) and shows the column only when a row is placed, so a project that does not use components sees no new column.
decisions.rationale: The two hand-written tables (Actions, Change requests) use the same hook. The people list (several kinds in one table) has no column.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: Perf tooling
decisions.statement: `add_tags` also calls `add_placements`, so every generator places its batch with no per-type call; `perf/datasets/profiles.yaml` gains `placements_per_record` (version 5).
decisions.rationale: A test checks the generated places stay inside their own project's tree and the application reads them.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component and category on every record: Template cloning
decisions.statement: Not part of this change: a template is cloned by the project-template work, which copies the tree and remaps ids.
decisions.section: Component and category on every record (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Requirement actions in the project bundle: Codes are kept
decisions.statement: An action keeps its `ACT-nnn` code, as a requirement does, so links by code and a person's references still hold, and the project's action counter moves past the imported codes.
decisions.rationale: A code that is missing, malformed or repeated is numbered afresh with a warning. (A change request and the module records are numbered afresh; those are the rule for records without a counter of their own.)
decisions.section: Requirement actions in the project bundle (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Kinds, not names, carry behaviour
decisions.statement: `StagePhaseKind`: open (editable, reorderable), review (review deadline and stakeholder responses), locked (entering writes the baseline and approves the requirements), on hold (no rules), closed (entering records completion, optional cascade).
decisions.rationale: Nothing reads a phase name.
decisions.section: Customisable stage workflows (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Two tiers on one table
decisions.statement: `stage_workflows` has `organization_id` always and `project_id` NULL for the organisation tier (migration `0144`, with `stage_workflow_phases`).
decisions.rationale: A project's effective set is the organisation's rows it has not hidden (`definition_suppression` kind `stage_workflow`; delete on an organisation row inside a project hides it, `Add organisation defaults` restores it) plus its own rows or, when it has none, its nearest ancestor's (the `resolve_effective_action_types` shape). **Nested projects:** decided as that fallback, additive with the organisation tier; hidden markers are per project and not inherited. A project always keeps at least one usable workflow.
decisions.section: Customisable stage workflows (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Standard is seeded per organisation, not per root project
decisions.statement: Because the organisation tier is additive and always present, a root-only project seed would only add a duplicate.
