decisions.rationale: New organisations get Standard (`create_organization`, bootstrap, organisation import); `default_workflow` re-creates it for an organisation that has none at all; the migration adds it to every existing organisation and maps each stage: Scoping open, Review review, Approved locked, Completed closed, **Archived on hold** (the plan listed four phases; the old `archived` status had no gating, which `on_hold` reproduces exactly). The old status column is dropped.
decisions.section: Customisable stage workflows (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Free movement; a locked phase needs the project manager both ways
decisions.statement: The user decided only entering a locked phase needs the approver role.
decisions.rationale: Leaving one is the mirror image: it silently unlocks the requirements outside the change-request process (the rule the old forward-only state machine existed to protect, C-G-12), so `move_stage` requires the project manager for both. Everything else is free for a manager. Leaving a locked or closed phase clears the approval or completion stamp; the baseline stays as history.
decisions.section: Customisable stage workflows (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Editing a workflow in use
decisions.statement: A phase a stage is in can be renamed but not removed or given another kind; a workflow a stage follows cannot be deleted.
decisions.rationale: The plan said "reassign its stages"; that needs a phase-to-phase mapping with no single correct answer, so the edit is refused with a message instead. A stage changes workflow (`PATCH` with `workflow_id`) only while it is in an open phase with no baseline.
decisions.section: Customisable stage workflows (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: What a component's lock approves
decisions.statement: The edit lock is a requirement *status* (`approved`), set by a baseline, not a live check of the stage, so "the stricter lock wins" had nothing to compare.
decisions.rationale: Entering a locked phase on a track approves and baselines only that component's requirements that target that stage (`Baseline.component_id`, label "Stage / Component baseline"). Leaving a locked phase clears the stamp and keeps the baseline as history, as a stage does.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component phases: The stage's own lock
decisions.statement: With the switch on, a stage entering a locked phase approves only requirements of components with no applicable track for that stage; a stage's closed-phase cascade follows the same rule.
decisions.rationale: *Agent detail:* "tracked" means a row exists and is not "not applicable", so a not applicable component follows the stage. A component with no row is untracked until a manager changes it or moves its track.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Who may move a track
decisions.statement: A project manager or the track's owner (a user, or a member of a group by effective membership, `principals.is_principal_member`).
decisions.rationale: The owner may also move into or out of a locked phase. Only a manager sets the owner, workflow and applicability. The owner field is part of this phase, not the schedule phase.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: One implementation of phase behaviour
decisions.statement: `stage_workflows.move_stage` now delegates to `apply_phase_move`, which a stage and a component track both use, so approval, baseline, completion and stamps cannot drift.
decisions.rationale: `complete_stage` and `create_baseline_for_stage` take an optional component.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component phases: Rows are created lazily
decisions.statement: `component_stage_states` (migration `0145`) has a row only once a component picks a workflow, a phase, an owner or "not applicable"; no row means the stage's workflow at its starting phase.
decisions.rationale: The track reads (`project_tracks`) cost a fixed number of queries.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component phases: Workflow rules
decisions.statement: A track changes workflow or applicability only in an open phase with no baseline of its own (the stage rule).
decisions.rationale: A workflow or phase in use by a track cannot be deleted, re-kinded or removed (`workflow_in_use`, `_phase_in_use` read both tables). Progression is advisory : `previous_closed` is informational, nothing blocks an earlier start.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component phases: Nested projects
decisions.statement: States are state, not a definition table, so no fallback; only `component_phases_mode` inherits (own, else nearest ancestor, else off), the tag-mode shape.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Component phases: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: The project bundle carries the switch, each stored track (component prefix, stage name, workflow, phase, owner, applicability) and a baseline's component.
decisions.rationale: An imported track never lands in a locked or closed phase (it starts at the workflow's first phase with a warning) and carries no approval stamp. A template clone copies the switch and, for the new project's first stage (matched by name), each component's workflow and applicability, with the phase reset to the start; owners and progress are not copied, and stages are lifecycle state so other stages' tracks cannot exist yet.
decisions.section: Component phases (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Phase schedule and reminders: Time shapes
decisions.statement: Expected range: a person's calendar date.
decisions.rationale: Actual dates: past instants in UTC. The sweep has no caller's day, so "upcoming" compares with the latest day anywhere (UTC+14) and "overdue" requires the end to have passed everywhere (UTC-12) Tests pin both boundaries (09:59 and 10:00 UTC for the upcoming horizon, 11:59 and 12:00 UTC for overdue). The screen marks a phase overdue against the viewer's own day, so it can show Overdue for a few hours before the reminder is sent; the reminder never fires early.
decisions.section: Phase schedule and reminders (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Phase schedule and reminders: Once per date
decisions.statement: `upcoming_notified_for` holds the expected start notified and `overdue_notified_for` the expected end notified, so a rescheduled phase re-arms and a repeated sweep sends nothing.
decisions.rationale: (The specification stored the end date for both; the start date is the right key for the upcoming reminder, because moving the start is what makes it new.) The markers are derived and are not exported, so an import re-arms every reminder.
decisions.section: Phase schedule and reminders (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Phase schedule and reminders: Nested projects
decisions.statement: Plan rows are state, no fallback; only the lead time inherits (own, else nearest ancestor, else 7 days).
decisions.rationale: Component plans are inert while component phases are off (rows kept).
decisions.section: Phase schedule and reminders (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Phase schedule and reminders: Bundles and templates
decisions.statement: The project bundle carries the lead time, each stage's owner by name or email (imported after groups and tracks exist) and each plan row with its actual dates as history.
decisions.rationale: A template clone copies the lead time and no dates or owners.
decisions.section: Phase schedule and reminders (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Phase schedule and reminders: Report fields
decisions.statement: Requirements gain "Target stage phase expected end" and "Target stage phase started at" (the stage's own current phase).
decisions.rationale: **Not built :** a variance field and per-component fields; the screen shows the variance, and a component's schedule is read per track, for the same reason as the component phase column in the previous phase (the inherited switch). **Not built:** the project overview metric, which belongs to the overview widgets phase and its metric catalogue.
decisions.section: Phase schedule and reminders (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Navigation names: Stable keys
decisions.statement: A core entry has a fixed key (`overview`, `requirements`, `change-requests`, `actions`, `files`, `reviews-due`, `history`, `admin`).
decisions.rationale: A module entry's key is derived from the registry, `<module key>:<path below the module root>` (`decisions:`, `risk_management:risks`), by `services.nav_labels.nav_key`, so it never contains a project id and a module declares nothing new. Writes accept only keys the registry knows, whether or not the module is enabled, so switching a module off does not discard its names; the catalogue a person sees lists only what the project (or organisation) can reach. A name is plain single-line text of at most 40 characters; blank means no name.
decisions.section: Navigation names (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Lookup by route path, not key
decisions.statement: `GET .../nav-labels` returns each entry's key, built-in name, resolved path, own name, inherited name and source.
decisions.rationale: The browser keys the effective names by path (`NavLabelContext`), because every list page already knows its own route and a record page already passes its list route to `RecordHeader`'s `back`; no module or page names a key. `Layout`, `ListPageLayout` and `RecordHeader` read it generically, so no core file names a module. A page that draws its own heading (History, Compliance) reads `useCurrentNavLabelOverride`. Two caveats: a title or back label is replaced by the name verbatim even where the built-in was a plural of a singular entry label (Context & Strategy entries are singular, their titles the same), and a page that hosts several record kinds under one route (People) shows the entry's name for all of them.
decisions.section: Navigation names (2026-11-07)

decisions.title: Server and organisation messages: One mechanism, two scopes
decisions.statement: One table `announcements` (migration `0148`) with a nullable `organization_id` (NULL is platform-wide), the shape `Tag.project_id` and the organisation/server defaults use.
decisions.rationale: One service (`services.announcements`), one API shape and one panel (`AnnouncementsPanel`, scope passed in) serve both; Server Management has a Messages group and Organisation Admin a Messages group.
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Scope is enforced in the service, not the route
decisions.statement: Every lookup takes the owning organisation (NULL for platform), so an organisation administrator can neither read nor change a platform message or another organisation's message.
decisions.rationale: A mismatch is a 404, so an id of another tenant is not confirmed; another organisation's collection is a 403 from `require_org_role`. Personal access tokens cannot reach the server routes (`require_server_admin`).
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Server and organisation messages: Where it shows
decisions.statement: `/login`: platform messages flagged for login.
decisions.rationale: `/login/:slug`: platform plus that organisation's flagged messages. After sign-in, a dismissible banner pinned above the top bar on every page (a full-width strip per message, tinted by severity; the top bar, navigation rail and pinned designer bar sit below it through `--announcement-height`, which the banner keeps equal to its measured height; organizationId`). The banner request names an organisation only to select among those the person belongs to; one they are not a member of is ignored.
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Server and organisation messages: Plain text only
decisions.statement: The login page is the highest phishing risk and an organisation administrator is lower trust than the server administrator.
decisions.rationale: Text is rendered as React text (never HTML, markup or links; a story pins it), control characters are removed, the title is one line (120 characters), the message at most 1000. **Added beyond the plan :** an organisation message may not contain a web address (`http:`, `https:`, `ftp:`, `www.`); a platform message may. The rendering rule alone leaves "go to evil.example and sign in" possible, and a mail client may turn a typed address into a link in the notification email. Imported messages follow the same rule.
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Server and organisation messages: Unauthenticated read
decisions.statement: `GET /api/v1/announcements/login` returns only active, login-flagged messages as `{id, title, body, severity, scope}`: no author, no organisation id, no send data.
decisions.rationale: An unknown slug returns the platform messages only (it does not reveal whether a slug exists; `login-info` already answers that). It is rate limited per client address with its own token bucket (`public_announcement_rate_limit_*`, a reserve of 30 then 60 a minute, per worker process), separate from the password-reset bucket so a login page view never spends reset attempts. The address is the first `X-Forwarded-For` hop, with the same spoofing caveat as the reset limit (recorded in the access control policy). A failed read shows nothing, never an error, so the login form stays usable.
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Server and organisation messages: Time shape
decisions.statement: `starts_at` and `ends_at` are instants stored in UTC (a window a person picks in the browser's local time, converted by `utils/dateTimeLocal`), both optional; a value with no timezone is refused (a bare local time is ambiguous).
decisions.rationale: Active means `starts_at <= now < ends_at`. Tests cover the two edges and the boundary hours (09:00 at UTC+10 stores as 23:00Z the day before, 23:00 at UTC-8 as 07:00Z the next day). The server resolves a message's status (scheduled, active, ended) on its own clock.
decisions.section: Server and organisation messages (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Axis scope is a generic extension
decisions.statement: `ScoringAxisDefinition.per_target`, `ScoringSchemeDefinition.target_label` and `scoring_custom_axes.per_target` (migration `0149`) are core and generic; Severity, Frequency, Confidence and User/business value are per persona, Time criticality, Risk reduction and Job size are for the whole Pain Point.
decisions.rationale: A custom axis chooses when created and cannot change it, because stored scores depend on it; a scheme with no target refuses a per-target axis.
decisions.section: Pain Point scoring on the Product Feedback model: General row, custom criteria, Cost of Delay (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Template projects: Nested projects
decisions.statement: A clone copies the template's own rows only, never an ancestor's effective rows; the new project's fallback then follows its own parent.
decisions.rationale: A template that is itself a child with no rows of its own therefore gives a root project the usual root seeding.
decisions.section: Template projects: full configuration and starter records (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: A flow grid with width and height, edited on the page
decisions.statement: Reversing the first decision (order and width only, no free placement), the user asked for widgets that can be made bigger or smaller and edited on the page itself while staying responsive.
decisions.rationale: A widget has a width of 1 to 12 columns and a height of 1 to 12 rows (a minimum: the grid rows are `minmax(44px, auto)`, so content is never clipped). The layout is a flow with spans, not absolute positions, so it collapses to six columns on a medium screen and two on a phone with no second layout (`gridSpans`: a small tile stays one column on a phone, any other widget takes the full width). (for the user to veto): no grid library; dragging reorders the flow and the corner changes the spans, with arrow-key equivalents on the handle and the corner and width and height boxes in the settings; the resize corner is hidden below 1,000px because the columns no longer match the stored width. The built-in layout's first row is 3+3+2+2+2 columns so the five key tiles share a row.
decisions.section: Project overview widgets (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Project overview widgets: Extension points
decisions.statement: `ModuleDefinition.overview_widgets` and `TierAModuleDefinition.overviewWidgets` (a module's own widget type, validated on the server, rendered through the registry) and `ModuleDefinition.overview_metrics`.
decisions.rationale: (2026-11-08, replacing the first version): there is no special group for module tiles. The core "Module summary tiles" widget and `TierAModuleDefinition.projectOverviewTiles` are gone; Compliance's per-standard tiles are its `standards_status` widget, so every module contribution is an ordinary widget that can be placed anywhere, sized, hidden or removed. `OverviewWidgetType.in_default_layout`, `width` and `height` let the built-in layout include a module's widget while the module is enabled (after the five key tiles) and set the size a new one starts with; a layout a person has saved is never changed when a module is enabled later, so they add the widget from the list. A widget with nothing to show renders empty and is hidden outside edit mode. No `overview_metrics` entry is declared by a first-party module yet.
decisions.section: Project overview widgets (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: A text widget on the project overview
decisions.statement: Markdown of at most 4,000 characters, plain text on the server.
decisions.rationale: It is rendered by `utils/safeMarkdown` as elements: headings, lists, quotes, rules, bold, italic, code and links, with no raw HTML and no image, and only `http` and `https` links (opened with `rel="noopener noreferrer"`), because an organisation administrator's text reaches every project member. : a subset on purpose; an unknown construct shows as the text typed.
decisions.section: Project overview widgets (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: A template carries a project's scoring configuration
decisions.statement: A project created from the Product Design template came out on the platform default model, and the project bundle did not carry it either (an earlier choice recorded as not carried).
decisions.rationale: (2026-11-08, asked with options): carry all of it. `services/scoring_config.py` exports and imports, per registered scheme, a project's default model, offered models, bands, level thresholds and cell ratings, in the project bundle (`scoring_configuration`) and in a template copy. Levels are matched by scheme, axis and name (never id), so a bundle moves between organisations and a missing level is skipped with a warning. A custom model or axis is created afresh with a new key on import, so the bundle carries its label and the import matches the project's own by label (tested: a default naming the template's own model follows it). The organisation's levels and the organisation-level overrides are still not carried. The Risk and Product Feedback export notes, the website template and export pages and `docs/modules.md` §4k are updated.
decisions.section: Phase 17: demo data, and what reading the generated document found (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: The group suffix is a file format, so it keeps reading the old form
decisions.statement: `PRINCIPAL_TYPE_LABEL` is also what an export writes in a person cell (`Name (Org group)`), so it changed to `Name (Organisation group)` with the interface label, keeping one term for one thing.
decisions.rationale: `group_ref_from_text` still accepts the earlier `(Org group)` suffix so a file exported before the change re-imports (`test_csv_import_still_reads_the_earlier_org_group_suffix`). The alternative, leaving exports with the abbreviation, would have kept two names for one thing.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19a: wording, loading indicators, import warnings, style guide (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: UI/UX fixes 19a: Style guide
decisions.statement: Principle 8 and the compact-forms and button-size sections now say an icon-only button's name is its `aria-label` and a native `title` may only repeat it; "explain in help" says a `title` never explains.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19a: wording, loading indicators, import warnings, style guide (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Triage of the helpNotNeeded fields
decisions.statement: The scan found 344 uses whose label is not a plain name; each was judged by whether a person could tell what the field is, what it affects and a typical value from its caption alone.
decisions.rationale: About 100 now have help: component, category, reasoning and owner on requirements and change requests, action type, cascade on completion, new-user role, organisation and server branding, e-mail footer, SCIM token, SMTP settings, personal access token lifetime and expiry, custom role preset, sign-up mode, project status and parent, custom field type, options and required, preferences (pronouns, content width, landing page, e-mail notifications), template and organisation on New project, report block source (linked from, direction, group, include archived), and the module fields (Compliance dates, owners and the default managers group, Context & Strategy priority, time horizon and dates, Decision type, date, maker and owner, Risk type, owner and next review, Engagement channel, Stakeholder organisation and parent group). Left as self-explanatory, with the reason: names, titles, descriptions, notes, e-mail and password captions on sign-in pages, filter controls, search boxes, date-range endpoints and the report designer's own editing controls (Blocks, columns, conditions, grid), whose side panel already describes them. A field helped in one place keeps its text in one table (`strings.help`, or the module's `help.ts`), so create, edit and detail views read the same.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19b: help instead of permanent text, shared strings (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Create and Import are two doors
decisions.statement: New project and New organisation are a `SplitButtonTrigger`: the default click opens the create dialog and the chevron offers **Import project** / **Import organisation**, each its own dialog.
decisions.rationale: The earlier "Or import from an exported bundle" file field inside the create form hid the code, report name, template and creation-choice fields once a file was chosen, with a note explaining why; that behaviour and the `importIgnoresTemplate` note are gone. (the phase 18 checkpoint approved group B); the split button over a menu is on the style guide's wording for a primary action with one alternative, and matches New standard.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19c: creation routes and the Nesting group (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: UI/UX fixes 19c: Nesting group
decisions.statement: Parent, Inheritance and Mirror role are one collapsed "Nesting" `CollapsibleSection` on New project, with the chosen parent as its pill and an accent border when a parent is set (it also covers "Add sub-project", which pre-selects the parent).
decisions.rationale: The group is absent when no project can be a parent, as before. `components/ProjectNestingFields` is shared with the project settings page, which carried a second copy of the same three fields and of the rule that a parent change resets an elevated inheritance mode; `MODES_NEEDING_CONFIRMATION` moved to `utils/projectInheritance.ts` and both copies of the constant are gone. Collapse state is remembered per person (the shared section's own behaviour).
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19c: creation routes and the Nesting group (2026-11-08)

decisions.title: Three components, one per place
decisions.statement: `FilterSelect` (filter panels: caption, optional `(?)` help, "All" entry, accessible name from the caption), `LabeledSelect` (form fields, existing) and `InlineSelect` (a control in a row with no caption, existing, now generic with `className`, `autoWidth`, per-option `disabled` and `group`).
decisions.rationale: All 75 selects in filter panels and the 20 remaining hand-written ones (module availability, staged member role, link type flow and nesting, change request proposed fields, scoring bands and matrix, project scope, quick link relationship, report block target, delete-in-use reassignment, the mobile resource menu with its option groups, overview editor, history entity type, bulk move) moved onto them; the tag-mode setting became a `LabeledSelect`.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19d: one select component per place (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: UI/UX fixes 19d: Typed to the enum
decisions.statement: `FilterSelect` is a discriminated union: with `allLabel` the value and change handler take `V | ""`, without it `V`.
decisions.rationale: `labelOptions(LABEL_MAP)` (`utils/labelOptions.ts`) builds options from the existing label map, so the compiler now checks that a status filter's state type matches the label map's keys; the one `Object.keys` cast sits in that helper.
decisions.section: UI/UX fixes 19d: one select component per place (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: One slot, not a per-page row
decisions.statement: `components/PageActions` (`PageActionsProvider`, `PageActionsSlot`, `PageActions`) lets a section render its own actions into the page's title row through a portal.
decisions.rationale: The organisation overview places the slot first in its action group, so Export sits just before Reports and the Files and Settings links, and the group does not move when the section changes. A section keeps its own state (its filters feed the report), and the core page names no module. With no slot (a story, a section used alone) the action renders inline and right-aligned as before.
decisions.section: Organisation compliance pages: Export beside Reports (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: One grid, editor and catalogue
decisions.statement: The project overview's grid, editor and widget settings are reused with a third edit target (`kind: "dashboard"`) and an organisation endpoint set, not copied: `useOverviewMetrics` takes the endpoint, `OverviewWidgetGrid` takes `organizationId` beside `projectId`, and `overview_widgets.WidgetRules` (core types, module types, metric validator, whether a widget has a project scope) lets the project…
decisions.rationale: and the organisation validate through the same code.
decisions.section: Organisation dashboards (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Organisation dashboards: Organisation catalogue
decisions.statement: Core metrics are the four headline figures (the stats endpoint's own computation, extracted to `services/org_overview_stats.py` so the two cannot disagree), projects by status, and a record count over a registered type summed across the projects the caller may read (one `count_in_project` per project, bounded by the caller's projects; no filters in this version).
decisions.rationale: Modules add organisation figures as their own widget (`org_overview_widgets`), not as metrics. An organisation administrator keeps seeing the organisation's real totals and everyone else their own scope, the standing rule from the stats header.
decisions.section: Organisation dashboards (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Layout storage and the built-in page
decisions.statement: Pages are rows (`organization_dashboards`), viewers are rows (`organization_dashboard_viewers`, migration 0152).
decisions.rationale: The built-in Overview page exists before it is stored, answers to the id `overview`, and is stored (empty layout, so the built-in layout still applies) on its first edit; it cannot be renamed, moved or deleted. Organisation `overview_widgets` stays the default **project** layout; the dashboard layout is a separate thing, not a reuse of that column.
decisions.section: Organisation dashboards (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Component stage and phase setup: review fixes: W7, phase on lists
decisions.statement: `RequirementOut.phase_name`/`phase_kind` on the project list and a `phase` filter (also on the shared record list and its export).
decisions.rationale: The governing phase is the component's own track when component phases are on and the component has a track row, else the stage's phase; a component marked not applicable has none. This is the rule the lock and approval use (`tracked_component_ids`), read once (`requirement_phase_lookup`), and the filter is a plain SQL condition built from the project's stages and tracks, so paging stays in the database. Overview metrics `phases_overdue` and `phases_upcoming` count scheduled phases against the viewer's own calendar day (`phase_attention_counts`, the daily reminders' reading). **Known difference:** a component with no track row is shown by the track list at its workflow's starting phase (what a move starts from) but is governed by the stage's phase; the requirement list shows the governing one. Not built: a report field for the governing phase (the inherited switch cannot be resolved in report SQL).
decisions.section: Component stage and phase setup: review fixes (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Collapsible workflows: Shared row
decisions.statement: `DisclosureRow` (presentational: toggle, summary, actions beside it, detail) and `useDisclosureState`.
decisions.rationale: `CollapsibleSection` was not reused: it is a titled card whose whole header is the click target and cannot hold per-item actions without nesting buttons.
decisions.section: Collapsible workflows (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Collapsible workflows: Open state storage
decisions.statement: One `ui_preferences` key per list (`disclosure_toggled:<list>`) holding only the ids that differ from the default, capped at 50.
decisions.rationale: The preference bag allows 200 keys in total, so a key per workflow or stage would eventually fail to save for a person with many items. The default is open for one item and closed for several. The ids of deleted items are not pruned (bounded by the cap).
decisions.section: Collapsible workflows (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Sweep of stacked per-item lists
decisions.statement: Moved: stage workflows (organisation and project, one panel) and the stage phase schedule (a table, owner and scope selector per stage).
decisions.rationale: Examined and unchanged: project stages and organisation projects (one line per item), `DefinitionList` (fields edited in place; collapsing would hide the edit), link-type rows, overview widget rows and the scoring sections (already `CollapsibleSection`). `ComponentTracksList` keeps its own toggle because the next phase replaces it with a flat list ; moving it onto the row first would be rework.
decisions.section: Collapsible workflows (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Component phases setup: Track list
decisions.statement: `ComponentTracksList` is one `DirectoryTable` row per component and stage (component, stage, phase picker, workflow, owner, state, and an edit column only where the host passes `onEdit`), ordered by component then stage.
decisions.rationale: (rows per component and stage, not a column per stage: a column per stage grows wide with many stages and has to hold a picker, workflow and owner in each cell). The disclosure, its summary line and the `toggleComponent` string are removed.
decisions.section: Component phases setup: compact switch, flat track list (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Component phases setup: Filters kept, not extended
decisions.statement: The stage filter and "Only tracks I can move" remain as built; the earlier review also named phase and owner filters but only these two were ever built, and the table is not long enough per stage to need more.
decisions.rationale: Not added without a request.
decisions.section: Component phases setup: compact switch, flat track list (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Component delivery status page: Data source
decisions.statement: Composed in the browser from the existing bulk reads (stages, component tracks, phase plans) through `utils/deliveryPlan`: no new endpoint for the figures, so one server definition of who may move what and no second definition of progress or overdue.
decisions.rationale: Overdue is the overview figure's rule (the current phase is not closed and its own expected end is before the viewer's day); progress is the step reached in the holder's workflow ("Step 2 of 5", "Completed" for a closed phase). Time shapes: expected dates are calendar dates compared with `localToday()`; recorded start and completion are UTC instants shown as the viewer's local day. Boundary test: an expected end equal to today is not overdue, the next day is.
decisions.section: Component delivery status page (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Shared pieces extracted, call sites moved
decisions.statement: `usePhaseMove` (closed-phase confirmation and transition post) replaces three copies (track list, stage list in project administration, the new stage table); `usePhaseRangeEditor` replaces the phase schedule panel's own save; `ProgressMeter` is the one progress bar; `formatDay` moved to `utils/deliveryPlan`.
decisions.section: Component delivery status page (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Component delivery status page: Naming and columns
decisions.statement: The page, its navigation entry (`stage-phases` default label in `services/nav_labels.py`; the route is unchanged) and its documentation are **Delivery status**; the stage section is "Project stages" (`{Project} {stage}s`) and the component section "By component", rendered only while component phases are on (no explanatory text in its place). "Phase" is "Current phase"; the Workflow column is not…
decisions.rationale: shown on this page (project administration keeps it). Internal identifiers (`utils/deliveryPlan`, `DeliveryTimeline`) keep their names.
decisions.section: Component delivery status page (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Navigation entry hidden until stages are used
decisions.statement: Every project is created with one "Scoping" stage and the last stage cannot be deleted, so "has stages" never distinguishes a project.
decisions.rationale: The entry is shown only when `GET /projects/{id}/stage-usage` (`services/stage_usage.stages_in_use`, read-gated like the stage list) says the project goes beyond it: several stages, or a stage that left its first phase or has an owner, review deadline or completion, or any phase schedule row, or component phases on. `useProjectHasStages` asks again on each route change, so using stages in administration appears on the next navigation; unknown or a failed read counts as not in use. Advisory only, never an authorisation decision; the route still opens by address. Nothing stored changed, so no bundle, template or seed change.
decisions.section: Component delivery status page (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Demo project from this repository: Known gaps are loaded
decisions.statement: The SOC 2 package is in a public repository, so loading the open known gaps as Risks publishes nothing new (checked: the repository is public and `docs/soc2/` holds no credentials).
decisions.rationale: `--skip-gaps` on `seed_repo_demo.py` leaves them out; resolved (struck through) gaps are never loaded.
decisions.section: Demo project from this repository (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Up to 1,000 decisions, fewer if the log has fewer
decisions.statement: The log holds about 2,470 bullets, but most are findings, bug notes, results and process remarks, not decisions.
decisions.rationale: After a review of the candidates the fixture holds every bullet that records a `Decided by` attribution plus the unattributed bullets of the log's original design sections , about 480 in all. Bullets that are notes, routes, files or results are excluded by pattern, a hand-reviewed list in `backend/scripts/data/repo_demo_curation.json` excludes a further 60 and rewrites ten titles, titles too short to stand alone take their section's subject as a prefix (`Context & Strategy: Nested projects`), and the text is cleaned of attribution notes and line breaks. Types come from keyword rules on the section heading
decisions.section: Demo project from this repository (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Demo project from this repository: Lifecycle follows the attribution
decisions.statement: User-attributed and unattributed decisions are Approved; Agent-attributed ones are Under review, because the log records them as the agent's choices for the user to veto.
decisions.section: Demo project from this repository (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Demo project from this repository: SOC 2
decisions.statement: One standard with a requirement per criterion group and per criterion (34), assessed from the control matrix status (implemented, partial, gap), the eleven policies as evidence linked to the criteria that cite them, and the architecture document's four principles as approved guiding principles.
decisions.section: Demo project from this repository (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: The fixture follows the documents, but a growing log is not drift
decisions.statement: `--check` and the test fail when a requirement, SOC 2 entry or a decision in the fixture was edited or removed in its source; a new log entry does not fail them, since the log is appended to with every change.
decisions.section: Demo project from this repository (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: More example template projects: The set
decisions.statement: Software delivery, Compliance readiness, Research and discovery, and a Hardware design example "like some IoT sensor or datalogger".
decisions.rationale: The proposed Risk-led programme was not chosen. The Hardware design template is an IoT data logger.
decisions.section: More example template projects (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Each template differs in kind, not only in name
decisions.statement: Its own stage workflow with different phase kinds (a release train with a locked release candidate; audit readiness with a locked audit window; a research cycle; hardware design gates with an on-hold validation phase), component phases switched on, its own Pain Point, action, decision and risk types, its own enabled modules, a custom requirement field and an overview dashboard.
decisions.rationale: A test asserts that the four workflows, action types and Pain Point types are pairwise different.
decisions.section: More example template projects (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: More example template projects: Starter records stay drafts
decisions.statement: Requirements always; plus decisions, risks, actions, Pain Points, a persona, stakeholder, need, open question and an engagement with a finding where the module is on.
decisions.rationale: Nothing is approved, so a template never carries an approval into a new project. A project created from each template is tested to receive the requirements as drafts, the workflow and the dashboard.
decisions.section: More example template projects (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Compliance readiness assigns an example standard
decisions.statement: "Information security baseline (example)", four criteria in two groups, published and assigned, so the template shows assessments without depending on another seed.
decisions.rationale: It is an organisation-level standard, visible to the demonstration organisation only.
decisions.section: More example template projects (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: More example template projects: Idempotent by skipping
decisions.statement: A template whose name exists is left unchanged.
decisions.rationale: The existence check passes `include_templates`, because templates are left out of the project list by default; the first version of the check missed them and recreated all four on the second run, which the test caught.
decisions.section: More example template projects (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Messages: Not dismissible
decisions.statement: `announcements.dismissible` (migration 0153, default true, so existing messages keep their close control), on the create and replace payload, the reader shape, the audit detail (a flag, never the text) and the organisation bundle.
decisions.rationale: The banner shows no close control for a message with the flag cleared, and shows it even when it was dismissed earlier in that browser. It stays a banner above the page and never becomes a modal. **It is a display rule, not a security control:** dismissal was already only a per-browser convenience, and a person can hide the banner with their own tools. Organisation administrators may clear it on their own organisation's messages; the no-web-address rule still applies, so it adds no phishing route, and a server-wide message stays out of their reach (a 404 test covers it).
decisions.section: Messages: defaults, severity mark, not dismissible, history (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Messages: Cap and history
decisions.statement: `MAX_PER_SCOPE` (50) now counts only messages that have not ended, so history never forces a deletion; a new ceiling `MAX_STORED_PER_SCOPE` (1,000, ended messages included) still bounds the table against a loop, since a message can be created already ended.
decisions.rationale: Bundle import follows the same two limits.
decisions.section: Messages: defaults, severity mark, not dismissible, history (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Messages: History and Duplicate
decisions.statement: The panel has Current (active and scheduled) and Previous (ended) views and a search over the title and text, in the browser over the scope's list.
decisions.rationale: Duplicate opens the editor with the content, severity, login flag and dismissible flag, a start of now, no end and no notification, and saves as a new message; no endpoint was added.
decisions.section: Messages: defaults, severity mark, not dismissible, history (2026-11-09)

decisions.title: Demonstration accounts survive a reset
decisions.statement: Organisation deletion exists (`DELETE /orgs/{id}`), but accounts are never deleted (audit rows reference users), so a second seed finds `demo.admin@example.com` already present.
decisions.rationale: The user chose a fixed password by default, with password rotation as an option (`--rotate-passwords` or `DEMO_ROTATE_PASSWORDS=1`). `seed_demo_data.create_org_user` now re-joins an existing account to the new organisation through the roles route. Rotation keeps the current random password in `DEMO_STATE_DIR` (mode 0600, a volume shared by the backend and the scheduler) and changes it through `/auth/change-password` before seeding; if the stored password no longer signs in, the run stops and says why.
decisions.section: Demonstration setup command and daily reset (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Demonstration setup command and daily reset: Failure handling
decisions.statement: Names and account emails are unique, so the new data cannot be seeded beside the old.
decisions.rationale: A failed seed therefore removes the partly seeded organisation, says the previous data could not be kept, writes `reqtrack_demo_reset_last_success 0` to the status directory and exits 1. A failure before seeding (guards, password change) leaves existing data alone. One run at a time through a file lock (exit 75).
decisions.section: Demonstration setup command and daily reset (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Demonstration setup command and daily reset: Microsoft Clarity
decisions.statement: Off unless `DEMO_CLARITY_PROJECT_ID` is set (`scripts/demo.sh --clarity <id>`), which becomes `CLARITY_PROJECT_ID` in the frontend's runtime `env-config.js`.
decisions.rationale: The identifier is restricted to letters and digits in the entrypoint and again in `utils/clarity.ts` before it is used in a script address. Masking is configured in the operator's Clarity project; the documentation says to use Strict and never to enable it on a deployment with real data, because the sign-in details message is on screen. Recorded as a vendor exception in the vendor management policy (known gap 6). No content security policy exists to amend (only `frame-ancestors`).
decisions.section: Demonstration setup command and daily reset (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation settings: usage table: One read path
decisions.statement: `OrgUsageTable` reads `GET /orgs/{id}/overview-stats`, the function the organisation dashboards' core metrics already use (`services/org_overview_stats.py`), so the table and the widgets cannot disagree; a backend test pins the equality for project count, member count and file storage.
decisions.section: Organisation settings: usage table (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation settings: usage table: Archived projects
decisions.statement: The stats gained `archived_project_count` (the plan asked for projects including archived, with the active count) rather than changing `project_count`, which the project list and the dashboards define as active only.
decisions.section: Organisation settings: usage table (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation settings: usage table: No quota row
decisions.statement: The plan said "with the organisation's quota if one is set"; no organisation storage quota exists in the product, so there is nothing to show.
decisions.rationale: A quota, if added later, becomes a further row.
decisions.section: Organisation settings: usage table (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Empty means the platform value
decisions.statement: On the organisation company settings (header title, email footer name, website, address) the Custom pill and the reset link are removed.
decisions.rationale: An empty field already stores null and uses the platform value, so the platform value is shown as the field's placeholder to make that visible. The logo and login background keep a Remove control without a pill, and show the platform file muted when none is set.
decisions.section: Organisation administration UI/UX review (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation administration UI/UX review: Scope of the rule
decisions.statement: The removal concerns **platform defaults** only, because organisations do not manage them.
decisions.rationale: A pill that says a project's value comes from its organisation or a parent project stays. The style guide's Principle 2 and "Pattern: platform default vs. override" are edited in the fixing change to say so.
decisions.section: Organisation administration UI/UX review (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Platform defaults are not shown to an organisation
decisions.statement: On the company settings the "Custom" pill and the reset link are gone; an empty text field uses the platform value, which is its placeholder (`usePlatformBranding`, the public branding read `BrandingContext` already makes).
decisions.rationale: The logo and login background use `BrandingImageField`: a **Remove** button while the organisation has its own file, the platform picture shown dimmed under a "Platform default" caption otherwise. The style guide's Principle 2 and "Pattern: platform default vs. override" now say this, with the tier pills ("Inherited from organisation") unchanged.
decisions.section: Organisation administration UI/UX fixes (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: A deviation from "remove the reset"
decisions.statement: A band set, a set of models or a link rule cannot be emptied, so removing the reset would remove the only way back to the module default (the *Prefer the flexible reading* rule).
decisions.rationale: `OverridePill` gained `platformFallback`: no pill, and a reset button only while the value differs, the same shape as the files' Remove button. Text fields and the personal data switch lose the control entirely, as the user asked.
decisions.section: Organisation administration UI/UX fixes (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: One settings save per page
decisions.statement: `PUT /orgs/{id}/advanced-settings` reset every field a request did not send to its default, so a partial request would have turned off, for example, the two-factor requirement.
decisions.rationale: It is now a partial update (`model_fields_set`): an omitted field is left as it is, an explicit null still clears. The page saves email, security, token lifetime and report configuration separately (`saveAdvanced(group)`); the token lifetime had no Save of its own and the hint "Saved with the Security settings above" is gone. The audit event now lists the field names sent, never values. Test: `backend/tests/test_org_advanced_settings_partial.py`. The 14 invite, import and OIDC tests that fail on a host without the mail catcher fail identically before and after.
decisions.section: Organisation administration UI/UX fixes (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Compact row, editor in a Modal
decisions.statement: The Default overview section keeps its place and heading (with a `(?)` stating what the default affects) but its body is one row: "Built-in layout" or "Customised: N widgets", and **Edit overview default**.
decisions.rationale: The button opens the unchanged `OverviewEditor` in a `Modal` of size `lg` (900 px, the widest the shared dialog offers). A `SidePanel` was rejected: the style guide gives it the job of detail about the content pane, and a 12-column grid needs the width. No behaviour change to what is saved; the project overview and the organisation dashboard pages still share the one editor.
decisions.section: Organisation default overview: edited in a dialog (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation Files in the navigation rail: Entry and route
decisions.statement: A **Files** link directly below Projects in the Global section, to `/org-files`, which renders `OrgListPage` with `target="files"`: it redirects to `/orgs/{id}/files` for one organisation and lists the organisations otherwise, exactly as `/org-overview` does, so the rail never needs an organisation id.
decisions.rationale: The overview icon link stays as the in-context route.
decisions.section: Organisation Files in the navigation rail (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation Files in the navigation rail: Active state
decisions.statement: `NavRailLink` gained `alsoActiveOn` (a pattern for a second route family), because the entry's own path redirects away and would never otherwise show as active on the page it opens.
decisions.section: Organisation Files in the navigation rail (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation Files in the navigation rail: Not renamable
decisions.statement: The plan asked for the entry to join the navigation names.
decisions.rationale: Those are project-scoped (resolved per project through its ancestors and organisation, then looked up by route in `NavLabelContext`), and the Global section entries (Projects, Organisation overview) are outside it, so a Global entry has no project to resolve against. Making it renamable needs an organisation-only name map for the Global section, which is a separate feature; the label reuses `strings.files.title`, the project entry's term.
decisions.section: Organisation Files in the navigation rail (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Navigation rail: Reviews due
decisions.statement: `useHasReviewsDue` reads `GET /me/reviews/due?limit=1` and uses the `X-Total-Count` header; it runs when the person is signed in and on the notification poll's 30-second interval, never per navigation.
decisions.rationale: Unknown counts as nothing due, so the entry appears once known; a failed read keeps the last answer. The endpoint now pages before it looks up reviewers, components and projects, so the one-row probe no longer labels the whole list (the response for any page is unchanged). The page stays reachable by address and from notifications.
decisions.section: Navigation rail: order, Notifications, reviews due, Organisation settings (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Demo usage metrics: Scope of the metrics
decisions.statement: System behaviour only (routes, latency, status, lifecycle counts, sign-in results, database and worker load), used together with Microsoft Clarity for on-screen behaviour, matched by time only.
decisions.rationale: No session identifier or other use label is added to a metric (an unbounded label on the unauthenticated `/metrics` output); no use-metric extension point is built.
decisions.section: Demo usage metrics: Prometheus collection and a downloadable bundle (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Demo usage metrics: Marking resets
decisions.statement: The plan proposed recording reset start and end "as metrics".
decisions.rationale: The reset command runs outside the application and its existing metrics file is a textfile only Alloy reads, so putting them on `/metrics` would need a demonstration-only code path in the backend or a Pushgateway for one pair of times. Instead each run appends `reset_started` and `reset_finished` (UTC instant and outcome, nothing else) to `reqtrack-demo-resets.jsonl` in the status volume (500 lines kept; a write failure never fails a run) and the manifest lists the ones inside the range. This explains counter drops the same way and adds no service.
decisions.section: Demo usage metrics: Prometheus collection and a downloadable bundle (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Demo usage metrics: Scrub check
decisions.statement: Every series is checked before anything is written against an allow-list of label names and a value shape per label (a `path` must be `unmatched` or a route template and may not contain a UUID or a query string).
decisions.rationale: A failure names the label, never the value, and writes no file. A test compares the allow-list with the labels `app.metrics` defines, so a new label fails there until it is reviewed.
decisions.section: Demo usage metrics: Prometheus collection and a downloadable bundle (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: Name clash
decisions.statement: The existing Server Management group "Data policy" (the personal data rule for exports and imports) was renamed **Personal data in exports** (route `dataPolicy` became `personalDataExport`, the old address redirects), so "Data policy" now means only the published document.
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: Body format
decisions.statement: A visual editor (TipTap, a new frontend dependency `@tiptap/react`, `@tiptap/pm`, `@tiptap/starter-kit`) was chosen over a Markdown subset or plain text when asked.
decisions.rationale: The stored body is the editor's ProseMirror JSON, validated on write against a closed vocabulary (paragraph, heading 1 to 3, bulleted and numbered lists, quotation, horizontal rule, line break; bold, italic, link) and rebuilt field by field , never accepted as markup. The frontend renders it as React elements (no HTML insertion), so there is no sanitiser to bypass. A link may use https, http or mailto, checked on write, in the editor and on render; the rendered link carries `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: One table, nullable owner
decisions.statement: `organization_id` is NULL for a server policy, so the organisation policies of the next piece of work reuse the table, service, API shape and editor.
decisions.rationale: `key` marks the two built-in slots (unique per owner, partial indexes); a slot keeps its title and cannot be deleted, only unpublished. Any other policy has a title of its own (a server administrator may add an acceptable use policy or terms of service).
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: Working copy and versions
decisions.statement: Saving writes the working copy only; readers get `current_version`, so an edit never changes the public text until it is published again, as a new immutable version with its date and an optional change note (administrators only).
decisions.rationale: Unpublishing hides the policy and keeps every version.
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: Public read
decisions.statement: Two unauthenticated endpoints return published server policies only, with no author, working copy, change note or organisation id; an unpublished, unknown or organisation policy is the same 404.
decisions.rationale: `Cache-Control: no-store`. Throttled per client address in a bucket of its own using the existing `PUBLIC_ANNOUNCEMENT_RATE_LIMIT_*` settings (no new setting; the configuration reference says so).
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server policies: Where it is linked
decisions.statement: The plan named the login-page footer, the user menu and the in-application footer.
decisions.rationale: The application has no user menu and no footer, so the link ("Policies", shown only while a policy is published) sits below the sign-in form on both login pages and in the footer block at the foot of the navigation rail, where the build identity already is. A header icon was not added. With no policy published the page itself is not shown either : `/policies` redirects to the front page (the sign-in page, or the project list when signed in), so no empty page exists; the administration group stays, since it is where policies are written.
decisions.section: Server policies: privacy policy, data policy and others (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation policies: No built-in slots
decisions.statement: An organisation adds policies by title; a key is refused.
decisions.rationale: Starter titles (Access policy, Confidentiality agreement, Acceptable use policy, Code of conduct) only fill the title field of the add dialog.
decisions.section: Organisation policies (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation policies: Links setting
decisions.statement: `allow_policy_links`, off by default, kept as its own column and its own endpoint (`/policies/settings`, applied at once from a switch in the panel) rather than another field on the organisation settings endpoint, so the toggle sits beside the policies it governs.
decisions.rationale: The page is members-only, so the phishing concern that bars web addresses from organisation messages does not apply; a setting is the flexible reading. The setting is checked on save and again at publication, so turning it off blocks publishing a working copy that still has a link, and never changes a version already published.
decisions.section: Organisation policies (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation policies: Audience labels
decisions.statement: The editor keeps the audience as display values, and a person or group picked there is named by `POST /policies/audience-labels` (organisation administrators only, validated against the organisation exactly as a save is), because the administration page's user list is paged and filtered and cannot name every pick.
decisions.section: Organisation policies (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Live requirement, no per-version snapshot
decisions.statement: `policy_documents.requires_acknowledgement` is a setting of the policy, not copied into each version.
decisions.rationale: The plan's per-version "required from" field would have meant that switching a requirement off needs a new publication, which is the opposite of the escape hatch the same plan asks for ("a server administrator can switch a requirement off"). With a live flag, switching it off takes effect at once; accepting is always against the current published version, so a new version asks again.
decisions.section: Policy acceptance (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Policy acceptance: Who is asked
decisions.statement: A server policy: every active, non-archived user.
decisions.rationale: An organisation policy: the people who may read it (`org_policies.can_view`: the audience with effective group membership, and always the organisation's administrators). Acceptance is personal, so a group is never asked as a unit; a requirement reaches a group through its members (users and groups on parity as the audience does). An organisation administrator cannot require acceptance of a server policy (the server routes are server-administrator only; tested).
decisions.section: Policy acceptance (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Policy acceptance: The block
decisions.statement: `deps._require_policies_accepted` runs where every bearer-token dependency resolves its user (session token, access token and module frame), and `services/policy_acknowledgements.enforce_accepted` refuses a request that changes data (403, `detail.code = policy_acknowledgement_required`, with the ids to accept) while a required, published policy that applies to the person is unaccepted at its…
decisions.rationale: current version. Open requests: any GET, HEAD or OPTIONS; `/api/v1/auth/` (sign-in, sign-out, account); `/api/v1/policies/` (read and accept); `/api/v1/system/policies` and `/api/v1/orgs/{id}/policies` (so an administrator can switch the requirement off or unpublish the policy while blocked); `/api/v1/search`, `/api/v1/notifications` and `…/files/search` (reads sent as POST, or marking a notification read). This is a rule over the request, not a per-route annotation, so a new route is covered without a change; the price is that a *new read sent as POST* is blocked until added to the open list (`test_which_requests_stay_open` pins the list). It applies to access tokens and the MCP server too, because the obligation is the person's; an agent acting for a blocked person gets the same 403 and message. A module-frame token is covered.
decisions.section: Policy acceptance (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Policy acceptance: Sign-in prompt
decisions.statement: After sign-in a dialog shows the first pending policy (full text, Accept in the header; the close button leaves), once per person per browser session (`sessionStorage`, keyed by user id so a second person on the same tab is also asked); a notice stays at the top of every page, with a link to the policy, until everything is accepted; the Policies page shows an accept panel above a pending policy.
decisions.rationale: The list reloads when the window regains focus. A failed read leaves the last list: a notice must never block the page it sits on, and the server enforces the rule either way.
decisions.section: Policy acceptance (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Policy acceptance: Status and export
decisions.statement: An **Acceptance** action on a required policy lists everyone it applies to with their latest acceptance (those yet to accept the current version first, capped at 2,000 rows with the cap stated), an **Export** (CSV; formula-guarded cells through `csv_safe`; audited as one event with a row count) and **Send reminder**.
decisions.rationale: The plan said "through the shared list actions"; those exist for registered artefact types with a `RecordTableProvider`, and a policy is not one, so the export is on this dialog, with the same cell-safety rule and no cell values in the audit event.
decisions.section: Policy acceptance (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: File uploads: deployment-wide switch: One gate
decisions.statement: `services.files.upload_file` calls `assert_uploads_allowed(db, organization_id)` first (403, `detail.code = uploads_disabled`).
decisions.rationale: The `organization_id` argument is for the per-organisation rules a later phase adds to the same function. The check reads the one `server_settings` column (a single-row select, no commit, unlike `get_server_settings`).
decisions.section: File uploads: deployment-wide switch (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Deletion needs no prior suspension
decisions.statement: Delete keeps the typed-name confirmation, the audit event and the cascade unchanged.
decisions.section: Server roles: Platform subscription manager and Subscription removal authority (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Server roles: Counts only
decisions.statement: The roles read the same thin `OrganizationOut` directory a server administrator already reads (`list_organizations`/`get_organization` now admit a holder of either role through `_sees_every_organization`); no record titles, files or member emails.
decisions.rationale: No per-organisation usage read exists yet; phase 44 adds one and must keep this rule.
decisions.section: Server roles: Platform subscription manager and Subscription removal authority (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation file uploads: Server default limit
decisions.statement: Settable by a server administrator only, in Server management → File uploads (`PUT /system/default-storage-quota`): it is a deployment-wide setting, which the subscription roles' allow-list keeps with the server administrator; a manager sets a limit per organisation instead.
decisions.rationale: Resolution: own limit, else the server default, else none (`services.storage_usage.effective_quota`).
decisions.section: Organisation file uploads: disable and storage limit (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation file uploads: One gate, extended
decisions.statement: `assert_uploads_allowed(db, organization_id, incoming_bytes)` checks the deployment switch (`uploads_disabled`), the organisation switch (`organization_uploads_disabled`), then `used + incoming > limit` (`storage_quota_exceeded`, with `quota_bytes`, `used_bytes`, `remaining_bytes`), so the interface and a person can tell which rule applied.
decisions.rationale: The refusal message names who to ask. The static test that every storage writer is gated is unchanged and now also pins the `len(data)` argument.
decisions.section: Organisation file uploads: disable and storage limit (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation file uploads: Lowering below usage
decisions.statement: Only blocks new files: existing files stay readable and deletable, deleting frees space.
decisions.section: Organisation file uploads: disable and storage limit (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation file uploads: Who may change it
decisions.statement: `PUT /orgs/{id}/storage` needs the Platform subscription manager role or server administrator (a personal access token never does); an organisation administrator reads (`GET`, counts only, `can_edit` false) but cannot write, so they cannot lift their own limit.
decisions.rationale: A Subscription removal authority alone may not read or write. Audited as `storage_rules_updated` with the role used and the old and new values; the 90% notice as `storage_limit_near` with counts only.
decisions.section: Organisation file uploads: disable and storage limit (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation file uploads: Notice at 90%
decisions.statement: After allowing an upload, the gate notifies the organisation's administrators once (`storage_limit_near`, in-app and email per their preferences) and sets `storage_warned`; the flag clears when usage before the new file is below 90% or when the limit changes, so a later crossing is announced again.
decisions.rationale: The usage table shows a warning at or above 90%. No separate email was added.
decisions.section: Organisation file uploads: disable and storage limit (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Request inbox: organisation level only: Generic field
decisions.statement: `ModuleSubComponentDefinition.organization_only` (default false); Product Feedback sets it on `organization_requests`.
decisions.rationale: No core file names the key and no core enum or column gains a value (Modular Feature System Boundary). Project API: the sub-component list omits such entries and the `PUT` answers 404, so a stale client cannot store an override that does nothing. Resolver: `is_module_subcomponent_enabled` returns the organisation's state for it and never reads a project row, so a row stored by an earlier version can neither enable nor disable it; `snapshot_project_module_state`, `freeze_projects_subcomponent_default` and the template copy (`copy_module_enablement`) write no row for it. No migration: nothing ever read such rows.
decisions.section: Request inbox: organisation level only (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Audit of the other sub-components
decisions.statement: Every other sub-component is also gated by a project route (`require_project_subcomponent_enabled`) or is read at project level (references card, research extras), so none has the dead-toggle shape.
decisions.rationale: Only the inbox is flagged, as asked.
decisions.section: Request inbox: organisation level only (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Three nullable columns on server_settings
decisions.statement: (migration 0160): `footer_prefix` (50), `company_id_label` (50) and `company_id` (100); partial update, public read (the signed-out footer needs them), audit event naming the fields only.
decisions.rationale: The identifier is a label and a value : any country's identifier fits and the label can change; a label without a value is ignored, a value without a label shows alone.
decisions.section: Footer prefix and company identifier (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Shown in the page footer and the email footer
decisions.statement: Page footer: `Prefix Company name | address | label identifier | Policies | Version`.
decisions.rationale: Email: the prefix replaces the copyright mark ("Hosted by Host Pty Ltd", not "(c) 2026 Host Pty Ltd", since the host is not the copyright holder), the identifier is a line after the address, and the plain-text templates carry both.
decisions.section: Footer prefix and company identifier (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Operator details stay with the operator
decisions.statement: The prefix needs a platform company name, and neither the prefix nor the identifier is added to an email for an organisation that has set its own company name (`resolve_email_branding`), because they describe the operator and not that organisation.
decisions.rationale: The page footer is server-level and always shows them.
decisions.section: Footer prefix and company identifier (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Who may upload and delete : organisation administrators and a named organisation group
decisions.statement: Implemented as one new administrative permission atom, `manage_org_resources` (`services/permissions.py`, `services/rbac.py`), not a new setting: organisation administrators hold it through the role table, and a custom role can give it to a user or an organisation group (nested groups count), so users and groups are on parity with no new group column.
decisions.rationale: `POST` and `DELETE /orgs/{id}/resources` use `require_permission(MANAGE_ORG_RESOURCES)` (the server-administrator bypass is unchanged from the previous `ORG_ADMIN` gate, which also admitted a server administrator); `GET` stays open to every member.
decisions.section: Organisation shared resources on the Files page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: The server decides what the page shows
decisions.statement: `GET /orgs/{id}/resources/access` returns `can_manage`; the page never infers it from a role name.
decisions.rationale: The list response (`OrgResourceOut`) now carries `uploaded_by_display_name` and `link_count` from two bulk reads (statement count pinned flat in the test).
decisions.section: Organisation shared resources on the Files page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Delete states its links
decisions.statement: The confirmation names the number of requirements that link the file, which are removed with it (the existing behaviour), and asks for the file name to be typed (Tier 2) when there are any, a plain Tier 1 confirm when there are none.
decisions.rationale: The count comes with the list, so there is no extra preflight request.
decisions.section: Organisation shared resources on the Files page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation administrator: Identity-only rows
decisions.statement: `ProjectListItemOut` could not be trimmed (its parent `ProjectOut` requires `summary`, `status_id` and settings), so the extra rows are a separate narrower schema, `UnjoinedProjectListItemOut` (id, organisation, name, code, archived, template, parent, `is_member: false`), and the response is a union discriminated by `is_member`.
decisions.rationale: No summary, counts, stage, status, dates or owners. Search on these rows matches the name only (the summary is content).
decisions.section: Organisation administrator: all projects in the project list (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation administrator: Challenge to the plan
decisions.statement: The plan added a `templates_only` read on `GET /orgs/{id}/projects` for the Default template picker.
decisions.rationale: That endpoint has a second reader, the role-grant project picker, and is already name-only, so it is unchanged; Organisation administration still reads it for both. Only the list, its Manage users buttons and their strings are removed. The Projects section was a collapsible section, not a routed address, so no redirect is needed; the group's own address is unchanged.
decisions.section: Organisation administrator: all projects in the project list (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation details page: Partial branding update first
decisions.statement: `PUT /orgs/{id}/branding` overwrote the accent colour, header title and the three footer fields with whatever the request held, so two pages saving their own fields through it would have erased each other's values.
decisions.rationale: It is now partial by `model_fields_set` (a field not sent is left alone, null clears it); a boolean and the colour scheme still treat null as "leave as it is" (`[]` clears the scheme). The audit event names the fields changed, never their values (the pattern of the platform endpoint). Tested in `test_org_branding_partial.py` for every clearable field.
decisions.section: Organisation details page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Organisation details page: Name moves, slug stays
decisions.statement: The organisation name is a field on the new page (saved through the existing rename endpoint in the same Save as the company details, each call only when its field changed); the Rename entry and dialog on the Overview menu are removed.
decisions.rationale: The slug stays under OAuth / SSO because it is the SSO login address and saves with the SSO configuration.
decisions.section: Organisation details page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Logo moves, report logo option stays
decisions.statement: The logo is edited only on the new page.
decisions.rationale: **Include logo** on reports stays on Branding & defaults: it is a report setting, not identity.
decisions.section: Organisation details page (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Project History page redesign: Table, not a timeline
decisions.statement: `DirectoryTable` with Time (the only sortable column; oldest first is a server `order` parameter), Type, Event, Record and Person.
decisions.rationale: A day is written once per local day. Roughly twice the events fit on a screen. `DirectoryColumn.width` is a new optional prop for a column of long text.
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Record names for every type
decisions.statement: The server adds `record_label` for an entry about a record of any registered type the viewer may see, through `ArtefactResolver` (the Links panel's visibility rule, one lookup per type, for the returned page only); the browser links it through `getArtefactPath`.
decisions.rationale: A record the viewer cannot open keeps its type and gets no label, so the page reveals what happened and not the title of a hidden record. Requirements and change requests keep carrying code and title in `detail`.
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Project History page redesign: Kinds of event
decisions.statement: `services/activity_kinds.py`: created, edited, status, links, tags, access, comments, deleted, other.
decisions.rationale: An unclassified action is Other, so no event is hidden. A module classifies its own actions through the new generic `ModuleDefinition.activity_action_kinds` (a test fails for an unknown kind); no per-module entry in core. Not built: a "changed to Approved" status-value filter. The events carry the new status for requirements and change requests only (`detail.status`), not for module records, so a filter would be partial; recorded as a gap.
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Project History page redesign: Person or group
decisions.statement: `actor=user:<id>|org_group:<id>|project_group:<id>`, repeatable; a group resolves to its effective members (`principal_member_ids`); a group of another organisation or project is refused (422), a user is not checked against the organisation so a person who has left can still be filtered by.
decisions.rationale: An empty group matches nothing (not "no filter"). `GET .../changes/actors` names the chips from a restored link; it names a user only when they belong to the organisation or have acted in the project, so it cannot be used to read an arbitrary account's name.
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Paging is bounded by the page
decisions.statement: Every filter is part of each source query (audit events, requirement versions, change request versions, comments); each source returns its newest `offset + limit` rows and its own count; the merge sorts `(timestamp, source, id)` so equal timestamps page deterministically.
decisions.rationale: Statements per page no longer grow with the history (`test_a_page_costs_the_same_statements_however_large_the_project_history_is`). The record activity panels keep using the whole filtered timeline through `get_project_changes`. **Behaviour change:** `GET .../changes` without `limit` used to return every entry; it now returns the newest 30 (maximum 1000). The only callers were this page and the overview's activity widget, which now passes its `limit` (it used to download the whole timeline and discard all but a few); there is no MCP or API consumer in the repository.
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: Export is an exception to "Every record list exports and imports"
decisions.statement: The history is not a registered record type (an event is never authored), so it has no `RecordTableProvider`, no Import and no `code` column; its Export is `GET .../changes/export` (CSV, PDF, Word, ODT, ODS, Excel, HTML) with the page's filters, formula-guarded cells, the Person column governed by the one personal-data decision (`tag_decisions`), UTC times, record codes through `display_code`…
decisions.rationale: one `records_exported` audit event with counts and filter names only, and a row cap (50,000; 5,000 for a PDF or Word document, 413 above it).
decisions.section: Project History page redesign (2026-11-10)

decisions.title: S1, S2, J2, NEW-4 (sign-in)
decisions.statement: `get_client_ip` now returns the connecting address as uvicorn determined it (the forwarded address only from `FORWARDED_ALLOW_IPS`), cut to 64 characters.
decisions.rationale: Sign-in has a progressive delay (`services.login_throttle`): failed password attempts in a 15-minute window count per address typed (since its last success) and per source address; past 5 (30 for an address) each further failure doubles a 5-second wait up to 5 minutes, refused attempts are stored (`login_events.kind = throttled`) and do not count, and an advisory lock per account refuses parallel guesses. A delay, not a lock, so a third party can slow a person by at most the maximum (). Sign-up has a limit per address. Tests: `test_login_throttle.py`.
decisions.section: Security hardening of the whole product (fixes and guards)

decisions.title: P1, P3, J1 (credentials a token must not use)
